records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.2
records.statement: Let $S$ be a finite simple group, and let $G$ be a finite group for which there exists a bijection $f:G\to S$ such that $|x|$ divides $|f(x)|$ for all $x\in G$. Must $G$ necessarily be simple?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.3
records.statement: Let $G=A_n$ or $S_n$ and let $H,K$ be soluble subgroups of $G$. For all sufficiently large $n$, can we always find an element $x\in G$ such that $H\cap K^x=1$? Does this hold for all $n\geqslant 21$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.4
records.statement: Let $G$ be a finite group with trivial solvable radical and let $H_1,\ldots,H_5$ be solvable subgroups of $G$. Then do there always exist elements $x_i\in G$ such that $\bigcap_i H_i^{x_i}=1$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.5
records.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime. Let $G$ be a transitive subgroup of the group of finitary permutations $\operatorname{FSym}(\Omega)$ of a set $\Omega$, let $N$ be a normal subgroup of $G$, and let $S$ be a transitive Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G$.

(a) Is it true that $S\cap N$ is a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $N$?

(b) Is it true that $SN/N$ is a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G/N$?

(c) Are any two transitive Sylow $p$-subgroups of $G$ locally conjugate in $G$?

Two subgroups $X,Y$ of a group $G$ are said to be locally conjugate if there is a locally inner automorphism $\phi$ of $G$ such that $X^\phi=Y$. An automorphism $\phi$ of $G$ is said to be locally inner if for every finite subset $A\subseteq G$ there is an element $g=g(A)\in G$ such that $a^\phi=g^{-1}ag$ for all $a\in A$.

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.6
records.statement: Let p be a prime. A totally imprimitive p-group H of finitary permutations is said to have the cyclic-block property if in the cycle decomposition of every element the support of every cycle is a block for H. Let G be a transitive subgroup of the group of finitary permutations $\operatorname{FSym}(\Omega)$ of a set $\Omega$. Does every transitive Sylow p-subgroup of G contain a transitive subgroup which has the cyclic-block property?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.7
records.statement: (Well-known problem). A finite group G is called an IYB-group if it is isomorphic to the permutation group of a finite involutive non-degenerate set-theoretic solution of the Yang--Baxter equation, or equivalently, G is isomorphic to the multiplicative group of a finite left brace. Assume that the Sylow subgroups of a finite soluble group G are IYB-groups. Is G an IYB-group?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.8
records.statement: As in 17.57, let $r(m)=\{r+km\mid k\in\mathbb Z\}$ for integers $0\leqslant r<m$; for $r_1(m_1)\cap r_2(m_2)=\emptyset$ let the class transposition $\tau_{r_1(m_1),r_2(m_2)}$ be the involution which interchanges $r_1+tm_1$ and $r_2+tm_2$ for each integer t and fixes everything else, and let $\operatorname{CT}(\mathbb Z)$ be the group generated by all class transpositions. Let $\operatorname{CT}_k$ be the subgroup of $\operatorname{CT}(\mathbb Z)$ generated by the class transpositions $\tau_{r_1(k),r_2(k)}$ for $0\leqslant r_1\ne r_2<k$. Since $\tau_{r_1(k),r_2(k)}$ permutes the residue classes modulo k, the group $\operatorname{CT}_k$ is isomorphic to the symmetric group $S_k$. Let $\operatorname{CT}(k)=\langle\operatorname{CT}_2,\operatorname{CT}_3,\ldots,\operatorname{CT}_k\rangle$. Is it true that for $k>3$ the group $\operatorname{CT}(k)$ is isomorphic to the symmetric group $S_N$, where N is the least common multiple of the numbers $2,3,\ldots,k$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.9
records.statement: Let $F$ be a non-abelian free pro-$p$ group of finite rank. Can one find a finite collection $U_1,\ldots,U_n$ of open subgroups of $F$, including $F$ itself, such that the only subgroup of $F$ which is contained in $U_i$ and is characteristic in $U_i$ for every $i$ is the trivial subgroup?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.10
records.statement: We call a group presentation finite if it represents a finite group. We say that a presentation is just finite if it is finite and is no longer finite on removal of any relation from it. Is it true that every finite group has a just finite presentation?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.11
records.statement: Can some or all groups of the following sorts be written as homomorphic images of nonprincipal ultraproducts of countable families of groups?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.12
records.statement: Suppose that $U$ is a nonprincipal ultrafilter on $\omega$, and $B$ is a group such that every element $b\in B$ belongs to a subgroup of $B$ that is a homomorphic image of $\mathbb Z^\omega/U$. Must $B$ then be a homomorphic image of an ultraproduct group $(\prod_{i\in\omega}G_i)/U$ for some groups $G_i$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.13
records.statement: Does $\mathbb Z^\omega$ have a subgroup whose dual is free abelian of still larger rank (the largest possible being $2^{2^{\aleph_0}}$)?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.14
records.statement: Suppose $\alpha$ is an endomorphism of a group G such that for every group H and every homomorphism $f:G\to H$, there exists an endomorphism $\beta_f$ of $H$ such that $\beta_f f=f\alpha$. Must $\alpha$ then be either an inner automorphism of G or the trivial endomorphism?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.15
records.statement: Suppose B is a subgroup of the symmetric group $S_\Omega$ on an infinite set $\Omega$. Will the amalgamated free product $S_\Omega *_B S_\Omega$ of two copies of $S_\Omega$ with amalgamation of B be embeddable in $S_\Omega$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.16
records.statement: Let the width of a group (respectively, a monoid) H with respect to a generating set X mean the supremum over h $\in$ H of the least length of a group word (respectively, a monoid word) in elements of X expressing h. A group (or monoid) is said to have finite width if its width with respect to every generating set is finite. (A common finite bound for these widths is not required.) Do there exist groups G having finite width as groups, but not as monoids?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.17
records.statement: If $X$ is a class of groups, let $H(X)$ denote the class of homomorphic images of groups in $X$, let $S(X)$ denote the class of groups isomorphic to subgroups of groups in $X$, let $P(X)$ denote the class of groups isomorphic to (unrestricted) direct products of families of groups in $X$, and let $P_f(X)$ denote the class of groups isomorphic to direct products of finite families of groups in $X$. By Birkhoff's theorem, $H(S(P(X)))$ is the variety of groups generated by $X$. If $M$ is a class of metabelian groups, must $H(S(P_f(M)))\subseteq S(H(P(S(M))))$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.18
records.statement: Suppose that G is a finite group, and $A_1,A_2,A_3$ are subsets of G such that the multiplication map $A_1\times A_2\times A_3\to G$ is bijective. Must the subgroup $\langle A_2\rangle$ generated by $A_2$ have order divisible by the cardinality $|A_2|$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.19
records.statement: Suppose that S and M are groups of finite Morley rank, S is an infinite group, and M is a non-trivial connected group definably and faithfully acting on S. This action is said to be irreducible if M does not leave invariant any definable non-trivial proper subgroup of S. Prove that if S is a simple group such that every proper definable subgroup of S is nilpotent, and the action of M on S is irreducible, then this action is equivalent to the action of S on itself by conjugation.

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.20
records.statement: Prove that a simple group of finite Morley rank without involutions cannot act definably, faithfully, and irreducibly on a connected group other than on itself acting by conjugation.

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.21
records.statement: Prove that a simple (that is, without proper non-trivial connected normal subgroups) algebraic group M over an algebraically closed field cannot act definably, faithfully, and irreducibly on a simple group of finite Morley rank other than M/Z(M).

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.22
records.statement: Is the (standard, restricted) wreath product $G\wr H$ of two finitely generated Hopfian groups Hopfian?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.23
records.statement:
A graph is called a cograph if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to a path with 4 vertices. A graph is said to be chordal if it has no induced cycles with n vertices for every $n\geqslant 4$. For a finite group G, the enhanced power graph E(G) is the graph with vertex set G and edges \{x, y\} for all $x\ne y\in G$ such that $\langle x,y\rangle$ is cyclic.

(a) For a given integer $n\geqslant 4$, determine the set of all finite nonabelian simple groups G such that E(G) has no induced cycles with n vertices.

(b) Determine the set of all finite nonabelian simple groups G such that E(G) is chordal.

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.24
records.statement: For a finite group G, the power graph P(G) is the graph with vertex set G and edges \{x, y\} for all $x\ne y\in G$ such that either $x\in\langle y\rangle$ or $y\in\langle x\rangle$. Is it true that, for every finite group G, if P(G) is a cograph, then P(G) is chordal?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.25
records.statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple group and let $p_1,p_2$ be any (not necessarily distinct) prime divisors of $|G|$. Then can we always find Sylow $p_i$-subgroups $H_i$ such that $G=\langle H_1,H_2\rangle$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.26
records.statement: Let $G$ be a non-trivial finite group and let $p_1,\ldots,p_k$ be the distinct prime divisors of $|G|$. For each $i$, let $H_i$ be a Sylow $p_i$-subgroup of $G$. Is it true that there exists an element $x\in G$ such that for all $i$ the subgroup $H_i\cap H_i^x$ is inclusion-minimal in $\{H_i\cap H_i^g:g\in G\}$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.27
records.statement: A permutation on a set $\Omega$ is called a derangement if it has no fixed points in $\Omega$. Let G be a finite simple transitive permutation group. Is it true that every element in G is the product of two derangements?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.28
records.statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple transitive permutation group, and let $\delta(G)$ be the proportion of derangements in $G$. Is it true that $\delta(G)\geqslant 89/325$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.29
records.statement: Let $G\leqslant\operatorname{Sym}(\Omega)$ be a finite primitive permutation group with a regular suborbit (that is, $G$ has a trivial 2-point stabiliser). Then is it true that for all $\alpha,\beta\in\Omega$, there exists $\gamma\in\Omega$ such that the 2-point stabilisers $G_{\alpha,\gamma}$ and $G_{\beta,\gamma}$ are both trivial?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.30
records.statement: (Well-known question). A discrete group G is said to have the Haagerup property (also known as Gromov's a-T-menability property) if there exists a metrically proper isometric action of G on a (possibly infinite-dimensional) Hilbert space. Are all 1-relator groups Haagerup groups?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.31
records.statement: Conjecture: If N is a finite soluble group, then any regular subgroup in the holomorph Hol(N) of N is also soluble.

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.32
records.statement: Is the following problem decidable, and if so, what is its complexity? Given a finite group G, is there a finite group H such that the derived subgroup of H is isomorphic to G?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.33
records.statement: Does an analogue of Dunwoody's theorem hold for totally disconnected locally compact groups, that is, must a tdlc group of rational discrete cohomological dimension at most 1 be topologically isomorphic to the fundamental group of a graph of profinite groups?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.34
records.statement: (Well-known problem). A group $G$ is a unique product group if, for any nonempty finite subsets $A,B$ of $G$, there exists an element of $G$ which can be written uniquely as $ab$ with $a\in A$ and $b\in B$. A group $G$ is locally invariant orderable if $G$ admits a partial order $<$ such that for all $g,h\in G$ with $h\ne 1$, we have either $gh>g$ or $gh^{-1}>g$. Does there exist a unique product group which is not locally invariant orderable?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.35
records.statement: Let $G$ be a finite group, $w$ a multilinear commutator group-word, and $p$ a prime. Suppose that $p$ divides the order $|xy|$ whenever $x$ is a $w$-value of $p'$-order in $G$ and $y$ is a $w$-value in $G$ of order divisible by $p$. Is it true that then the verbal subgroup $w(G)$ must be $p$-nilpotent?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.36
records.statement: Let a hierarchy of tdlc groups $\mathbf H\mathcal K$ be defined analogously to Kropholler's hierarchy in 15.45, with $\mathcal K$ being the class of profinite groups and with the cell stabilisers of the admissible action required to be open. Is it true that $\mathbf H\mathcal K$ is closed under profinite extensions, that is, $(\mathbf H_\alpha\mathcal K)\mathcal K\subseteq \mathbf H_\alpha\mathcal K$ for every $\alpha$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.37
records.statement: By definition, a constructible totally disconnected, locally compact (tdlc) group is the result of a sequence of profinite extensions and ascending HNN-extensions starting from the trivial group. Are soluble tdlc groups of type $FP_\infty$ constructible?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.38
records.statement: The spread of a group $G$ is the greatest nonnegative integer $k$ such that for all nontrivial elements $x_1,\ldots,x_k\in G$ there exists $y\in G$ such that $\langle x_1,y\rangle=\cdots=\langle x_k,y\rangle=G$, or is $\infty$ in case there is no such maximum. Does there exist a group with spread equal to 1?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.39
records.statement: Are there any locally finite, characteristically simple groups with finitely many orbits under automorphisms that are not residually finite?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.40
records.statement: Let G be a subgroup of GL(n, Q) with finitely many orbits under automorphisms. Is G a virtually soluble group?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.41
records.statement: A group is said to be self-similar if it admits a faithful state-closed representation by automorphisms of a regular one-rooted m-tree for some m. Can a torsion-free finitely presented metabelian group which is self-similar contain a subgroup isomorphic to the restricted wreath product H = $\mathbb Z\wr\mathbb Z$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.42
records.statement: Let $\mathcal T_{d,c}$ denote the class of $d$-generated, torsion-free nilpotent groups having class $c$. Are there $\mathcal T_{3,3}$-groups that are not self-similar?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.43
records.statement: Conjecture: Suppose that for a fixed positive integer $k$ at least half of the elements of a finite group $G$ have order $k$. Then $G$ is solvable.

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.44
records.statement: Let $W_n=A_5\wr\cdots\wr A_5$ be the $n$-times iterated permutational wreath product of $A_5$ in its natural action (so $W_n$ acts on $5^n$ points), and let $W=\varprojlim W_n$ be the inverse limit (infinite iterated wreath product of $A_5$). Does $W$ contain a finitely generated dense subgroup of subexponential growth?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.45
records.statement: (Well-known problem). Does there exist a finitely presented (infinite) simple group requiring more than two generators?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.46
records.statement: (Well-known problem). Does there exist a finitely presented (infinite) simple group of finite cohomological dimension greater than 2?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.47
records.statement: (Well-known problem). Does there exist a finitely presented group $G$ such that $G\cong G\times H$ for some non-trivial group $H$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.48
records.statement: A quasimorphism on a group $G$ is a function $f:G\to\mathbb R$ such that the quantity $\sup_{g,h}|f(g)+f(h)-f(gh)|$ is finite. A quasimorphism is homogeneous if it restricts to a homomorphism on every cyclic subgroup of $G$. Let $G$ be a group admitting an unbounded homogeneous quasimorphism $G\to\mathbb R$ that is not a homomorphism. Must $G$ contain a non-abelian free subgroup?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.49
records.statement: An isometric action of a group G on a metric space S is called acylindrical if for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exist R, N > 0 such that for every two points x, y with $d(x,y)\geqslant R$, there are at most N elements $g\in G$ satisfying $d(x,gx)\leqslant\varepsilon$ and $d(y,gy)\leqslant\varepsilon$. A group is said to be acylindrically hyperbolic if it is not virtually cyclic and admits an acylindrical action on a hyperbolic space with unbounded orbits. Is the automorphism group of a finitely generated acylindrically hyperbolic group also acylindrically hyperbolic?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.50
records.statement:
Does every finite 3-group $T$ have a nontrivial characteristic subgroup $C$ such that if $T$ is a Sylow 3-subgroup of a finite group $G$, then $T\cap G'=T\cap H'$, where $H=N_G(C)$?

The group $S_4$ shows that no such characteristic subgroups can be found in some Sylow 2-subgroups.

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.51
records.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, and $P$ a finite $p$-group.

(a) Suppose that $P$ has an abelian subgroup of order $p^n$. For which $n$ does $P$ necessarily have a normal abelian subgroup of order $p^n$?

(b) Suppose that $P$ has an elementary abelian subgroup of order $p^n$. For which $n$ does $P$ necessarily have a normal elementary abelian subgroup of order $p^n$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.52
records.statement: Let $L$ be a finite non-abelian simple group, and let $D$ be a conjugacy class of involutions in $L$. Consider the complete graph $\Gamma$ with vertex set $D$. Define an equivalence relation $\sim$ (graph coloring) on the set of edges as follows: $(a,b)\sim(c,d)$ if and only if $|ab|=|cd|$. An automorphism of the coloured graph $\Gamma$ is a permutation $\tau\in S_D$ such that $(a,b)\sim(a^\tau,b^\tau)$ for every edge $(a,b)$. Is it true that the automorphism group of $\Gamma$ is a subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}(L)$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.53
records.statement: In the notation of 21.52, let $\operatorname{Aut}_t(\Gamma)$ be the set of permutations $\tau\in S_D$ such that $(a,b)\sim(a^\tau,b^\tau)$ whenever $|ab|=t$ for $a,b\in D$. Clearly, $\operatorname{Aut}(\Gamma)=\bigcap_t\operatorname{Aut}_t(\Gamma)$. Is it true that for every finite simple group $G$ we have $\operatorname{Aut}(\Gamma)=\operatorname{Aut}_2(\Gamma)\cap\operatorname{Aut}_p(\Gamma)$, where $\{2,p\}$ are the two minimal prime divisors of $|G|$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.54
records.statement: Let $G$ be a finite soluble group with triality, which means that $G$ admits a group of automorphisms $S$ isomorphic to the symmetric group of degree 3 given by the presentation $S=\langle\sigma,\rho\mid \sigma^2=\rho^3=1;\ \sigma\rho\sigma=\rho^2\rangle$ such that $m\cdot m^\rho\cdot m^{\rho^2}=1$ for all $m$ in the set of commutators $M(G):=\{[g,\sigma]\mid g\in G\}$. Suppose in addition that $G=[G,S]$, the group $G$ is generated by $d$ elements of $M(G)$ and their images under $S$, and $x^n=1$ for all $x\in M(G)$. Is it true that the Fitting height of $G$ is bounded in terms of $d$ and $n$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.55
records.statement: Let $q$ be a power of a prime $p$, and let $m_n(q)$ be the maximum $p$-length of $p$-solvable subgroups of $\operatorname{GL}(n,q)$. Is it true that $\lim_{n\to\infty}m_n(q)/\log_2 n=1$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.56
records.statement:
Let $\ell(X)$ denote the composition length of a finite group $X$. Let $A$ be a finite nilpotent group acting by automorphisms on a finite soluble group $G$. Let $c(G,A)$ be the number of trivial $A$-modules in a given $A$-composition series of $G$. (Note that $c(G,A)=\ell(C_G(A))$ if $(|A|,|G|)=1$.)

Conjecture: there are absolute constants $C_1$ and $C_2$ such that the Fitting height of $G$ is at most $C_1\ell(A)+C_2c(G,A)$.

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.57
records.statement: Let X be a non-empty class of finite groups of odd order closed under taking subgroups, homomorphic images, and extensions. Let H be an X-maximal subgroup of a finite group G, and N a normal subgroup of G. Must H $\cap$ N be an X-maximal subgroup of N?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.58
records.statement: We say that a product $XY=\{xy\mid x\in X,\ y\in Y\}$ of two subsets $X,Y$ of a group $G$ is direct if for every $z\in XY$ there are unique $x\in X$, $y\in Y$ such that $z=xy$. Is there an infinite group $G$ such that every subset $A\subseteq G$ satisfies the following property: all the maximal subsets $B$ for which the product $AB$ is direct have the same cardinality?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.59
records.statement:
For a finite group $G$, let $\chi_1(G)$ denote the totality of the degrees of all irreducible complex characters of $G$ with allowance for their multiplicities. Suppose that $H$ is a finite group with $\chi_1(H)=\chi_1(G)$.

a) If $G$ is an almost simple group, must $H$ be isomorphic to $G$?

b) If $G$ is a quasisimple group, must $H$ be isomorphic to $G$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.60
records.statement: Let $G$ be a finite group, $\mathbb Z_{(p)}$ the localization at $p$, and $\mathbb F_p$ the field of $p$ elements. Let $\mathcal X$ be the class of $\mathbb F_pG$-modules obtained by reduction of simple $\mathbb QG$-modules. Is it true that $\mathbb Z_{(p)}G$ is semiperfect if and only if each projective indecomposable $\mathbb F_pG$-module can be written as an $\mathbb N$-linear combination of modules in $\mathcal X$ inside the Grothendieck group of $\mathbb F_pG$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.61
records.statement: For a fixed (finitely generated free)-by-cyclic group $G=F_n\rtimes\mathbb Z$, is there an algorithm that, given a finite subset $S$ of $G$, finds a finite presentation for the subgroup $H=\langle S\rangle$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.62
records.statement: Is the uniform subgroup membership problem decidable for (finitely generated free)-by-cyclic groups? That is, for a fixed group $G=F_n\rtimes\mathbb Z$, is there an algorithm that, given elements $w,h_1,\ldots,h_k\in G$, decides whether or not $w$ belongs to the subgroup $H=\langle h_1,\ldots,h_k\rangle$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.63
records.statement: Let $F$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, and let $\Gamma$ be the principal congruence subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}(F[x_1,\ldots,x_n])$ consisting of all automorphisms that send each variable $x_i$ to $x_i$ modulo terms of higher degree. Then $\Gamma$ is a residually-$p$ group. Does $\Gamma$ satisfy a pro-$p$ identity?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.64
records.statement: Is it true that if a normal subgroup $A$ of a Sylow $p$-subgroup of a $p$-soluble finite group $G$ has exponent $p^e$, then the normal closure of $A$ in $G$ has $(p,e)$-bounded (or even $e$-bounded) $p$-length?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.65
records.statement:
Suppose that $\phi$ is an automorphism of a finite soluble group $G$. Must $G$ contain a subgroup of index bounded in terms of $|\phi|$ and $|C_G(\phi)|$ whose Fitting height is bounded

(a) in terms of $|\phi|$?

(b) or even in terms of the composition length of $\langle\phi\rangle$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.66
records.statement:
Suppose that A is a nilpotent group of automorphisms of a finite soluble group G. Is the Fitting height of G bounded in terms of |A| and |CG(A)|?

Isaacs), when A is cyclic (see 19.43), or when CG(A) = 1 (E. C. Dade).

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.67
records.statement: Suppose that $\phi$ is an automorphism of a finite soluble group $G$, and let $r$ be the (Pr\"ufer) rank of the fixed-point subgroup $C_G(\phi)$. Is the Fitting height of $G$ bounded in terms of $|\phi|$ and $r$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.68
records.statement:
A finite group $G$ is said to be semi-abelian if it has a sequence of subgroups $1=G_0\leqslant G_1\leqslant\cdots\leqslant G_n=G$ such that for every $i$ the subgroup $G_{i+1}$ is isomorphic to a quotient of a semidirect product $A_i\rtimes G_i$ for some abelian group $A_i$.

Conjecture: Semi-abelian finite groups are monomial.

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.69
records.statement: Is there an algorithm deciding if a given one-relator group is hyperbolic?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.70
records.statement: A group $G$ is called an orientable Poincar\'e duality group of dimension $n$ over a ring $R$ if it is of type $FP$ over $R$ and $H^i(G;RG)=0$ for $i\ne n$, while $H^n(G;RG)=R$ as an $RG$-module, where the action on $R$ is trivial. (Note that $G$ is not required to be finitely presented.) If $G$ is an orientable Poincar\'e duality group of dimension $n$ over all fields, is it an orientable Poincar\'e duality group over the integers?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.71
records.statement: For a ring $R$, we say that a group $G$ is of type $FL(R)$ if the trivial $RG$-module $R$ admits a finite resolution by finitely generated free modules. If $R$ is a field, we define the Euler characteristic of $G$ over $R$ to be the alternating sum of $R$-ranks of homology groups $H_i(G;R)$. Does there exist a group of type $FL(F_i)$ for two fields $F_1$ and $F_2$ such that the Euler characteristics of the group over the fields $F_1$ and $F_2$ differ?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.72
records.statement:
We say that a group is a Tarski monster if it is finitely generated, not cyclic, and all of its proper non-trivial subgroups are isomorphic to each other.

a) Do there exist amenable torsion-free Tarski monsters?

b) Do there exist amenable Tarski monsters of prime exponent?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.73
records.statement: Is the conjugacy problem in $\operatorname{CT}(\mathbb Z)$ algorithmically decidable?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.74
records.statement:
Is it algorithmically decidable whether a given element $g\in\operatorname{CT}(\mathbb Z)$

(a) permutes a nontrivial partition of $\mathbb Z$ into residue classes?

(b) has only finite cycles?

(c) has no finite cycles?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.75
records.statement: Given two distinct sets $P_1$ and $P_2$ of odd primes none of which is a subset of the other, is it true that $\langle \operatorname{CT}_{P_1}(\mathbb Z),\operatorname{CT}_{P_2}(\mathbb Z)\rangle \lneq \operatorname{CT}_{P_1\cup P_2}(\mathbb Z)$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.76
records.statement: Let $\sigma=(\sigma_{ij})$, $1\leqslant i\ne j\leqslant n$, be an irreducible elementary net (carpet) of order $n\geqslant 3$ over a field $K$ (see 19.48). The net $\sigma$ is said to be closed if the elementary net subgroup $E(\sigma)$ does not contain new elementary transvections. The net $\sigma$ is said to be completable if its diagonal can be supplemented with subgroups to a complete net. Do there exist irreducible closed elementary nets of order $n\geqslant 3$ over a field of odd characteristic that are not completable?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.77
records.statement: Let $d$ be an integer that is not divisible by $n$-th powers of primes, let $x^n-d$ be an irreducible polynomial over $\mathbb Q$, let $\theta=\sqrt[n]{d}$, and let $K=\mathbb Q(\theta)$ be the radical extension of degree $n$ of the field $\mathbb Q$. The multiplicative group $K^*$ of the field $K$ is canonically embedded into the group $\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathbb Q}(K)$ of all invertible $\mathbb Q$-linear mappings of the $\mathbb Q$-space $K$; let $T$ be the image of $K^*$ under this embedding. In the natural basis $1,\theta,\theta^2,\ldots,\theta^{n-1}$ of the $\mathbb Q$-space $K$ the group $\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathbb Q}(K)$ corresponds to $G=\operatorname{GL}(n,\mathbb Q)$, and the subgroup $T$ to a subgroup $T(d)$ (unsplit maximal torus). Every subgroup $H$ of $G$ containing $T(d)$ and some one-dimensional transformation is rich in elementary transvections and thus defines a net $\sigma=\sigma(H)$. Let $E(\sigma)$ denote the subgroup generated by all transvections in the net group $G(\sigma)$. Is it true that $H\leqslant N_G(E(\sigma))$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.78
records.statement: Let $p$ be a prime and let $G$ be a pro-$p$ group. Suppose that all of the (continuous Galois) cohomology groups $H^n(G,\mathbb F_p)$ of $G$ with coefficients in the field of $p$ elements are finite. Does it necessarily follow that the cohomology ring $H^*(G,\mathbb F_p)$ is finitely generated?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.79
records.statement: Let $G$ be a finitely generated group with a fixed finite generating set $S$ and the corresponding word metric $L_S(*)$. An element $g$ is said to be distorted in $G$ if $L_S(g^n)/n\to 0$ as $n\to\infty$; this notion is independent of the choice of the generating set $S$. For any, not necessarily finitely generated, group $H$, an element $g\in H$ is said to be distorted if there is a finitely generated subgroup $G$ of $H$ containing $g$ in which $g$ is distorted. Do there exist finitely generated left-orderable groups in which every nontrivial element is distorted?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.80
records.statement: Do there exist finitely generated left-orderable groups with only one nontrivial conjugacy class?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.81
records.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite simple group and let $N_n(\Gamma)$ denote the set of normal subgroups of the free group $F_n$ of rank $n$ whose quotient is isomorphic to $\Gamma$.

Conjecture: $\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$ acts transitively on $N_n(\Gamma)$ for $n\geqslant 3$.

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.82
records.statement: Conjecture: For $n\geqslant 3$, there are no finite simple characteristic quotients of the free group $F_n$.

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.83
records.statement: Conjecture: Metabelian groups are permutation-stable.

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.84
records.statement: For $\sigma\in S_n$ and $\tau\in S_m$, where $n\leqslant m$, let $d_n^{\mathrm{flex}}(\sigma,\tau)=(1/n)\cdot(|\{x\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\mid \sigma(x)\ne\tau(x)\}|+(m-n))$. An almost-homomorphism $\{f_n\}$ is said to be flexibly close to a homomorphism if there is a sequence of group homomorphisms $\rho_n:G\to S_{m_n}$ with $n\leqslant m_n$ such that $d_n^{\mathrm{flex}}(\rho_n(g),f_n(g))\to 0$ as $n\to\infty$ for all $g\in G$. The group $G$ is said to be flexibly permutation stable if every almost-homomorphism of $G$ is flexibly close to a homomorphism. Is $\operatorname{SL}_n(\mathbb Z)$ flexibly permutation-stable?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.85
records.statement: Is a flexibly permutation-stable group always permutation-stable?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.86
records.statement: A group $G$ is said to be sofic if for every finite set $F\subseteq G$ containing $1$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ there exist $n\in\mathbb N$ and a map $\phi:F\to S_n$ such that $\phi(1)=1$, $d(\phi(gh),\phi(g)\phi(h))<\varepsilon$ for all $g,h$ such that $gh\in F$, and $\phi(g)$ does not have fixed points for every $g\in F\setminus\{1\}$. Is every group sofic?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.87
records.statement: Assume that a finite group G has a family of d-generator subgroups whose indices have no common divisor. Is it true that G can be generated by d+1 elements?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.88
records.statement: Is there a finite non-abelian group $G$ of odd order, with $k(G)$ conjugacy classes, such that $k(G)/|G|=1/17$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.89
records.statement: For $n>39$, is it true that the number of conjugacy classes in the symmetric group $S_n$ of degree $n$ is never a divisor of the order of $S_n$? In other words, is it true that, for $n>39$, the number $p(n)$ of integer partitions of $n$ is never a divisor of $n!$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.90
records.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a graph of diameter $d$. For $i\in\{1,2,\ldots,d\}$, let $\Gamma_i$ be the graph on the same vertex set as $\Gamma$ with vertices $u,w$ adjacent in $\Gamma_i$ if and only if $d_\Gamma(u,w)=i$. Does there exist a $Q$-polynomial distance-regular graph $\Gamma$ of diameter 3 such that $\Gamma_2$ and $\Gamma_3$ are strongly regular?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.91
records.statement: Conjecture: The sum of squares of the degrees of the irreducible $p$-Brauer characters of a finite group $G$ is at least the $p'$-part of $|G|$.

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.92
records.statement: Conjecture: The number of irreducible $p$-Brauer characters of a finite group $G$ is bounded above by the maximum of the number of conjugacy classes $k(H)$ in $p'$-subgroups $H$ of $G$.

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.93
records.statement: Let $G$ be a group and let $k\geqslant 2$. Let $H_1,\ldots,H_k$ be subgroups of $G$, and $g_1,\ldots,g_k$ elements of $G$ such that the cosets $g_1H_1,\ldots,g_kH_k$ form a partition of $G$. Is it true that $|G:H_i|=|G:H_j|$ for some $i\ne j$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.94
records.statement: The Gruenberg--Kegel graph (or the prime graph) GK(G) of a finite group G is a labelled graph with vertex set consisting of all prime divisors of the order of G in which different vertices p and q are adjacent if and only if G contains an element of order pq. Let GK(G) denote the abstract graph obtained from GK(G) by removing all labels. A finite group G is said to be recognizable by the isomorphism type of its Gruenberg--Kegel graph if there are no finite groups H $\ncong$ G with GK(H) isomorphic to GK(G). Are there infinitely many (pairwise non-isomorphic) finite groups which are recognizable by the isomorphism type of the Gruenberg--Kegel graph?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.95
records.statement: Is there an almost simple but not simple group which is recognizable by the isomorphism type of its Gruenberg--Kegel graph?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.96
records.statement: Is it true that a periodic group containing an involution is locally finite if the centralizer of every element of even order is locally finite?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.97
records.statement: Is it true that for every positive rational number $r$ there exists a finite group $G$ such that $|\operatorname{Aut}(G)|/|G|=r$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.98
records.statement: Let w be a multilinear commutator word, and assume that G is a group where the set of w-values is covered by finitely many cyclic subgroups. Is it true that the verbal subgroup w(G) is finite-by-cyclic?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.99
records.statement: Conjecture: If $G$ is a transitive permutation group on a finite set $\Omega$, then for any distinct $\alpha,\beta\in\Omega$ there is an element $g\in G$ with $\alpha^g=\beta$ whose number of fixed points is different from 1.

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.100
records.statement: Suppose that $A$ and $G$ are finite groups such that $A$ acts coprimely on $G$ by automorphisms. Let $C=C_G(A)$ be the fixed-point subgroup, and let $C'$ denote its derived subgroup. Is it true that the number of $A$-invariant irreducible characters $\chi$ of $G$ whose restriction $\chi_C$ is never zero is exactly $|C/C'|$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.101
records.statement: Which finite almost simple groups are the automorphism groups of regular polytopes of rank 3? In other words, which finite almost simple groups are generated by three involutions two of which commute?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.102
records.statement: Let $V$ be a variety generated by a finite group, and let $f(n)$ be the order of the free group in $V$ on $n$ generators. Is it true that the sequence $\sqrt[n]{\log f(n)}$ has a limit as $n\to\infty$, and this limit is an integer?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.103
records.statement: A Hausdorff topological group G is called minimal if it does not admit a strictly coarser Hausdorff group topology. A topological group is called Raikov complete if its two-sided uniform structure is complete. Is it true that an arbitrary Cartesian product of Raikov complete minimal topological groups remains minimal?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.104
records.statement:
For a group word $w(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ on $n$ letters, define $e_0(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=x_1$ and $e_{k+1}(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=w(e_k(x_1,\ldots,x_n),\ldots,x_n)$ for all $k\in\mathbb N$. A group $G$ is said to satisfy the Engel type iterated identity $w$ if for all $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in G$ there exists $m\in\mathbb N$ such that $e_m(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=1$.

Conjecture: For every non-trivial word $w$, if a finitely generated branch group $G$ (see 15.12) satisfies the iterated identity $w$, then $G$ is a torsion group.

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.105
records.statement: A group word $w$ is said to be concise in a class $\mathcal C$ of groups if for every group $G$ in $\mathcal C$ such that the set $G_w$ of word values of $w$ in $G$ is finite, the verbal subgroup $w(G)=\langle G_w\rangle$ is also finite. Is every word concise in the class of residually finite groups?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.106
records.statement: A first order formula $\phi(x)$ in the group language with one free variable is said to be concise in a class $\mathcal C$ of groups if for every group $G$ in $\mathcal C$ such that the set $G_\phi$ of elements in $G$ satisfying $\phi$ is finite, the subgroup $\phi(G)$ generated by $G_\phi$ is also finite. Is every formula with one free variable concise in the class of residually finite groups?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.107
records.statement: A sequence $\{F_n\}$ of pairwise disjoint finite subsets of a topological group is called expansive if for every open subset $U$ there is a number $m$ such that $F_n\cap U\ne\emptyset$ for all $n>m$. Suppose that a countable group $G$ can be partitioned into countably many dense subsets. Is it true that in $G$ there exists an expansive sequence?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.108
records.statement: For a finite group $G$ let $\operatorname{Cod}(G)$ denote the set of irreducible character codegrees of $G$ (see 20.78). Define $\sigma(G)=\max\{|\pi(m)|:m\in\operatorname{Cod}(G)\}$, where $\pi(m)$ denotes the set of prime divisors of an integer $m$. Can the constant $k$ be taken as 4?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.109
records.statement: Conjecture: The derived length of a finite solvable group $G$ does not exceed $|\operatorname{Cod}(G)|-1$.

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.110
records.statement:
Let $S$ be a nonabelian finite simple group, and $x$ a nonidentity automorphism of $S$. Let $\alpha(x)$ be the smallest number of conjugates of $x$ in $G=\langle x,\operatorname{Inn}S\rangle$ that generate $G$.

(a) Conjecture: If $S$ is an exceptional group of Lie type, then $\alpha(x)\leqslant 5$ for every nonidentity automorphism $x$ of $S$.

(b) For each exceptional group $S$ of Lie type, find the largest value of $\alpha(x)$.

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.111
records.statement:
Let $S$ be a finite simple nonabelian group that is not isomorphic to any group ${}^2B_2(q)$. A nonidentity automorphism $x$ of $S$ is called a $\tau$-automorphism if every two conjugates of $x$ in $\langle x,\operatorname{Inn}(S)\rangle$ generate a subgroup of order not divisible by 3. If $S$ admits a $\tau$-automorphism, we call $S$ a $\tau$-group.

(a) List all $\tau$-groups up to isomorphism.

(b) Do $\tau$-automorphisms of odd order exist?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.112
records.statement:
A nonempty class $\mathcal X$ of finite groups is said to be complete if $\mathcal X$ is closed under taking subgroups, homomorphic images, and extensions. The symmetric boundary of a complete class $\mathcal X$ other than the class of all finite groups is defined as the largest integer $n$ such that $S_n\in\mathcal X$. For every positive integer $n\ne 3$, let $f_+(n)$ and $f_-(n)$ be respectively the maximum and the minimum of $\operatorname{BS}(\mathcal X)$, where $\mathcal X$ runs over all complete classes of symmetric boundary $n$.

(a) Find $f_+(n)$ for $n=4,5,6$.

(b) Is it true that $f_-(n)=n$ for all $n\ne 3$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.113
records.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group and $p$ be a prime. Let $\Psi_{p,G}$ be the class function of $G$ which vanishes on all $p$-singular elements of $G$ and whose value at each $p$-regular element $x$ of $G$ is the number of $p$-elements of $C_G(x)$.

(a) Is it true that $\Psi_{p,G}$ is a character of $G$?

(b) If yes, can $\Psi_{p,G}$ be afforded by a projective $RG$-module, where $R$ is a complete discrete valuation ring of characteristic zero such that the field of fractions of $R$ is a splitting field for $G$ and its subgroups, and the residue field $R/J(R)$ is a splitting field of characteristic $p$ for $G$ and its subgroups?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.114
records.statement: A finite group G is called weakly ab-maximal if |H : [H, H]| $\leqslant$ |G : [G, G]| for all H $\leqslant$ G. Do weakly ab-maximal groups have bounded derived length?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.115
records.statement: Let $C_1,\ldots,C_n$ be (left or right) cosets of a finite group $G$ such that $U:=C_1\cup\cdots\cup C_n$ is not $G$. Is it always true that $|G\setminus U|\geqslant |G|/2^n$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.116
records.statement: A group is boundedly acyclic if its bounded cohomology with trivial real coefficients vanishes in all positive degrees. Is every branch group boundedly acyclic?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.117
records.statement:
(a) Does there exist a finitely generated simple group that is of exponential growth but not of uniformly exponential growth?

(b) Does there exist a finitely generated hereditarily just-infinite group that is of exponential growth but not of uniformly exponential growth?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.118
records.statement: Is there any group which is not isomorphic to the quotient of a residually finite group by an amenable normal subgroup?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.119
records.statement: Does there exist a group $G$ that contains a family $(G_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ of finite-index subgroups such that for every $n$ there is a homomorphism $f_n:G_n\to\mathbb Z$ whose kernel is of type $F_n$, but not of type $F_{n+1}$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.120
records.statement:
A pro-p group is (relatively) strictly finitely presented if it is the pro-p completion of a group that is finitely presented (respectively, finitely presented in some finitely-based variety of groups). A pro-p group is finitely axiomatizable if it is determined up to isomorphism by a single sentence in the first-order language of group theory.

(a) Does there exist a (relatively) strictly finitely presented pro-p group that is not finitely axiomatizable in the class of all pro-p groups?

(b) In particular, is every finitely generated free pro-p group finitely axiomatizable?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.121
records.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime number. A group $\Gamma$ is called $p$-Jordan if there exist constants $J$ and $e$ such that any finite subgroup $G\subset\Gamma$ contains a normal abelian subgroup of order coprime to $p$ and of index at most $J\cdot |G(p)|^e$. (For example by the results of Brauer--Feit and Larsen--Pink, for any field $K$ of characteristic $p$ the group $\operatorname{GL}_n(K)$ is $p$-Jordan with $e=3$.) Let the $p$-Jordan exponent $e(\Gamma)$ of the group $\Gamma$ be the infimum of all constants $e$ for which the above bound holds for some constant $J=J(e)$.

a) Is it true that this infimum is always attained?

b) Is it true that $e(\Gamma)\leqslant 3$ for any $p$-Jordan group $\Gamma$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.122
records.statement: Let w be a group word, and G a profinite group. Is it true that the cardinality of the set of w-values in G is either finite or at least continuum?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.123
records.statement: Is it true that the extension of the A. Agrachev--R. Gamkrelidze construction of groups from pre-Lie rings suggested in Definition 66 produces groups from pre-Lie rings? If this extended construction does give a group, then it also gives a brace, and so an affirmative answer to this question would have consequences for the theory of set-theoretic solutions of the Yang--Baxter equation and for the theory of braces.

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.124
records.statement:
A group G is said to be virtually special if G has a finite-index subgroup isomorphic to the fundamental group of a special complex. A group G is called a CAT(0) group if it acts properly discontinuously and cocompactly by isometries on a CAT(0) metric space.

a) Is every CAT(0) free-by-cyclic group virtually special?

b) A weaker question: does every CAT(0) free-by-cyclic group virtually embed into a right-angled Artin group?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.125
records.statement:
Let $F_m$ be a free group of rank $m$ and let $\varphi\in\operatorname{Aut}(F_m)$ be a polynomially growing automorphism of maximal degree $m-1$, which means that for some (equivalently, any) free basis $\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}$ of $F_m$, the sequence $\max_i |\varphi^n(x_i)|$ grows at the rate of $n^{m-1}$, where $|g|$ denotes the minimal length of $g$ in the $x_i$ and their inverses.

a) Is the free-by-cyclic group $F_m\rtimes_\varphi\mathbb Z$ virtually special?

b) In particular, are the Hydra groups $G_m=F_m\rtimes\mathbb Z=\langle a_1,\ldots,a_m,t\mid t^{-1}a_1t=a_1,\ t^{-1}a_it=a_ia_{i-1}\text{ for all }i>1\rangle$ virtually special?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.126
records.statement: Do there exist finitely presented subgroups of right-angled Artin groups whose Dehn functions are super-exponential, or sub-exponential but not polynomial?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.127
records.statement: Let G be a right-angled Artin group. Is the stable commutator length scl(g) a rational number for every g $\in$ [G, G]?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.128
records.statement: Two groups $G_1$ and $G_2$ are said to be commensurable if there exist finite-index subgroups $H_1\leqslant G_1$ and $H_2\leqslant G_2$ (not necessarily of the same index) such that $H_1\cong H_2$. Let $A[F_4]$ and $A[H_4]$ denote the Artin groups of spherical types $F_4$ and $H_4$, respectively. Are these two groups commensurable?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.129
records.statement: If two Artin groups of spherical type are quasi-isometric, must they be commensurable? (This is not true for right-angled Artin groups.)

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.130
records.statement: Conjecture: Let $G$ be a finite additive abelian group with $|G|$ odd. Then any subset $A$ of $G$ with $|A|=n>2$ can be written as $\{a_1,\ldots,a_n\}$ in such a way that all the sums $a_1+a_2,a_2+a_3,\ldots,a_{n-1}+a_n,a_n+a_1$ are distinct.

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.131
records.statement: Construct a homomorphism of a subgroup of a Golod group onto an infinite AT-group.

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.132
records.statement: Based on the development of E. S. Golod's construction, for each prime number p, construct a finitely generated residually finite p-group with a non-trivial finite centre.

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.133
records.statement: Does a group need to have a subnormal abelian series if every countable subgroup of it has such a series?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.134
records.statement:
For a finite group $G$, let the type of $G$ be the function on positive integers whose value at $n$ is the number of solutions of the equation $x^n=1$ in $G$.

a) Is it true that a group having the same type as a group with trivial solvable radical must also have trivial solvable radical?

b) Is it true that a group having the same type as an almost simple group must be isomorphic to it?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.135
records.statement: For a finite group $G$, let $\chi_1(G)$ denote the totality of the degrees of all irreducible complex characters of $G$ with allowance for their multiplicities. Suppose that $H$ is a finite group with $\chi_1(H)=\chi_1(G)$. If $G$ has trivial solvable radical, must $H$ also have trivial solvable radical?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.136
records.statement: Let G be a profinite group with fewer than $2^{\aleph_0}$ conjugacy classes of elements of infinite order. Must G be a torsion group?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.137
records.statement: If the $p$-th powers in a finite $p$-group form a subgroup, must that subgroup be powerful? That is, for $p\ne 2$, if the $p$-th powers in a $p$-group of exponent $p^2$ form a subgroup, must that subgroup be abelian? For a 2-group of exponent 8, if the squares form a subgroup, must that subgroup be abelian?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.138
records.statement: Let G be an infinite finitely presented group such that every subgroup of infinite index is free. Must G be isomorphic to either a free group or a surface group?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.139
records.statement: Let G be a hyperbolic group which is virtually compact special in the sense of Haglund--Wise. Suppose that the set of second Betti numbers of the finite-index subgroups of G is bounded. Must G be virtually either a free group or a surface group?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.140
records.statement: Let G be a torsion-free group of type $F_\infty$ of infinite cohomological dimension. Must G contain a copy of Thompson's group F?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.141
records.statement: Let $G=G_1\amalg_H G_2$ be a free pro-$p$ product of coherent pro-$p$ groups with polycyclic amalgamation. Is $G$ coherent?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.142
records.statement: A group $G$ is said to be invariably generated by $a$ and $b$ if $G$ is generated by the conjugates $a^g,b^h$ for every $g,h$. Let $p\ne q$ be fixed primes. Does every finite group embed into a finite group invariably generated by an element of order $p$ and an element of order $q$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.143
records.statement: (Well-known problem). Is Thompson's group F automatic?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.144
records.statement: Conjecture: Every subgroup of Thompson's group F is either elementary amenable or else contains a subgroup isomorphic to F.

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.145
records.statement:
Is Thompson's group F quasi-isometric

(a) to F $\times$ Z?

(b) to F $\times$ F?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.146
records.statement: (Well-known problem). A classifying space for a group $G$ is a connected CW-complex with fundamental group $G$ and all higher homotopy groups trivial. A group is of type $F_n$ if it has a classifying space with finite $n$-skeleton. For example, type $F_1$ is equivalent to finite generation, and type $F_2$ is equivalent to finite presentability. Type $F_\infty$ means type $F_n$ for all $n$. For $n\geqslant 3$, does every group of type $F_{n-1}$ embed as a subgroup of a group of type $F_n$? Or even in a group of type $F_\infty$?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.147
records.statement: A subgroup H of a right-orderable group G is said to be right-relatively convex if it is convex under some right ordering on G. Is the lattice of right-relatively convex subgroups of a right-orderable group always a sublattice of the lattice of its subgroups?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.148
records.statement: Is it true that the lattice of right-relatively convex subgroups of a right-orderable group is distributive if and only if it is a chain?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.149
records.statement: Are there order automorphisms of Dlab groups that are not inner automorphisms?

records.name: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.150
records.statement: Let $G$ be an extension of a normal elementary abelian subgroup $A$ by an elementary abelian group $B\cong G/A$ such that $A$ contains an element $a$ with $C_B(a)=1$. Is it true that the rank of the subgroup $Z(\langle a,B\rangle)\cap\langle a,B\rangle'$ is at most the rank of $B$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.1
records.statement:
Is the crossing number additive under connected sum:
$c(K_{1}\#K_{2}) = c(K_{1}) + c(K_{2})$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.2
records.statement:
(a) Show that if $P$ is a nontrivial satellite operator and $K_{P}$ is a nontrivial
satellite of a knot $K$, then

$$
c(K_{P}) \geq c(K),
$$

where $c$ denotes the crossing number.
(b) More generally, show that if $P$ is a satellite operator then

$$
c(K_{P}) \geq c(K) \cdot w(P)^{2},
$$

where $w(P)$ denotes the geometric winding number.

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.3
records.statement:
How does unknotting number behave under connected sum and
mutation?
(a) Does the connected sum of $n$ nontrivial knots have unknotting number at
least $n$?
(b) Is unknotting number invariant under mutation?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.4
records.statement:
Let $P$ be a nontrivial satellite pattern with winding number
$w(P) \neq 0$. Then for any nontrivial knot $K$ and its satellite $K_{P}$ , one has

$$
u(K_{P}) \geq w(P) + 1.
$$

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.5
records.statement:
Is there a relationship between genus and unknotting number
for specific classes of knots? Here are two instances of classes of knots for which
there might be an interesting answer.
(a) Conjecture (Murasugi-Przytycki). For every positive fibered knot $K$, the
genus of $K$ equals its unknotting number.
(b) Question (Stoimenow). For every alternating fibered knot, is the genus
greater than or equal to the unknotting number?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.6
records.statement:
Suppose that $V_{1}$ and $V_{2}$ are $S$–equivalent Seifert forms. Does
there exist a fixed knot $K$ bounding Seifert surfaces $F_{1}$ and $F_{2}$ for which the as-
sociated Seifert forms are $V_{1}$ and $V_{2}$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.7
records.statement:
Show that the sequence of absolute values of the coefficients of
the Alexander polynomial of a link are:
(a) concave $($ Fox’s trapezoidal conjecture $)$, or
(b) for an alternating link, log concave $($ Stoimenow’s strong Fox conjecture $)$.
(c) For a positive link, is the sequence of the coefficients of the Conway poly-
nomial strongly log concave?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.8
records.statement:
Which multi-variable Laurent polynomials arise as the multi-
variable Alexander polynomial of a link in the 3-sphere or, more generally, a ho-
mology 3-sphere?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.9
records.statement:
If Dehn surgery on a knot $K$ gives a lens space, then $K$ is a
Berge knot.

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.10
records.statement:
(Generalized Property R Conjecture). Let $L \subset S^{3}$ be an $n$-
component link such that 0-framed Dehn surgery on $L$ results in $\#^{n}(S^{1} \times S^{2})$. Is
there a sequence of handleslides converting $L$ into an $n$-component unlink?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.11
records.statement:
(Cabling conjecture). Let $K \subset S^{3}$ be a knot and $r \in \mathbb{Q}$. If
$r$-framed Dehn surgery on $K$ is not prime, then $K$ is a nontrivial cable of a knot
$J \subset S^{3}$ and $r$ is the slope of the cabling annulus.

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.12
records.statement:
This problem presents several variations on the Cosmetic
Surgery Conjecture, discussed in turn below.
(a) $($ Cosmetic Surgery Conjecture $)$ Two surgeries along inequivalent slopes are
never purely cosmetic.
(b) $($ Oriented knot complement conjecture $)$ If $K_{1}$ and $K_{2}$ are knots in a closed,
oriented 3-manifold $N$ whose complements are homeomorphic via an orientation-
preserving homeomorphism, then there exists a homeomorphism of $N$ tak-
ing $K_{1}$ to $K_{2}$.
(c) Let $K \subset S^{3}$ be a nontrivial knot, then $K$ admits no purely cosmetic surg-
eries.
(d) If $K \subset S^{3}$ is not the torus knot $T_{2g+1,2}$, then $K$ admits no chirally cos-
metic surgeries with inequivalent slopes.

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.13
records.statement:
Let $K$ be a null-homotopic knot in a 3-manifold $Y$ , and let
$Y_{0}(K)$ be the manifold obtained by 0-surgery on $K$.
(a) Conjecture: Let $F$ be a Seifert surface for $K$, and let $\widetilde{F} \subset Y_{0}(K)$ be the
closed surface obtained by capping off $\partial F$ with a disk. If $Y_{0}(K)$ is a surface
bundle over $S^{1}$ with fiber in the homology class $[\widetilde{F}]$, then $K$ is a fibered
knot with fiber in the homology class $[F]$.
(b) Conjecture: If $F$ is taut in the exterior of $K$ in $Y$ , then $\widetilde{F}$ is also taut in
$Y_{0}(K)$.

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.14
records.statement:
For which nonzero $r \in \mathbb{Q}$ is it true that for every nontrivial
knot $K \subset S^{3}$ there is a homomorphism

$$
\pi_{1}(S^{3}_{r}(K)) \to \operatorname{SU}(2)
$$

with nonabelian image?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.15
records.statement:
(a) Are there integral homology spheres with arbitrarily large (integral) Dehn
surgery number? Are there irreducible examples? Does the connected sum
of $n$ nontrivial homology spheres have Dehn surgery number at least $n$?
(b) Given a 3-manifold $Y$ with a smooth orientation-preserving $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ sym-
metry $\varphi$, Sakuma [Sak01] (generalizing [PS01]) proved that $Y$ admits a
surgery description compatible with the symmetry. Define the equivariant
(integral) Dehn surgery number of $(Y, \varphi)$ as the minimal number of con-
nected components of any such link. Do there exist $(Y, \varphi)$ whose equivari-
ant (integral) Dehn surgery number is arbitrarily larger than the (integral)
Dehn surgery number?
(c) Following the remarks below, we can consider the following specific case:
Does there exist a manifold with a 2-fold symmetry whose equivariant
(integral) Dehn surgery number is larger than the (integral) Dehn surgery
number?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.16
records.statement:
(a) Given a knot $K \subset S^{3}$ determine all knots $K' \subset S^{3}$ for which the branched
double covers of $S^{3}$ along $K$ and $K'$ are homeomorphic.
(b) Find a set of moves on links in $S^{3}$ so that two links are related by these
moves if and only if they have the same branched double cover.

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.17
records.statement:
Can an alternating link and a non-alternating link have home-
omorphic branched double covers?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.18
records.statement:
(a) $($ Meridional Rank Conjecture $)$ Is the meridional $\operatorname{rank} \mu(L)$ of every link
$L$ equal to its bridge number $b(L)$?
(b) Given two knots $K_{1}, K_{2} \subset S^{3}$ such that $\pi_{1}(S^{3}\setminus K_{1})$ and $\pi_{1}(S^{3}\setminus K_{2})$ have
the same finite quotients, does $\mu(K_{1}) = \mu(K_{2})$? In particular, is it possible
to explicitly detect the meridional $\operatorname{rank} \mu(K)$ of a knot $K \subset S^{3}$ from the
finite quotients of $\pi_{1}(S^{3}\setminus K)$?
(c) Given two links $L_{1}, L_{2} \subset S^{3}$, if there exists a surjective homomorphism
$\pi_{1}(S^{3}\setminus L_{1}) \twoheadrightarrow\pi_{1}(S^{3}\setminus L_{2})$ that sends the meridians of $L_{1}$ to the meridians
of $L_{2}$, do the bridge numbers satisfy $b(L_{1}) \geq b(L_{2})$?
(d) Given two knots $K_{1}, K_{2} \subset S^{3}$, if there exists a surjective homomorphism
$\pi_{1}(S^{3}\setminus K_{1}) \twoheadrightarrow\pi_{1}(S^{3}\setminus K_{2})$ (which may not send meridians to meridians):
(i) Do the meridional ranks satisfy $\mu(K_{1}) \geq \mu(K_{2})$?
(ii) Do the bridge numbers satisfy $b(K_{1}) \geq b(K_{2})$?
(e) Let $K \subset S^{3}$ be a hyperbolic knot. Is every subgroup of $\pi_{1}(S^{3}\setminus K)$ generated
by at most $b(K) - 1$ meridians free? See [BJW18].

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.19
records.statement:
Let $Y = Y_{1}\#Y_{2}$ be a connected sum of 3-manifolds with $Y_{i} \neq$
$S^{3}$, for $i = 1, 2$. Let $\Phi: Y \to Y$ be a Dehn twist around the connected sum separating
2-sphere, and assume $Y_{1}$ and $Y_{2}$ are such that $\Phi$ is not isotopic to the identity. Does
there exist a knot $K \subseteq Y$ such that $K$ and $\Phi(K)$ are not ambiently isotopic?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.20
records.statement:
(a) Are there any null-homologous Floer minimal knots with irreducible com-
plements other than the Borromean knots $B_{g}, g \geq 0$, in any 3-manifolds?
It is reasonable to make the following more concrete conjectures.
(b) Conjecture (Ni): If $b_{1}(Y) < 2$, then the only null-homologous Floer mini-
mal knot in $Y$ is the unknot.
(c) Conjecture (Ni): If the Thurston norm of $Y$ is not identically zero, then $Y$
does not contain any null-homologous Floer minimal knot with irreducible
complement.
(d) Conjecture (Hedden, Rasmussen): The only Floer minimal knots in lens
spaces are simple knots.

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.21
records.statement:
(a) For a given positive integer $g$, are there only finitely many L-space knots
of genus $g$?
A related but more general question is:
(b) Question (Hedden): For which knots $L \subset S^{3}$ are there only finitely many
knots $K \subset S^{3}$ with
$\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(S^{3},K) \cong \widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(S^{3},L)$?

(c) In some special cases, one expects stronger results saying that a class of
knots is characterized by its knot Floer homology. We state 3 conjectures,
ordered by their strength.
(i) For a knot $K \subset S^{3}$, if
$\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(S^{3},K) \cong \widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(S^{3},T_{2g+1,2})$, then
$K = T_{2g+1,2}$.
(ii) For a knot $K \subset S^{3}$, if
$\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(S^{3},K) \cong \widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(S^{3},T_{p,q})$, then $K$ is an
iterated torus knot.
(iii) Conjecture (Ni): For an L-space knot $K \subset S^{3}$, if all roots of $\Delta_{K}(t)$
lie on the unit circle, then $K$ is an iterated torus knot.

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.22
records.statement:
If $K$ is a hyperbolic $L$-space knot, show that its branched cover
$\Sigma_{2}(K)$ is not an $L$-space.

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.23
records.statement:
Let $K$ be a cubic graph embedded in the plane, and let $\mathrm{Tait}(K)$
be the number of Tait colorings of $K$.
(a) Is $\dim J^{7}(K) = \mathrm{Tait}(K)$?
(b) Is $J^{5}(K)$ nonzero when $K$ is bridgeless?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.24
records.statement:
(Jones Unknot Detection).
(a) Is there a nontrivial knot with the same Jones polynomial as the unknot?

(b) Does there exist a nontrivial knot whose colored Jones polynomials are all
trivial?
(c) Is there a nontrivial knot with trivial HOMFLYPT polynomial? (A knot
with trivial HOMFLYPT polynomial would have trivial Jones polynomial.)

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.25
records.statement:
(a) Conjecture: The noncommutative $A$-ideal of a knot $K$ is exactly the an-
nihilator of the colored Jones polynomial $($ the infinite dimensional vector
whose entries are the colored Jones polynomials of $K)$.
(b) $($ AJ Conjecture $)$ Let $A(K; L, M)$ be the $A$-polynomial of the knot $K$, and
$\alpha(K, q; M, L)$ a polynomial of minimal degree in $L$ and co-prime coeffi-
cients that annihilates the colored Jones polynomial $J_{n}(K; q)$. Then

$$
\alpha(K, -1; M, L) = A(K; L, M)
$$

up to a factor depending on $M.$

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.26
records.statement:
(Jones Slope Conjecture). For a knot $K$, the Jones slopes $js(K)$
are the set of cluster points in

$$
\left\{\frac{4}{n^{2}}\deg_{+}\bigl(J_{n}(K;q)\bigr)\right\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}
\cup
\left\{\frac{4}{n^{2}}\deg_{-}\bigl(J_{n}(K;q)\bigr)\right\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}},
$$

where deg $^{+}$ denotes the highest degree and deg $^{-}$ the lowest degree.

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.27
records.statement:
(Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami Volume Conjecture). For a
link $L \subset S^{3}$,

$$
\frac{1}{2\pi}\operatorname{Vol}_{\mathrm{hyp}}(S^{3}-L)
=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\log\left|J_{n}\bigl(L,e^{2\pi i/n}\bigr)\right|.
$$

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.28
records.statement:
Let $L$ be a link in the thickened annulus $S^{1} \times I \times I$.
(a) Wrapping conjecture: $w(L)$ is equal to the maximal nonzero annular de-
gree of the annular Kauffman bracket of $L$.
(b) Categorifed wrapping conjecture: $w(L)$ is equal to the maximal nonzero
annular grading of the annular Khovanov homology of $L$.

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.29
records.statement:
Is the first inequality below true? If so, is the second?
(a) $(\operatorname{Vol}$-Det Conjecture $)$ For any alternating hyperbolic knot $K \subset S^{3}$,
vol $(K) < 2\pi \log \det(K),$
where vol is the hyperbolic volume of $K$ and det is the determinant.
(b) For any hyperbolic knot $K \subset S^{3}$,
vol $(K) < 2\pi \log \operatorname{rank} \mathrm{Kh}(K),$
where Kh is the reduced Khovanov homology of $K$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.30
records.statement:
Does the Khovanov homology of every nontrivial knot contain
2-torsion?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.31
records.statement:
(a) Compute the Khovanov homology for all torus knots $T(m, n)$.
(b) Compute the Khovanov–Rozansky $\mathfrak{g}\mathfrak{l}(N)$ homology for all torus knots.

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.32
records.statement:
(a) Recover the Jones polynomial of links $L \subset \mathbb{R}^{3}$ by counting solutions to
the Kapustin–Witten equations on $\mathbb{R}^{3} \times \mathbb{R}_{+}$ with Nahm pole boundary
conditions;
(b) Recover the Khovanov homology of links $L \subset \mathbb{R}^{3}$ by counting solutions to
the Haydys–Witten equations on $\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^{3} \times \mathbb{R}_{+}$ with Nahm pole boundary
conditions;

(c) Use the Kapustin–Witten or Haydys–Witten equations to construct invari-
ants of links in other 3-manifolds.

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.33
records.statement:
Describe topological necessary or sufficient conditions for a
link to have KR-parity. For example:
(a) Are all links with KR-parity positive? Quasipositive?
(b) Do all algebraic links have KR-parity?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.34
records.statement:
(a) Khovanov and Rozansky [KR08b] used braid presentations to define a
triply graded link homology theory whose Euler characteristic is the HOM-
FLYPT polynomial. Find a description of this homology in terms of arbi-
trary planar diagrams of the link, and determine whether some flavor of
this theory is functorial with respect to link cobordisms.
(b) Do the same for Cautis’ link homologies from [Cau17], which are also
defined in terms of braid presentations.

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.35
records.statement:
(a) Is symplectic Khovanov homology isomorphic to Khovanov homology, over
$\mathbb{Z}$?
(b) Give a construction of odd symplectic Khovanov homology $\mathrm{Kh}^{\mathrm{odd}}_{\mathrm{symp}}(K)$.

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.36
records.statement:
Categorify the ($\mathfrak{s}\mathfrak{l}(2), \mathfrak{s}\mathfrak{l}(N)$, HOMFLYPT) skein algebras for
surfaces.

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.37
records.statement:
(a) For every link $L \subset \mathbb{R}^{3}$, every simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$, and every coloring
of the components of $L$ with irreducible representations of $\mathfrak{g}$, construct
a bigraded link homology theory that is functorial under link cobordisms,
and whose Euler characteristic is the Reshetikhin–Turaev link invariant
associated to $\mathfrak{g}$ and $L$.
(b) For each of the theories above, define an odd version $($ with the same mod
2 reduction $)$ or explain the obstruction to its existence.

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.38
records.statement:
What is the structure of the smooth knot concordance group?
(a) Is there a torsion element of the smooth concordance group $\mathcal{C}$ having order
other than two? Is there a torsion element in $\mathcal{C}_{TS}$, the smooth concordance
group of topologically slice knots, having order other than two?
(b) Is there a knot $K$ having concordance order two in $\mathcal{C}$ that is not concordant
to a strongly negatively amphichiral knot?
(c) Do there exist infinitely divisible elements in $\mathcal{C}$, that is, does there exist $K$
such that for infinitely many $n \in \mathbb{N}$, there is a $J$ such that $[K] = n[J]$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.39
records.statement:
(a) Do the algebraic knots freely generate a subgroup of the smooth concor-
dance group $\mathcal{C}$?
(b) Do the algebraic knots freely generate a subgroup of the topological con-
cordance group $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{TOP}}$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.40
records.statement:
A satellite operator $P \subset S^{1} \times D^{2}$ induces an operation $P$ on
the concordance group $\mathcal{C}$ [Gor75].
(a) Let $P$ be a winding number one satellite operator with $P(\operatorname{U}) \simeq \operatorname{U}$.
If
$P(K) \simeq \operatorname{U}$, does this mean that $K \simeq \operatorname{U}$?
(b) Is the Whitehead doubling operator injective on $\mathcal{C}$? Can we exhibit any
(winding-number-zero) operator that is injective on $\mathcal{C}$?
(c) Conjecture (Hedden; see [HPC21]). The only homomorphisms on $\mathcal{C}$ in-
duced by satellite operators are the zero map, the identity, and the invo-
lution induced by orientation reversal.
(d) Conjecture (Hedden, Pinzón Caicedo) Let $P$ be a non-constant satellite
operator with winding number zero. Does $\\langle \\operatorname{im} P \\rangle$ necessarily have infinite
rank? Some special cases are:
(i) Does there always exist a fixed knot $K$ such that $\langle\{P(nK)\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\rangle$ has
infinite rank?
(ii) If $\{nK\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}$ is any rank-one subgroup of $\mathcal{C}$, does $\langle\{P(nK)\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\rangle$ have
infinite rank?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.41
records.statement:
This problem is concerned with the stable 4-genus $g_{s}(K)$ of a
knot $K$, defined below.
(a) Is there a knot $K$ such that $g_{s}(K) \in \mathbb{Q}\setminus\mathbb{Z}$?
(b) Is there a knot $K$ such that $g_{s}(K) \notin \mathbb{Q}$?
(c) Is there a knot $K$ such that $0 < g_{s}(K) < 1/2$?
(d) [Liv10, Question 1] Does $K$ represent a torsion element in the concor-
dance group if and only if $g_{s}(K) = 0$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.42
records.statement:
Do there exist algebraically concordant Seifert forms $V_{1}$ and
$V_{2}$ for which there do not exist concordant knots $K_{1}$ and $K_{2}$ with Seifert forms $V_{1}$
and $V_{2}$, respectively?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.43
records.statement:
Does knot Floer homology give a categorification of the Fox–
Milnor condition?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.44
records.statement:
(a) If $K \in \mathcal{F}_{n}$ for all $n$, is $K$ topologically slice?
(b) If $K \in \mathcal{T}_{n}$ for all $n$, is $K$ smoothly slice?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.45
records.statement:
(a) For arbitrary $n \geq 2.5$ and $g > 1$, does there exist a knot in $\mathcal{F}_{n}$ with
topological slice genus at least $g$?
(b) For arbitrary $n \geq 0$ and $g > 1$, does there exist a knot in $\mathcal{T}_{n}$ with smooth
slice genus at least $g$?
(c) Could the $L^{(2)}$-signature invariants used to obstruct membership in deeper
levels of the solvable/bipolar filtration be used to give bounds on the slice
genus?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.46
records.statement:
(a) Determine the topological slice genera of torus knots. In particular, does
the topological slice genus of a torus knot equal half the absolute value of
its maximal Levine–Tristram signature?
(b) Is a two-bridge knot topologically slice if and only if it is ribbon, if and
only if it is topologically homotopy-ribbon?
(c) Are the Casson–Gordon ribbon and topological sliceness obstructions [CG86]
complete for two-bridge knots?
(d) Can the difference between the smooth and topological slice genus of a
two-bridge knot be arbitrarily large?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.47
records.statement:
Given a smooth knot $K \subset S^{3}$, determine its nonorientable 4-
genus $\gamma_{4}$, i.e. the minimal first Betti number for all compact nonorientable smooth
surfaces $F$ properly embedded in $B^{4}$ with boundary $K$. This question may be devel-
oped in several directions:
(1) (Allen’s Geography Question [All23]) For a given knot $K \subset S^{3}$, find
the pairs $(e, b) \in \mathbb{Z}^{2}$ realized by the normal Euler number and first Betti
number of a nonorientable bounding surface $F$.
(2) By analogy with the Milnor Conjecture for the orientable 4-genus of torus
knots, what is the nonorientable 4-genus of a torus knot $T_{p,q}$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.48
records.statement:
(a) Suppose $K$ and $K\#J$ are (smoothly) doubly slice knots.
Must $J$ be a
(smoothly) doubly slice knot?
(b) Does there exist a knot that is smoothly slice, topologically doubly slice, and
not smoothly doubly slice but such that $K\#K$ is smoothly doubly slice?
(c) Let $M$ and $N$ be closed 3-manifolds such that $M$ and $M\#N$ embed (smoothly)
in $S^{4}$. Must $N$ embed (smoothly) in $S^{4}$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.49
records.statement:
(a) What is the structure of the equivariant concordance groups?
(b) Is the strongly negative amphichiral concordance group abelian?
(c) For any type of knot involution, is it possible to exhibit $K_{1}$ and $K_{2}$ that
are equivariantly concordant but not standardly equivariantly concordant?
(d) Does there exist a freely periodic slice knot that is not equivariantly slice?
(e) (Boyle-Rouse) Is every periodic or freely periodic $L$-space knot either a
torus knot or an iterated torus knot?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.50
records.statement:
(a) Is every slice knot a ribbon knot?
(b) Is every slice link ribbon?
(c) Suppose $K$ is a knot with smooth four-genus $g_{4}(K) = g$. Does $K$ bound a
smooth, genus $g$, ribbon surface $F$ in $B^{4}$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.51
records.statement: Does every ribbon knot arise as a symmetric union?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.52
records.statement:
Given $K$ in $S^{3}$, is there an algorithm to detect if $K$ is slice?
Ribbon?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.53
records.statement:
(a) Which knot properties are hereditary under ribbon concordance? Is the
property of being alternating hereditary under ribbon concordance?
(b) Which knot properties imply minimality under ribbon concordance? Are
positive knots minimal under ribbon concordance?
(c) Which knot invariants are monotone under ribbon concordance? Is cross-
ing number, bridge number, or braid index monotone under ribbon con-
cordance?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.54
records.statement:
This problem is concerned with the restriction of the partial
ordering $\geq$ coming from ribbon concordance to the concordance class $[K]$ of a knot
$K$.
(a) What can be said about the order type of $[K]$?
(b) Does it depend on $[K]$? Must it contain a (unique) minimal element?
(c) (Gordon) Does there exist a concordance class of knots that contains two
minimal elements with respect to ribbon concordance?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.55
records.statement:
Suppose that $C$ is a ribbon concordance from a fibered knot $K_{1}$
to a fibered knot $K_{0}$.
(a) Does the capped-off monodromy of $K_{1}$ (i.e. extended over a disk) extend to
a compression body whose lower boundary gives the capped-off monodromy
of $K_{0}$?
(b) Is $C$ fibered by compression bodies?
(c) Suppose a fibered knot in a homology 3-sphere bounds a homotopy-ribbon
disk $D$ in a contractible 4-manifold $V$ . Is $V \setminus\nu(D)$ fibered by handlebodies?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.56
records.statement:
(Hom). If $K_{0}$ and $K_{1}$ are ribbon concordant and

$$
\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(K_{0}) \cong \widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(K_{1}),
$$

are $K_{0}$ and $K_{1}$ isotopic?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.57
records.statement:
(a) In either the smooth or topological settings, are 0-shake slice knots slice?
(b) Does there exist a knot $K$ whose topological 0-shake slice genus is strictly
less than the topological slice genus?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.58
records.statement:
What concordance information about a knot $K$ is contained in
its 0-trace $X_{0}(K)$ and in its 0-surgery $S^{3}_{0}(K)$?
Specifically,
(a) Suppose $K$ and $K'$ have homeomorphic 0-traces.
(i) Are $K$ and $K'$ topologically concordant?
(ii) What if one just assumes $K$ and $K'$ have homeomorphic 0-surgeries?
(iii) What if one just assumes $K$ and $K'$ have 0-surgeries that are topolog-
ically homology cobordant, preserving the homology class of a merid-
ian.

(b) Suppose $K$ and $K'$ have homeomorphic 0-surgeries, where the image of
the meridian of $K$ is freely homotopic to the meridian of $K'$. Are $K$ and
$K'$ smoothly concordant?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.59
records.statement:
Let $K \subset S^{3}$ be a slice knot.
(a) Determine the set $\mathcal{R}(K)$ of ribbon disks bounded by $K$ modulo isotopy.
(b) Determine the set $\mathcal{D}(K)$ of slice disks bounded by $K$ modulo isotopy and
local knotting.
(c) Determine the set $\mathcal{H}\mathcal{R}(K)$ of homotopy-ribbon disks bounded by $K$ modulo
isotopy.
(d) If $K$ is fibered, determine the set $\mathcal{F}\mathcal{H}\mathcal{R}(K)$ of fibered, homotopy-ribbon
disks bounded by $K$ in some homotopy 4-ball, modulo isotopy.

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.60
records.statement:
Is there a knot in $S^{3}$ that is not smoothly slice in $B^{4}$ but is
smoothly slice in an integer homology ball? What about a $\mathbb{Z}$/2-homology ball?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.61
records.statement:
A knot in $S^{3}$ bounds a topological disk in $B^{4}$ by coning (not
necessarily locally flat); this problem asks about topological disks that a knot in a
homology sphere $Y$ might bound in a homology or homotopy ball bounded by $Y$ .
(a) Given a locally flat knot in an integer homology 3-sphere, is it concordant
to a knot in $S^{3}$, via a locally flat annulus in a topological integer homology
cobordism? Variation: Can the homology cobordism be taken to be simply
connected?
(b) Given an arbitrary knot in an integer homology 3-sphere $Y$ , does it bound
an embedded disc (not necessarily locally flat) in $\Delta$, the Freedman filling
of $Y$ ? Variation: Is there such a disk in a homology ball bounded by $Y$ ?
(c) Is there a link in an integer homology 3-sphere, each of whose components
is independently concordant to a knot in $S^{3}$, that is not itself concordant
to a link in $S^{3}$.
(d) Suppose that $\mathbb{Z}_{n}$ acts semi-freely on the homology sphere $Y$ , with fixed
point set a knot $K$. Does the action of $\mathbb{Z}_{n}$ extend semi-freely over $\Delta$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.62
records.statement:
(a) Are all good boundary links topologically slice? Freely topologically slice?
