(b) A special case of interest: Is the Whitehead double of the Borromean rings
(with any choice of clasps) topologically slice?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.63
records.statement:
Is there a knot type with Legendrian representatives that do
not destabilize but have arbitrarily negative Thurston–Bennequin number?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.64
records.statement:
(a) Let $L \subset (S^{3}, \xi_{std})$ be a transverse link such that the branched double cover
$(\Sigma_{2}(L), \xi_{L})$ is Stein fillable. Is $L$ transversely isotopic to the closure of a
quasipositive braid?
(b) Is the same true if $(\Sigma_{n}(L), \xi_{L})$ is Stein fillable for some $n > 2$?
(c) Does Stein fillability of the branched cover imply that the slice-Bennequin
inequality must be sharp for the given link?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.65
records.statement:
Decomposable Lagrangian cobordisms between Legendrian knots
or links in $\mathbb{R}^{3}$ are compositions of certain simple pieces admitting diagrammatic de-
scriptions [EHK16]. Such cobordisms necessarily have no index 2 critical points.
Is every exact Lagrangian cobordism without index 2 critical points Lagrangian iso-
topic to a decomposable Lagrangian cobordism?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.66
records.statement:
For Legendrian links $\Lambda_{1}, \Lambda_{2} \subset (\mathbb{R}^{3}, \xi_{std})$, write $\Lambda_{1} \preceq \Lambda_{2}$ if
there is an exact Lagrangian cobordism in the symplectization $\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^{3}$ from $\Lambda_{1}$ to
$\Lambda_{2}$. Is $\preceq$ a partial order?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.67
records.statement:
Given a Legendrian link in the standard contact $\mathbb{R}^{3}$ besides the
standard unknot or Hopf link, classify its exact Lagrangian fillings up to compactly
supported Hamiltonian isotopy.

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.68
records.statement:
Determine the smooth knot types that have Legendrian repre-
sentatives with orientable exact Lagrangian fillings.

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.69
records.statement:
Let $L \subset (S^{3}, \xi_{std})$ be a transverse link with

$$
sl_{\Sigma}(L) = -\chi(\Sigma),
$$

for some Seifert surface $\Sigma$. Must $L$ be strongly quasipositive?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.70
records.statement:
(a) Let $L \subset (S^{3}, \xi_{std})$ be a transverse link with

$$
sl_{\Sigma}(L) = -\chi(\Sigma),
$$

for some smooth surface $\Sigma \subset B^{4}$ bounded by $L$. Is $L$ quasipositive?
(b) Is the class of strongly quasipositive links equal to the class of quasipositive
links whose Seifert and smooth slice genera are equal?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.71
records.statement: Does a Gordian unknot exist?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.72
records.statement:
(The equilateral stuck unknots conjecture.). Are there equilat-
eral embedded polygons that are unknotted yet cannot be unknotted through polygons
preserving edge lengths? Such an unknot is said to be stuck.

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.73
records.statement:
(The 15 pearls conjecture). Is the pearl number of the trefoil
equal to 15?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.74
records.statement:
How does ropelength behave under connected sum of knots?
Here are two conjectures, the second a weakening of the first.
(a) For any knot or link types $K_{1}$ and $K_{2}$,
Rop $(K_{1}\#K_{2}) \leq$ Rop $(K_{1}) +$ Rop $(K_{2}) - (4\pi - 4).$
(b) For any knot or link types $K_{1}$ and $K_{2}$,

$$
Rop(K_{1}\#K_{2}) \leq Rop(K_{1}) + Rop(K_{2}) - c,
$$

where $c > 0$ is some constant independent of knot type.

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.75
records.statement:
(a) Find some knot energy on the space of smoothly embedded unknotted circles
in $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ for which all unknotted critical points are great circles.
(b) Define a gradient flow for this knot energy which yields a deformation
retract of the space of unknots to the subspace of great circles.

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.76
records.statement:
(a) Is there an algorithm to detect the unknot that runs in polynomial time
(as a function of the number of crossings in an input diagram)?
(b) What is the structure of the unknot Reidemeister graph?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.77
records.statement:
How many Reidemeister moves are required to relate two dia-
grams of a knot (as a function of their numbers of crossings)?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.78
records.statement:
Let $D$ be any diagram of the unknot with $n$ crossings. Let $h(D)$
be the smallest number such that some series of Reidemeister moves that transforms

$D$ to a 0-crossing diagram has the property that all intermediate diagrams have at
most $h(D)$ crossings. Define $h(n)$ to be the maximum of $h(D)$ over all $n$-crossing
diagrams of the unknot. A diagram represents a hard unknot if $h(D) > n$. What
is $h(n)$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.79
records.statement:
Are there additional moves that, when added to the three Rei-
demeister moves, allow for strict monotonic descent in the crossing number of an
unknot diagram?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.80
records.statement:
Is unknotting number computable? Is there even an algorithm
to decide whether a knot has unknotting number one?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.81
records.statement:
(a) Are all knots trivial?
(b) Conjecture: The Bing sling is knotted.

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.82
records.statement:
(a) What is a positive knot?
(b) Describe a simple set of moves to convert between two positive diagrams
of the same knot or link.

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.83
records.statement:
Determine the algebraic structure of the concordance group $\mathcal{O}$
of open strings.
(a) Is it abelian?
(b) Does it contain torsion?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.84
records.statement:
For a classical knot, does its slice genus as a virtual knot agree
with its slice genus as a classical knot?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.85
records.statement:
Let $K$ be a hyperbolic knot in $S^{3}$ and $\chi(K)$ the space of con-
jugacy classes of $\operatorname{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{C})$ representations of $\pi_{1}(S^{3} - K)$. There is a distinguished
component of $\chi(K)$ that contains the discrete faithful representation coming from
the finite volume hyperbolic structure on the complement of $K$. Does this component
always contain an arc of representations to $\operatorname{SO}(3)$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.86
records.statement:
(a) Every connected cubic $($ i.e. trivalent $)$ graph has freeness index at least 2.
(b) Every graph has freeness index at least two.
(c) There is a graph with freeness index two.

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.87
records.statement:
Is every fibered link in $S^{3}$ realized as the link of an isolated
singular point of a polynomial map $\mathbb{R}^{4} \to \mathbb{R}^{2}$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.88
records.statement:
Are there infinitely many congruence arithmetic links in the
3-sphere?

records.name: Kirby Problem 1.89
records.statement:
(a) Fix a long link L. What is the homotopy type of the embedding space of
links isotopic to L?
(b) Fix a link L in a 3-manifold M. What is the homotopy type of the embed-
ding space of links in M isotopic to L?

(c) Given a link $L$ obtained by infecting a link $L_{1}$ by another link $L_{2}$, describe
the homotopy type of component of $L$ in the space of links in terms of the
components of $L_{1}$ and $L_{2}$.

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.1
records.statement:
(Ivanov conjecture). Let $S$ be an orientable surface of finite type
with genus at least three. If $G \leq \operatorname{Mod}(S)$ is a subgroup of finite index, does $G$ have
finite abelianization?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.2
records.statement:
(Congruence subgroup problem). Does every finite-index sub-
group of the mapping class group of $S$ contain a congruence subgroup?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.3
records.statement: Is the mapping class group of a surface of finite type linear?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.4
records.statement:
Let $S_{1}$ and $S_{2}$ be orientable surfaces of finite type. Under what
conditions do injective maps from (finite-index subgroups of) the mapping class
group of $S_{1}$ to the mapping class group of $S_{2}$ necessarily arise from “manipulations”
(e.g., inclusions, (branched) coverings, etc.) taking $S_{1}$ to $S_{2}$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.5
records.statement:
For $g \geq 3$, determine a finite presentation for the Torelli
group $\mathcal{I}_{g}$, or show that no finite presentation exists.

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.6
records.statement:
Give a classification or enumeration of the finite-index sub-
groups of $\operatorname{Mod}(S_{g})$ that are generated by Dehn twists, Dehn multitwists, or powers
thereof. Which of these subgroups are “geometrically meaningful”, in the sense that
they are given as the stabilizers of some kind of geometric or topological struc-
ture on the surface? Conversely, when is a geometrically meaningful subgroup (not
necessarily of finite index) generated by powers of Dehn multitwists?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.7
records.statement:
Classify the homomorphisms from the braid group $B_{n}$ on $n$
strands to the braid group $B_{m}$ on $m$ strands, where $n, m \in \mathbb{N}$ are arbitrary.

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.8
records.statement:
Fix distinct trivial tangles $\tau_{1}, \tau_{2}$ for which $\tau_{1} \cup\tau_{2}$ is the unknot.
Describe the intersection of the associated wicket groups $W_{n}(\tau_{1}) \cap W_{n}(\tau_{2}) \leq B_{2n}$.
Is this group finitely generated? Finitely presented?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.9
records.statement:
Is there a nice presentation of the $n$-stranded braid group whose
generating set is the set of all positive elementary braid half-twists?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.10
records.statement:
(a) Is there an efficient algorithm to compute distances in the curve complex
of a surface? The input to the algorithm should be the surface and the
curves. One may ask similar questions for related complexes, such as the
arc complex of a surface with boundary.
(b) Is there an algorithm (efficient or otherwise) to compute the distance be-
tween quasi-convex subsets of the curve complex? This question is partic-
ularly interesting in the case where the quasi-convex subsets are the disk
sets of handlebodies.

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.11
records.statement:
Find precise estimates for both the extremal and average behav-
ior of the simple lifting degree of curves, in terms of combinatorial (e.g., intersection
number) and/or geometric (e.g., geodesic length, word length) data.

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.12
records.statement:
(a) What is the maximum number of systoles on a closed, hyperbolic surface
of genus $g$?
(b) What is the maximum cardinality of a set of pairwise non-isotopic, essen-
tial, simple closed curves on a closed surface of genus $g$ with the property
that no two curves in the set intersect in more than one point?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.13
records.statement:
Let $S$ be a surface, and let $\Gamma_{1}, \Gamma_{2}$ be isotopy classes of embedded
graphs in $S$. Determine when $\Gamma_{1}$ and $\Gamma_{2}$ are related by a sequence of surgeries.

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.14
records.statement:
(a) Does every Jordan curve in the Euclidean plane contain the vertices of a
square?
(b) Does every Jordan curve in the Euclidean plane contain the vertices of the
affine image of a regular hexagon?
(c) Let $\gamma \subset \mathbb{C}$ be a smooth Jordan curve, and let $S \subset \mathbb{C}$ consist of $2n \geq 4$
concyclic points. Does there exist a non-constant polynomial $p(z) \in \mathbb{C}[z]$
of degree $< n$ such that $p(S) \subset \gamma$?
(d) Suppose that $h$ is a continuous, real-valued function defined on the unit
sphere $S^{2} \subset \mathbb{R}^{3}$ and that points $x_{1},..., x_{4} \in S^{2}$ form the vertices of
a square.
Is there an isometry $\rho \in \operatorname{SO}(3)$ such that $h$ is constant on
$\rho(x_{1}),..., \rho(x_{4})$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.15
records.statement:
Is the genus $g$ Goeritz group $\mathcal{G}_{g}$ finitely generated when $g \geq 4$?
If so, find a set of generators.

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.16
records.statement:
If two hyperbolic surfaces have the same unmarked simple
length spectra (i.e., the same multiset of lengths that correspond to simple closed
curves), are they isometric?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.17
records.statement:
Suppose that $c$ is a geodesic current on a hyperbolic surface,
and suppose that, on the space of hyperbolic metrics on the surface, $c$ has the same
length function as a closed geodesic.
Must $c$ be a convex combination of closed
curves?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.18
records.statement:
What is the best lower bound on the volume of a fibered hyper-
bolic 3-manifold one can give in terms of the translation length of the monodromy
with respect to various metric spaces, such as Teichmüller space with the Weil–
Peterson metric or the pants complex?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.19
records.statement:
Which mapping classes give rise to arithmetic hyperbolic 3-
manifolds as their mapping tori?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.20
records.statement:
Can one detect holomorphicity from a monodromy factoriza-
tion of a Lefschetz pencil, fibration, or a surface bundle over a surface? What are
the special properties of monodromy factorizations of holomorphic fibrations?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.21
records.statement:
What is the minimum number, $m_{g,b}$, of right-handed Dehn
twists along essential curves into which the boundary multi-twist, $\Delta:= T_{\delta_{1}} \cdots T_{\delta_{b}}$,
can be factorized in $\operatorname{Mod}(S_{g}^{b})$? Find factorizations realizing the minimum.

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.22
records.statement:
Does every Lefschetz fibration over the 2–sphere admit a sec-
tion?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.23
records.statement:
Does there exist a surface bundle over a surface that admits
a complete hyperbolic metric, or, more generally, a complete metric of variable
negative curvature?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.24
records.statement:
Does there exist a complex surface $X$ that admits three or more
non-isomorphic structures as a surface bundle over a surface?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.25
records.statement:
Consider surface bundles over surfaces where both fiber $F$ and
base $B$ have genus $\geq 2$ and where $\pi_{1}(B)$ injects in the mapping class group of the

fiber. Does such a bundle have a $k$–multisection for some $k > 0$ (i.e., a continuous
choice of $k$ everywhere distinct points)?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.26
records.statement:
(Kontsevich–Zorich conjecture). Understand the homotopy types
of strata of abelian differentials. Which stratum-components are $K(\pi, 1)$ spaces?
What are the fundamental groups? For which stratum-components $\mathcal{H}$ is some ver-
sion of the monodromy map $\rho: \pi_{1}(\mathcal{H}) \to \operatorname{Mod}(S_{g})$ injective? Do the answers to
these questions change in a predictable way as one moves from the principal stra-
tum down to the minimal?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.27
records.statement:
For $n \geq 4$, does the braid group $B_{n}$ admit a finite-index sub-
group that embeds in a right-angled Artin group?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.28
records.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a graph that is not a nontrivial join, and let $A(\Gamma)$
be the associated right-angled Artin group. Does there exist an injective map from
$A(\Gamma)$ to the mapping class group of a surface such that every loxodromic element
of $A(\Gamma)$ is sent to a pseudo-Anosov mapping class?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.29
records.statement:
Determine the Artin groups that can be embedded into a map-
ping class group.

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.30
records.statement:
Which right-angled Artin groups contain closed hyperbolic sur-
face groups? Is there an algorithmic or graph-theoretic criterion to decide this?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.31
records.statement:
Let $S$ be a closed surface of genus at least 2. Show that the
stable commutator length is rational on the commutator subgroup of $\pi_{1}(S)$.

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.32
records.statement:
Does every surface bundle over a surface admit a flat connec-
tion? What about surface bundles over 3-manifolds?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.33
records.statement:
Let $S$ be a closed compact surface (without boundary).
Is
there a finitely generated, torsion-free group $G$ such that $G$ cannot act faithfully by
homeomorphisms on $S$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.34
records.statement:
Let $S$ be a compact surface. For $0 \leq r < s$, does there exist a
nontrivial finitely generated subgroup $G_{r} \leq \operatorname{Diff}^{r}_{0}(S)$ such that every action of $G_{r}$
on $S$ by $C^{s}$ diffeomorphisms is trivial? Can these examples be torsion-free?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.35
records.statement:
Is the first-order theory of the mapping class group of a surface
decidable?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.36
records.statement:
Are systems of equations over mapping class groups and braid
groups decidable?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.37
records.statement:
Give a Nielsen–Thurston-type classification for the mapping
class groups of infinite-type surfaces. In particular, which homeomorphisms are the
appropriate generalization of pseudo-Anosov homeomorphisms in this setting?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.38
records.statement:
Give an appropriate analogue of the curve graph for infinite-
type surfaces, and characterize the surfaces for which no such graph exists.

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.39
records.statement:
(a) Does the mapping class group of an infinite-genus surface with no planar
ends contain every countable group?
(b) Does the mapping class group of the one-ended infinite-genus surface have
any proper finite-index subgroups?
(c) For an infinite-type surface, describe and characterize the subgroup of
mapping classes with quasi-conformal representatives. In particular, when
is it a normal subgroup of the mapping class group?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.40
records.statement:
(a) Let $S$ be an infinite-type surface and $\varphi$ a mapping class for which there is
a (marked) conformal structure $\Sigma$ on $S$ with respect to which $\varphi$ is realized
as a quasi-conformal homeomorphism.
Then for each quasi-conformal
structure in the connected component of Teichmüller space containing $\Sigma$,
there is a quasiconformal homeomorphism representing $\varphi$ which minimizes
the dilatation. If the infimum of the minimal dilatations for each structure
in this component is achieved and is greater than 1, is the minimizing
quasiconformal homeomorphism unique? What is the structure of such a
minimizer?
(b) If $\varphi$ is parabolic (see Remark (1) below) for $T$, must a sequence of con-
formal structures with dilatation converging to the infimum degenerate by
pinching along some sequence of essential simple closed curves? Is this
system unique? Can it depend on the component $T$?
(c) If $\varphi$ fixes more than one component $T, T'$ of $\operatorname{Teich}(S)$, can the type be dif-
ferent for $T$ and $T'$? In particular, can $\varphi$ be parabolic for $T$ and hyperbolic
for $T'$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.41
records.statement:
Give a finite list of practically computable invariants of the
mapping class group or pure mapping class group of an infinite-type surface $S$ that
determine the topology of $S$.

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.42
records.statement:
Is the geodesic flow in almost every direction on the Chamanara
surface ergodic? What about on the translation surface considered by Bruin and
Lukina, which is similar to the Chamanara surface?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.43
records.statement:
Let $X$ be a compact, totally disconnected subset of $\mathbb{R}^{2}$ with
$|X| \geq 2$, and let $\Gamma_{X}$ denote the mapping class group of $\mathbb{R}^{2} - X$.
(a) For $Y \subset X$, let $\Gamma_{X,Y}$ be the subgroup of $\Gamma_{X}$ permuting $Y$ . Classify in-
variants $q$ that are functorial.
(b) If $X \subset \mathbb{R}^{2}$ is totally disconnected and $\alpha$ is a homeomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^{2}$ fixing
$X$ as a set, let $C_{\alpha}(X)$ denote the space of $\alpha$-invariant closed subsets of

$X$, in the Hausdorff topology. Let $q$ be functorial as in part (a). Classify
those $q$ that are continuous or semi-continuous.
(c) What is the relationship between the translation length $\tau_{X}$ and topological
entropy? More precisely, is there a positive constant $C$ so that if $\alpha$ is a
homeomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^{2}$ permuting $X$ and $g$ is the class of $\alpha$ in $\Gamma_{X}$, then
the (topological) entropy of $\alpha$ is at least as big as $C \cdot \tau_{X}(g)$?
(d) Suppose $X$ is a Cantor set in the plane, and let $P\Gamma_{X}$ denote the ‘pure’
subgroup of $\Gamma_{X}$ fixing $X$ pointwise. Let $N$ be a subgroup of $P\Gamma_{X}$ that is
normal in $\Gamma_{X}$, and for each integer $n$, let $N_{n}$ be the subgroup of $P\Gamma_{n}$ that
is the image of $N$ restricted to any $n$-element subset of $X$. What possible
sequences of subgroups $N_{n}$ can arise in this way?
(e) For which $g \in \Gamma_{X}$ is there an embedding $X \to \mathbb{R}^{2}$ for which $g$ is represented
by a diffeomorphism $\alpha$ which is $C^{\infty}$? Or $C^{k}$ for fixed $k$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.44
records.statement:
Given an infinite-type surface $S$, which homeomorphisms $f: S \to$
$S$ give rise to mapping tori $M_{f}$ that admit a hyperbolic structure? For those which
do admit a hyperbolic metric, is $M_{f}$ homeomorphic to the interior of a compact
hyperbolic manifold with totally geodesic boundary?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.45
records.statement:
Compute the end-periodic cobordism group $\Delta^{e}_{2}$ of end-periodic
automorphisms (diffeomorphisms or homeomorphisms) of surfaces.

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.46
records.statement:
(a) Which coarsely boundedly generated mapping class groups of infinite-type
surfaces are hyperbolic?
(b) Consider the class of surfaces with $n \geq 2$ ends, all accumulated by genus.
Are the mapping class groups of these surfaces quasi-isometric for different
values of $n$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.47
records.statement:
(a) Given a mapping class $\psi$ of a based surface $S$, there is an induced endo-
morphism of the symmetric product $\operatorname{Sym}^{i}(S)$ and hence an endofunctor
$\psi_{*}$ of the partially wrapped Fukaya category $\mathcal{F}(S)$ as constructed, say, by
Auroux [Aur10]. Compute the categorical entropy of $\psi_{*}$, in the sense
of [DHKK14], for $\psi$ pseudo-Anosov.
(b) Given a fibered knot $K$ with pseudo-Anosov monodromy, what is

$$
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\left(\dim \widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(\Sigma^{n}(K),\widetilde{K};i)\right)^{1/n},
$$

where $\widetilde{K}$ is the branch locus in the $n$-fold cyclic branched cover $\Sigma^{n}(K)$,
and $i$ denotes the Alexander grading (in $\mathbb{Z}$) with respect to the fiber surface.
Here, $\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}$ denotes the knot Floer homology of $K$ [OS04c, Ras03].
(c) With notation as in the previous question, what is

$$
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\left(\dim \widehat{\mathrm{HF}}(\Sigma^{n}(K))\right)^{1/n}
$$

for the Heegaard Floer invariant $\widehat{\mathrm{HF}}$ [OS04e] of the closed 3-manifold
$\Sigma^{n}(K)$?
(d) Given a closed surface $S$ and a pseudo-Anosov automorphism $\psi$, let $M_{\psi}$
denote the mapping torus of $\psi$, and $\widehat{\mathrm{HF}}(M_{\psi};i)$ the summand of
$\widehat{\mathrm{HF}}(M_{\psi})$
spanned by the spin $^{c}$-structures $\mathfrak{s}$ with $\langle c_{1}(\mathfrak{s}), [F]\rangle = i$. What is

$$
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\left(\dim \widehat{\mathrm{HF}}(M_{\psi^{n}},i)\right)^{1/n}?
$$

What about

$$
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\left(\dim_{\mathbb{F}_{2}}\mathrm{HF}^{+}(M_{\psi^{n}},i)\right)^{1/n}
$$

for $i \neq 0$ (or for twisted $\mathrm{HF}^{+}$ for $i = 0$)?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.48
records.statement:
The mapping class group of a closed, orientable, genus $g$ sur-
face $S$ acts by symplectomorphisms on the symmetric product $\operatorname{Sym}^{g}(S)$. In partic-
ular, it acts smoothly on $\operatorname{Sym}^{g}(S)$.
(a) What is the kernel of the map from the mapping class group of $S$ to the
smooth mapping class group of $\operatorname{Sym}^{g}(S)$? What about in the based case?
(b) Given disjoint simple closed curves $\alpha_{1},..., \alpha_{g}$ in $S$, there is a correspond-
ing torus $T_{\alpha}$ in $\operatorname{Sym}^{g}(S)$: the image of $\alpha_{1} \times \cdots \times \alpha_{g} \subset S^{g}$. These are
the tori that appear in Heegaard Floer theory. When do $\alpha_{1},..., \alpha_{g}$ and
$\beta_{1},..., \beta_{g}$ give smoothly isotopic tori? When are they Lagrangian isotopic
for an appropriate choice of symplectic form?

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.49
records.statement:
(AMU conjecture). Let $S$ be a surface with negative Euler char-
acteristic. If $\varphi \in \operatorname{Mod}(S)$ acts by a pseudo-Anosov on some subsurface (including
$S$ itself), show that there exists $p_{0}(\varphi)$ such that the Witten–Reshetikhin–Turaev
representation $\rho_{p}(\varphi)$ has infinite order for $p \geq p_{0}(\varphi)$.

records.name: Kirby Problem 2.50
records.statement:
(Volume conjecture for surface diffeomorphisms). Let $S$ be a
closed oriented surface, let $q=e^{2\pi i/n}$ be a root of unity, and let $\mathcal{K}^{q}(S)$ be the Kauff-
man bracket skein algebra. Let $\phi: S \to S$ be a pseudo-Anosov diffeomorphism with
mapping torus $M_{\phi}$, and let $r: \pi_{1}(S) \to \operatorname{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{C})$ be a smooth point in the charac-
ter variety that is $\phi$-invariant. Finally, let $L$ be the intertwiner realizing an iso-
morphism between the representations of $\mathcal{K}^{q}(S)$ corresponding to $[r]$ and $[r \circ \varphi_{*}]$,
normalized so that $\det(L) = 1$. Show that

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\log|\operatorname{Trace} L|=\frac{1}{4\pi}\operatorname{vol}_{\mathrm{hyp}} M_{\phi}.
$$

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.1
records.statement:
Classify the smallest volume hyperbolic 3-manifolds of various types. In particular:

(a) Determine the nonorientable closed hyperbolic 3-manifolds of least volume.

(b) Determine the n-cusped hyperbolic 3-manifolds of least volume for each $n\geq 3$.

(c) Determine the smallest volume hyperbolic 3-manifolds with n orientable cusps for each n.

(d) Determine the n-cusped orientable hyperbolic 3-manifolds of least volume for each n.

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.2
records.statement: Show that the volumes of hyperbolic 3-manifolds are not all rationally related.

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.3
records.statement: Does every cusped hyperbolic 3-manifold have a geometric ideal triangulation?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.4
records.statement:
(Chen--Yang Volume Conjecture). (a) Prove that, for any hyperbolic 3-manifold $M$,

$$
\lim_{\substack{r\to\infty\\ r\ \mathrm{odd}}}\frac{1}{r}\log\bigl(TV(M;e^{2\pi i/r})\bigr)
=\frac{1}{2\pi}\operatorname{Vol}(M).
$$

(b) Prove that, for any closed, oriented, hyperbolic 3-manifold $M$,

$$
\lim_{\substack{r\to\infty\\ r\ \mathrm{odd}}}\frac{1}{r}\log\bigl(WRT(M;e^{2\pi i/r})\bigr)
=\frac{1}{4\pi}\bigl(\operatorname{Vol}(M)-i\operatorname{CS}(M)\bigr).
$$

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.5
records.statement:
(a) Do there exist closed non-Haken hyperbolic 3-manifolds with arbitrarily large injectivity radius?

(b) Does there exist a cofinal tower of regular covers of closed hyperbolic 3-manifolds where all of the manifolds in the tower are non-Haken?

(c) Is there a tower of hyperbolic rational homology spheres for which all fundamental groups are not left-orderable, the manifolds contain no coorientable taut foliations, or the manifolds are L-spaces? (The three properties listed are connected via the L-space conjecture. See Problem 3.48)

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.6
records.statement:
Given a cofinal tower of covers M $\leftarrow$ $M_1$ $\leftarrow$ $M_2$ $\leftarrow$ $\cdots$, is it true that the torsion subgroups $\operatorname{Tor}(M_{n})$ of $H_1(M_{n}, \mathbb{Z})$ and the hyperbolic volumes $\operatorname{vol}(M_{n})$ satisfy

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log|\operatorname{Tor}(M_n)|}{\operatorname{vol}(M_n)}=\frac{1}{6\pi}\,?
$$

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.7
records.statement: Does every finite-volume hyperbolic 3-manifold admit a finitesheeted cover fibering over the circle with orientable pseudo-Anosov monodromy?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.8
records.statement: If $M_1$ and $M_2$ are finite-volume hyperbolic 3-manifolds whose fundamental groups have isomorphic profinite completions, must $M_1$ and $M_2$ be isometric?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.9
records.statement: Is being Haken a profinite invariant amongst 3-manifolds? That is, if $M_1$ and $M_2$ are 3-manifolds so that $\pi_1(M_{1})$ and $\pi_1(M_{2})$ have isomorphic profinite completions, and $M_1$ is Haken, must $M_2$ also be Haken?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.10
records.statement:
(a) Are there infinitely many commensurability classes of arithmetic rational homology 3-spheres?

(b) Are there infinitely many arithmetic integral homology 3-spheres?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.11
records.statement: Does every hyperbolic knot in the 3-sphere have meridian length at most 4?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.12
records.statement:
(a) Considering all closed, orientable, $\pi_1$-injective surfaces (possibly non-embedded) in all closed hyperbolic 3-manifolds, what is the infimum of the areas of all these surfaces?

(b) One can ask the same question, but considering just closed, orientable, $\pi_1$-injective surfaces of a fixed genus g.

(c) One can also consider only closed, orientable, embedded $\pi_1$-injective surfaces.

(d) Alternatively, one can consider all closed, orientable, essential surfaces in all hyperbolic 3-manifolds M, allowing M not to be closed.

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.13
records.statement: Does every closed hyperbolic 3-manifold admit an immersed $\pi_1$-injective surface with only double points? More precisely, if M is a closed, connected, hyperbolic 3-manifold, is there a closed, connected surface $\Sigma$ (other than a 2-sphere) and an immersion f : $\Sigma$ $\to$ M such that $f_*$ : $\pi_1(\Sigma)$ $\to$ $\pi_1(M)$ is injective and $|f^{-1}(\{x\})|\leq 2$ for all $x\in M$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.14
records.statement: Can a hyperbolic knot complement in the 3-sphere contain a closed, embedded totally geodesic surface?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.15
records.statement:
Let $M$ be a closed hyperbolic 3-manifold with positive first Betti number.

(a) Which elements of $H^{2}(M;\mathbb{R})$ are realized as the Euler classes of taut foliations?

(b) Which elements of $H^{2}(M;\mathbb{R})$ are realized as the Euler classes of tight contact structures?

(c) How about universally tight contact structures?

(d) The question can also be asked for pseudo-Anosov flows...

(e)... and for quasi-geodesic flows. (f ) How about Euler classes of representations into $\operatorname{Homeo}^{+}(S^1)$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.16
records.statement: Does every finite-volume hyperbolic 3-manifold contain infinitely many simple closed geodesics?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.17
records.statement: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be finite-volume hyperbolic n--manifolds. If the length spectra of $M_1$ and $M_2$ coincide, must the two manifolds be commensurable?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.18
records.statement: Is there a closed hyperbolic 3-manifold that is foliated with minimal leaves?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.19
records.statement:
(a) Does every closed hyperbolic 3-manifold have a nowhere zero vector field whose lift to the universal cover has proper flow lines?

(b) Can one ensure that the leaf space of the foliation by flow lines in the universal cover is Hausdorff ?

(c) If so, the leaf space in the universal cover is homeomorphic to a plane and one can then ask: can the induced action of $\pi_1(M)$ on a plane be compactified to an action on the closed disk?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.20
records.statement: Let $M$ be a closed hyperbolic 3-manifold with a faithful homomorphism $\rho:\pi_1(M)\to \operatorname{Homeo}^{+}(\mathbb{R})$. Prove that $M$ supports a dual transversely orientable, essential lamination $\lambda$.

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.21
records.statement:
In this problem, all 3-manifolds are orientable, while all flows are considered up to orbit equivalence and are assumed to be transitive.

(a) Are there only finitely many Anosov flows on a given closed 3-manifold?

(b) Are there only finitely many pseudo-Anosov flows on a given closed 3-manifold?

(c) Are there only finitely many quasigeodesic pseudo-Anosov flows on a given closed 3-manifold?

(d) Are there only finitely many pseudo-Anosov flows without perfect fits on a given closed 3-manifold?

(e) Are there only finitely many veering triangulations on a given finite volume cusped hyperbolic 3-manifold?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.22
records.statement: Let $G=\pi_1(M)$ be the fundamental group of a finite-volume hyperbolic 3-manifold $M$. What is the regularity of the smoothest (virtual) action of $G$ on $S^1$? On the interval?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.23
records.statement: What is the Margulis constant in dimension 3? Is it realized uniquely by the Weeks manifold W, where $\mu(W)$ = 0.77442...?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.24
records.statement:
(a) (Cannon Conjecture) If G is a finitely presented, Gromov hyperbolic group with space at infinity equal to the 2-sphere, must G be a cocompact Kleinian group?

(b) More generally, if $G$ is a Gromov hyperbolic group whose boundary is planar, is G virtually a convex cocompact Kleinian group?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.25
records.statement:
(Bending Conjecture). (a) Is a quasi-Fuchsian group determined by the hyperbolic metric on the boundary of its convex core?

(b) Is a quasi-Fuchsian group with parabolics, other than a Fuchsian group, determined by the bending measure on the boundary of its convex core?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.26
records.statement: Let $M$ be a finite-volume hyperbolic 3-manifold, and let $M^1$ be a minimal-index finite cover of $M$ such that $\pi_1(M^1)$ embeds in a right-angled Artin group. Can one obtain good control over the complexity of the smallest right-angled Artin group containing $\pi_1(M^1)$ from the data of $M$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.27
records.statement:
(a) What is the computational complexity of the homeomorphism problem for compact, orientable 3-manifolds?

(b) Is there a polynomial-time algorithm to recognize the 3-sphere?

(c) What is the computational complexity of the recognition problem for other 3-manifolds?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.28
records.statement: How many Pachner moves are needed to pass between two triangulations of a compact 3-manifold?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.29
records.statement:
(a) Given a closed hyperbolic 3-manifold $M$, can one find an explicit bound on the degree of a finite cover $\widetilde M$ having $b_1(\widetilde M)>0$?

(b) For example, is there such a finite cover with degree at most a polynomial function of the number of tetrahedra in some triangulation of $M$?

(c) Similarly, can one find an explicit upper bound on the degree of a finite cover $\widetilde M_1$ that fibers over the circle?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.30
records.statement:
(a) What is the computational complexity of determining whether a compact 3-manifold admits a hyperbolic structure?

(b) If a compact 3-manifold does admit a hyperbolic structure, what is the computational complexity of finding it?

(c) In particular, do these problems lie in the complexity classes NP and FNP respectively?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.31
records.statement:
Suppose M is a closed 3-manifold.

(a) Can one decide if the fundamental group of M is left-orderable?

(b) What is the complexity of a certificate of left-orderability, or of non-left-orderability?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.32
records.statement: Is there an algorithm to determine whether two closed, embedded surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^3$ are isotopic?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.33
records.statement: Let M and N be closed orientable 3-manifolds. Prove that if there is a degree-1 map $f:M\to N$ then $g(M)\geq g(N)$, where $g(M)$ is the Heegaard genus of $M$.

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.34
records.statement: Do any two genus-g Heegaard splittings of a closed, orientable 3-manifold M become equivalent after at most g stabilizations?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.35
records.statement:
Given a compact manifold M, let $r(M)$ denote the rank of its fundamental group and $g(M)$ denote its Heegaard genus.

(a) Does every closed orientable hyperbolic 3-manifold M with $r(M)$ = 2 satisfy $g(M)$ = 2?

(b) Is there a non-Haken manifold $M$ such that $r(M)<g(M)$?

(c) Is there a constant $k>0$ such that $g(M)\leq k r(M)$ for every closed orientable 3-manifold $M$?

(d) If $\{M_i\}$ is the set of congruence covers of an arithmetic hyperbolic 3-manifold M, is the infimum of $r(M_i)/\operatorname{vol}(M_i)$ zero or positive?

(e) Is there a knot $K\subset S^3$ such that $r(S^3\setminus\nu(K))<g(S^3\setminus\nu(K))$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.36
records.statement: (Simple loop conjecture) Let f : F $\to$ M be a 2-sided immersion of a surface into a 3-manifold such that $f_*$ : $\pi_1(F)$ $\to$ $\pi_1(M)$ is not injective. Must some simple closed curve lie in the kernel of $f_*$ ?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.37
records.statement:
(a) Is every finitely generated 3-manifold group linear (over some field with characteristic zero)?

(b) If so, can one bound the dimension of a faithful linear representation?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.38
records.statement: Is every PD$_3$-group the fundamental group of a closed, aspherical 3-manifold?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.39
records.statement:
(a) Is every finitely generated perfect group the normal closure of a single element?

(b) Is there an integral homology sphere whose fundamental group has weight bigger than one?

(c) For any $n$, is there an integral homology sphere whose fundamental group has weight bigger than $n$?

(d) Specifically, are the weights of the fundamental groups of Seifert fibered homology spheres $\Sigma(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ unbounded?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.40
records.statement: Does every closed, orientable, hyperbolic 3-manifold admit a tight contact structure?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.41
records.statement: Is it true that for every knot $K\subset S^3$, there is an integer $n_K$ such that $S^3_r(K)$ admits a tight contact structure for all $r\geq n_K$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.42
records.statement: Does every tight contact 3-manifold have finite Giroux torsion?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.43
records.statement:
Understand how various properties of contact structures behave under different kinds of symplectic cobordism. For instance:

(a) Is tightness preserved under exact symplectic cobordism?

(b) Is weak fillability preserved under weak symplectic cobordism?

(c) How do the support genus and Giroux torsion behave under Legendrian surgery?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.44
records.statement: Is there an algorithm to decide, given an open book, whether the corresponding contact 3-manifold is tight or fillable?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.45
records.statement:
(a) Are there contact 3-manifolds with support genus greater than one?

(b) Are there contact 3-manifolds with arbitrarily large support genus?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.46
records.statement: Let $\lambda$ be a contact form on a closed 3-manifold that is not a lens space. Must the associated Reeb flow have infinitely many simple periodic orbits?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.47
records.statement:
(a) Does every Reeb flow on $S^3$, associated to a contact form giving the standard contact structure, have an elliptic periodic orbit?

(b) What about if one restricts to Reeb flows on $S^3$ arising from boundaries of strictly convex domains in $\mathbb{R}^4$ ?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.48
records.statement:
(L-space Conjecture). For prime rational homology 3-spheres Y, are the following equivalent?

(a) $\pi_1(Y)$ is left-orderable.

(b) Y is not an L-space.

(c) Y admits a coorientable taut foliation.

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.49
records.statement: Are any of the three conditions in the L-space Conjecture equivalent, for all prime rational homology 3-spheres Y, to the condition that Y admits a contact structure that is filled by a symplectic 4-manifold with $b_2^+>0$.

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.50
records.statement: (The Floer Poincaré Conjecture). If Y is an integral homology sphere that is an L-space, show that Y is $S^3$ or the connected sum of some copies of the Poincaré sphere (with arbitrary orientations).

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.51
records.statement:
Suppose Y is a rational homology 3-sphere such that every homomorphism $\pi_1(Y)$ $\to$ $\operatorname{SU}(2)$ has abelian image. Does it follow that

$$
\dim_{\mathbb{C}} I^{\#}(Y;\mathbb{C})=|H_1(Y;\mathbb{Z})|,
$$
 i.e., that Y is an instanton L-space?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.52
records.statement:
(a) Does every closed 3-manifold M besides the 3-sphere admit a nontrivial representation $\pi_1(M)$ $\to$ $\operatorname{SU}(2)$?

(b) For which M with nonabelian fundamental group does every homomorphism $\pi_1(M)$ $\to$ $\operatorname{SU}(2)$ have abelian image?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.53
records.statement: Are all strong L-spaces branched double covers of alternating links in $S^3$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.54
records.statement:
(a) Is there a closed 3-manifold $M$ whose Heegaard Floer homology $\widehat{HF}(M;\mathbb{Z})$ has torsion?

(b) Is there a rational homology 3-sphere $M$ for which $\widehat{HF}(M;\mathbb{Z})$ has torsion?

(c) Is there a knot $K\subset S^3$ whose knot Floer homology $\widehat{HFK}(S^3,K;\mathbb{Z})$ has torsion?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.55
records.statement:
(a) For $K$ a nontrivial knot in $S^3$, does $HFK^-(K)$ always admit an $\mathbb{F}_2$-summand, as an $\mathbb{F}_2[U]$-module?

(b) For $Y$ a rational homology sphere, if $HF_{\mathrm{red}}(Y)$ is nontrivial, does $HF_{\mathrm{red}}(Y)$ always admit an $\mathbb{F}_2$-summand?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.56
records.statement:
(a) For $Y^3$ a rational homology sphere, is the Seiberg--Witten Floer spectrum $SWF(Y)$ always a wedge of spheres?

(b) Is every monopole Floer homology L-space a Seiberg--Witten Floer homotopy L-space?

(c) Find an example of two rational homology spheres with the same monopole Floer homology but with different Seiberg--Witten Floer spectra.

(d) Develop an algorithm for computing Seiberg--Witten Floer spectra.

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.57
records.statement: Construct an $S^1$ - or $\operatorname{Pin}(2)$-equivariant lattice homotopy type that computes the Seiberg--Witten Floer homotopy type.

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.58
records.statement: Prove that there is an isomorphism relating Heegaard Floer homology and monopole Floer homology that commutes with the cobordism maps in the two settings. In particular, prove that the mixed invariant in Heegaard Floer homology is equal to the Seiberg--Witten invariant for closed 4-manifolds.

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.59
records.statement: Prove an isomorphism relating instanton Floer homology and Heegaard Floer homology.

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.60
records.statement: Find an algorithm to compute instanton Floer homology of closed 3-manifolds and the Donaldson invariants of closed 4-manifolds.

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.61
records.statement: Is the dimension of Heegaard Floer homology invariant under genus 2 mutation?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.62
Kirby Problem 3.63
records.statement: Give a method for computing the $\eta$ invariant for the Dirac operator, $\eta_{\mathrm{Dirac}}(Y, s)$, associated to a spin structure s on a hyperbolic 3-manifold Y.

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.64
records.statement:
Let A be a flat connection on the trivial $\operatorname{SU}(2)$ bundle on a closed three-manifold M. The Chern--Simons invariant $\operatorname{CS}(M, A)$ is defined to be

$$
\operatorname{CS}(M,A)=\frac{1}{4\pi^2}\int_M \operatorname{Tr}\!\left(A\wedge dA+\frac{2}{3}A\wedge A\wedge A\right).
$$
 Is $\operatorname{CS}(M, A)$ always rational?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.65
records.statement:
Let $S_{2,\infty}(Y)$ denote the Kauffman bracket skein module of a closed, oriented 3-manifold $Y$; this is a module over $R=\mathbb{Z}[A,A^{-1}]$. For $Y$ prime and connected, does $S_{2,\infty}(Y)$ having rank one, in the sense that

$$
S_{2,\infty}(Y)\otimes_R \mathbb{Q}(A)\cong \mathbb{Q}(A),
$$

imply that $Y$ is $S^3$ or $S^1\times S^2$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.66
records.statement:
Suppose that $Y$ is a closed, oriented 3-manifold, and let $S_{2,\infty}(Y)$ denote the Kauffman bracket skein module over $R=\mathbb{Z}[A,A^{-1}]$ as in Problem 3.65.

(a) Is the dimension

$$
\dim_{\mathbb{Q}(A)} S_{2,\infty}(Y)\otimes_R \mathbb{Q}(A)
$$

equal to the dimension of the degree 0 part of Abouzaid--Manolescu's sheaf-theoretic Floer homology $HP^{\bullet}_{\#}(Y)$ from [AM20]?

(b) When is $S_{2,\infty}(Y)\otimes_R\mathbb{Q}[A,A^{-1}]$ tame, as defined in Problem 3.65?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.67
records.statement: Categorify the Witten--Reshetikhin--Turaev invariants of 3-manifolds.

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.68
records.statement:
(a) Give a mathematical definition of the $\widehat{Z}$ invariants for all 3-manifolds.

(b) Categorify the $\widehat{Z}$ invariants.

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.69
records.statement:
(a) What is the isomorphism type of $\Theta^3_{\mathbb{Z}}$?

(b) Does there exist a torsion element $[Y]$ in $\Theta^3_{\mathbb{Z}}$?

(c) Does there exist a torsion element $[Y]\in\Theta^3_{\mathbb{Z}}$ having Rokhlin invariant $\mu([Y])=1$?

(d) Do there exist infinitely-divisible elements in $\Theta^3_{\mathbb{Z}}$; that is, does there exist a homology 3-sphere $Y$ such that for infinitely many $n\in\mathbb{N}$ there exists $[Z_n]\in\Theta^3_{\mathbb{Z}}$ such that $[Y]=n[Z_n]$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.70
records.statement: Is $\Theta^3_{\mathbb{Z}}$ generated by the classes of knot surgeries $[S^3_{1/n}(K)]$, where $n$ ranges over all integers and $K$ ranges over all knots in $S^3$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.71
records.statement:
Is there a nontrivial element in the kernel of the natural map

$$
\Theta^3_{\mathbb{Z}}\longrightarrow \Theta^3_{\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}};
$$

that is, does there exist an integer homology 3-sphere that does not bound a smooth $\mathbb{Z}$-homology 4-ball but does bound a smooth $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-homology 4-ball?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.72
records.statement:
(a) Does the kernel of the map $\Theta^3_{\mathbb{Z}}\to\Theta^3_{\mathbb{Q}}$ contain a subgroup that is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}^{\infty}$?

(b) If so, does it contain such a subgroup as a summand?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.73
records.statement:
(a) Calculate $\Theta^{\mathrm{TOP}}_{\mathbb{Z}/p}$.

(b) Calculate $\Theta^{\mathrm{TOP}}_{\mathbb{Q}}$.

(c) Is the linking form homomorphism $[\operatorname{lk}]$ injective?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.74
records.statement:
Let $Y$ be a rational homology sphere and $f:Y\to Y$ be a self-diffeomorphism of $Y$. Suppose $W$ is a 4-manifold with boundary $Y$ such that $f$ extends to a self-diffeomorphism of $W$.

(a) What constraints are there on the intersection form of $W$?

(b) Does there exist a pair $(Y,f)$ such that $Y$ bounds a homology ball but $f:Y\to Y$ does not extend over any definite manifold of either sign?

(c) Develop methods for constraining the intersection form of $W$ that apply to indefinite, non-spin $W$.

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.75
records.statement:
Let $Y$ be a rational homology 3-sphere equipped with an action of a cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$. Suppose $W$ is a 4-manifold with boundary $Y$ over which the action of $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ extends smoothly.

(a) What constraints are there on the intersection form of $W$?

(b) Does there exist an integer homology sphere $Y$ bounding a homology ball such that $Y$ admits a cyclic group action that does not extend over any definite manifold of either sign?

(c) Develop methods for constraining the intersection form of $W$ that apply to indefinite, non-spin $W$.

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.76
records.statement: What is the structure of the equivariant homology cobordism groups?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.77
records.statement: Does there exist a hyperbolic rational homology 3-sphere that is the totally geodesic boundary of a compact, orientable hyperbolic 4-manifold?

records.name: Kirby Problem 3.78
records.statement:
(a) Is there a non-semisimple 3-TQFT whose mapping class group representation is faithful or has an element in its kernel?

(b) Define a 4-manifold invariant via non-semsimple categories that can distinguish 4-manifolds that are not distinguished by classical or gauge-theoretic invariants.

(c) Is there is a full 3-TQFT extension of the representations, constructed by Bonahon and Wong, of the Kauffman bracket skein algebra? In particular, do non-semisimple TQFTs recover the Bonahon--Wong representations?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.1
records.statement: (4-dimensional Poincaré conjecture). Is there a unique smooth structure on the 4-sphere?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.2
records.statement: Does every smooth, closed 4-manifold admit an exotic smooth structure? Infinitely many?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.3
records.statement:
Are there exotic smooth structures on the following closed, simply-connected 4–manifolds?

(a) $\#_{k}\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ for any $k \geq$ 1.

(b) $\#_{m}(\mathbb{CP}^{2}\#\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^{2})$ and $\#_{n}(S^{2} \times S^{2})$ for $m \leq$ 8, $n \leq$ 10.

(c) $\#_{p}K3 \#_{q}(S^{2} \times S^{2})$ for any $p \geq$ q+5. If so, what are the smallest k, m and n? The largest p and q?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.4
records.statement: Is there an exotic smooth structure on some product 4-manifold $S^{1} \times Y^{3}$ or $\Sigma_{g} \times \Sigma_{h}$? Do they all admit exotic smooth structures?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.5
records.statement: Does every connected, open 4-manifold admit uncountably many smooth structures?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.6
records.statement: Does every closed, orientable 3-manifold bound an absolutely exotic pair of smooth, orientable 4-manifolds?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.7
records.statement:
(a) If $M_{1},M_{2}are$ two homeomorphic closed, oriented 4-manifolds, is $M_{1}\#S^{2} \times S^{2}$ diffeomorphic to $M_{2}\#S^{2} \times S^{2}$?

(b) Is there a fixedn>0such that $M_{1}\#_{n}S^{2} \times S^{2}$ is diffeomorphic to $M_{2}\#_{n}S^{2} \times S^{2}$ for every pair $M_{1}, M_{2}$ as above?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.8
records.statement: Let X be a closed, simply connected, smooth 4-manifold, and T a smoothly embedded torus in X with $\pi_{1}(X$ −T) =1 and $[T]^{2}$ =0. Let $X_{K}$ be the result of Fintushel–Stern knot surgery on X along a knot K. If $K_{1}$ and $K_{2}$ are two prime knots such that $X_{K,1}$ and $X_{K,2}$ are diffeomorphic, does it follow that $K_{1}$ is either $K_{2}$ or its mirror?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.9
records.statement: Is every Gluck twist in $S^{4}$ standard?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.10
records.statement:
(a) Is every homotopy $B^{4}$ with boundary $S^{3}$ obtained by performing a Gluck twist on some knotted 2-sphere in $B^{4}$?

(b) Suppose a homotopy 4-ball X is obtained by performing a Gluck twist on a knotted 2-sphere in $B^{4}$. Is $X \times I$ necessarily diffeomorphic to $B^{5}$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.11
records.statement:
Let M be a smooth 4-manifold and letf: $S^{2} \to M$ be a smooth embedding with trivial normal bundle. Then let $M_{f}$ denote the result of Gluck twisting on M along f.

(a) Does there exist an orientable M, and an embedding f, such that M and $M_{f}$ are homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic?

(b) Does there exist an orientable M, and smooth, homotopic embeddings f, $g: S^{2} \to M$ with trivial normal bundle such that $M_{f}$ and $M_{g}$ are homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.12
records.statement:
For X a closed simply connected smooth 4-manifold, let $g_{X}: H_{2}(X) \to \mathbb{N}$ denote the genus function, which assigns to every homology class the minimal genus of a smooth embedded surface representing that class.

(a) Suppose $f: X_{1} \to X_{2}$ is a homeomorphism between simply connected, smooth, closed 4-manifolds. Let $f_{*}: H_{2}(X_{1}) \to H_{2}(X_{2})$ be the induced map on homology. If for all x in $H_{2}(X_{1})$ we have $g_{X,1}(x) = g_{X,2}(f_{*}(x))$, is $X_{1}$ diffeomorphic to $X_{2}$?

(b) Suppose $f: X_{1} \to X_{2}$ is a homeomorphism between simply connected smooth compact 4-manifolds with the same boundary $\partial X_{1} = \partial X_{2}$, such thatf is the identity on the boundary. $Letf_{*}: H_{2}(X_{1},\partial X_{1}) \to H_{2}(X_{2},\partial X_{2})$ be the induced map on relative homology. If for all knots K and for all x in $H_{2}(X_{1},\partial X_{1})$ we have $g_{X,1,K}(x) =g_{X,2,K}(f_{*}(x))$, is $X_{1}$ diffeomorphic to $X_{2}$ rel. boundary?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.13
records.statement:
(a) Does every large $\mathbb{R}^{4}-homeomorph$ lie $in\mathcal{R}_{K}$ for some Kthat is not smoothly slice?

(b) Does there exist an infinite sequence of knots ${K_{i}}$ such that $\mathcal{R}_{K,i} \ne \mathcal{R}_{K,j}$ whenever $i \ne j$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.14
records.statement: Is there a universal cork? More precisely, does there exist some cork (C, f) such that given any pair W and $W^{1}$ of closed, simply connected 4-manifolds that are homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic, there exists a smooth embedding $C \hookrightarrow W$ such that (W $\setminus$ Int C) $\cup _{f} C$ is diffeomorphic to $W^{1}$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.15
records.statement: (11/8 Conjecture). Does every smooth, spin, closed 4-manifold X satisfy $b_{2}(X) \geq 11|\sigma(X)|$, where $\sigma(X)$ is the signature of the intersection form?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.16
records.statement:
(a) Do there exist closed, oriented, smooth, irreducible 4-manifolds with $b^{+}_{2} >$ 1 and $c^{2}_{1}:=2\chi+3\sigma<0$?

(b) Is there an irreducible exotic smooth structure on $\mathbb{CP}^{2}\#_{n}\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ for n>9?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.17
records.statement: Is there an irreducible, closed, simply connected, oriented 4– manifold with $b^{+}_{2}$ and $b^{-}_{2}$ both even?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.18
records.statement:
(a) Does there exist a pair of smooth, closed 4-manifolds that are homotopy equivalent but not simple homotopy equivalent?

(b) Does there exist a pair of smoothlyh-cobordant, smooth, closed 4-manifolds that are not smoothly s-cobordant?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.19
records.statement:
What are the possible Euler characteristics of closed, aspherical 4-manifolds? More specifically, we ask the following.

(a) Is it always the case that $\chi \geq |\sigma|$?

(b) What is the smallest Euler characteristic of a closed hyperbolic 4-manifold?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.20
records.statement: Is $*\mathbb{RP}^{4}\#*\mathbb{RP}^{4}$ smoothable? Is *En\#*En smoothable?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.21
records.statement: Is every topological closed 4–manifold M the union of submanifolds $Y \cup Z$, where Y is smoothable, Z is acyclic, and $Y \cap Z$ is their common boundary, a homology sphere $\Sigma$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.22
records.statement: Let $\pi$ be a good group, and let X be a smooth 4-manifold with $\pi_{1}(X) = \pi$. Does $L^{s}_{5}(\mathbb{Z}[\pi])$ act on the smooth structure set of X, in such a way that the action reduces under the forgetful map to the Wall realization action on the topological structure set? In particular, can this be done when $\pi= \mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}_{n}$, or $\mathbb{Z}_{2}*\mathbb{Z}_{2}$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.23
records.statement: (Schoenflies problem). If $\Sigma$ is a smoothly embedded $S^{3}$ in $S^{4}$, then its closed complements are smooth 4-balls.

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.24
records.statement: Let K be a framed knot in $S^{3} = \partial B^{4}$. Let U be a meridian of K. Does there exist a smoothly embedded disk D in $B^{4} \cup _{\nu K} h^{2}$ bounded by U that intersects the cocore of $h^{2}$ algebraically zero times, such that the 4-manifold obtained by removing an open tubular neighborhood of the disk is not diffeomorphic to the 4-ball?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.25
records.statement: Under what conditions does a closed, orientable 3-manifold M smoothly embed in $S^{4}$? Is this question algorithmically decidable?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.26
records.statement: If Y is a homology three-sphere, does the punctured manifold $Y_{0}$ =Y $\setminus \operatorname{Int}(B^{3})$ smoothly embed in $S^{4}$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.27
records.statement: Find exotic 3-balls in $S^{4}$, considered up to isotopy rel. boundary. That is, find a pair of 3-balls $B_{1}, B_{2}$ smoothly embedded in $S^{4}$ with the same boundary such that $B_{1}, B_{2}$ are topologically but not smoothly isotopic rel. boundary.

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.28
records.statement:
Every closed, orientable 3-manifold embeds smoothly in some connected sum of copies of $S^{2} \times S^{2}$. Given a closed 3-manifold M, let $s(M) \geq$ 0 denote the smallest integer such that M embeds smoothly (respectively locally flatly) in a connected sum of $s(M)$ copies of $S^{2} \times S^{2}$. Let $s(M) \geq$ 0 denote the smallest integer such that M embeds smoothly (respectively locally $flatly^{~})$ in a connected sum of $s_{~}(M)$ copies of $S^{2} \times _{~}S^{2}$. Compute the functions $s(M)$ and $s_{~}(M)$, in either the smooth or locally flat case, for interesting classes of 3-manifolds. Here are three more specific questions.

(a) What are the $functionssands_{~}for$ lens spaces, and for Brieskorn spheres?

(b) Freedman [Fre82] proved that every $\mathbb{Z}-homology$ sphere embeds topologically in $S^{4}$. Is there an integer homology 3-sphere such that (smoothly) $s(M)$ =1?

(c) Are the functions s or $s_{~}algorithmically$ computable?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.29
records.statement:
Let $\Sigma$ be a locally flat surface in $S^{4}$ with $\pi_{1}(S^{4} \setminus \Sigma)$ cyclic.

(a) Prove that $\Sigma$ is topologically unknotted.

(b) Assuming that $\Sigma$ is smoothly embedded and orientable, prove that $\Sigma$ is smoothly unknotted (or find an example that is not).

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.30
records.statement: Does there exist a pair of closed, oriented surfaces in $S^{4}$ that are topologically but not smoothly isotopic? If such an exotic pair exists, does there exist an infinite family? Can the surfaces be taken to be 2-spheres? Surfaces of genus-g for any given $g \geq$ 0?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.31
records.statement: Does every knot in $S^{3}$ bound an exotic pair of orientable surfaces in $B^{4}$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.32
records.statement: Does there exist a locally flat embedding $f: \Sigma \to S^{4}$ for some closed surface $\Sigma$ such that f is not topologically ambiently isotopic to a smooth embedding? Particularly in the case that $\Sigma=S^{2}$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.33
records.statement:
Let $S_{1}, S_{2}$ be two topologically isotopic, smoothly embedded closed surfaces in a closed, oriented, smooth 4-manifold X. When do $S_{1}$ and $S_{2}$ in X become smoothly isotopic after one

(a) external stabilization?

(b) standard internal stabilization?

(c) internal stabilizations? Is there an upper bound depending on X on the number of such stabilizations required to make the surfaces smoothly isotopic?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.34
records.statement: Let $\Sigma$ be a surface embedded in $S^{4}$. Can $\Sigma$ be unknotted by a sequence of torus surgeries in its complement, such that the ambient manifold is always $S^{4}$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.35
records.statement:
(a) Give an algebraic classification of groups that arise as the fundamental group of the complement of a smooth or locally flat 2-sphere in $S^{4}$.

(b) Let $\Lambda = \mathbb{Z}[t, t-^{1}]$. Classify the $\Lambda-modules$ that arise as the Alexander module of a smooth or locally flat 2-sphere in $S^{4}$.

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.36
records.statement: Are homotopy types of 2-knot complements determined by their homotopy 2-types?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.37
records.statement: (Kinoshita conjecture). Does every projective plane in $S^{4}$ decompose as a connected sum of a knotted 2-sphere and an unknotted projective plane?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.38
records.statement: Let $\Delta \subset B^{4}$ be a ribbon disk. Is $B^{4} \setminus \Delta$ aspherical, i.e. is $\pi_{i}(B^{4} \setminus \Delta)$ =0 for all i>1?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.39
records.statement: Let K be a closed surface smoothly embedded in a 4-manifold $M^{4}$. Describe the subgroup of the mapping class group $Mod(K)$ of diffeomorphisms of K that extend to diffeomorphisms of M. Conversely, is it possible to characterize when a given subgroup of the mapping class group arises as the group of extendable diffeomorphisms for some K inside some $M^{4}$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.40
records.statement: Is every link of 2-spheres in $S^{4}$ slice?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.41
records.statement: Let $\Sigma$ be a compact surface and let X be a connected 4manifold. Let $f_{0}, f_{1}: \Sigma \to X$ be $\pi_{1}-negligible$ embeddings that agree on $\partial\Sigma$ and that are homotopic rel. boundary. Give computable invariants that decide whether there is $a \pi_{1}-negligible$ concordance in $X \times I$ between $f_{0}$ and $f_{1}$.

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.42
records.statement:
(a) If X is a smooth, closed, simply connected 4-manifold $withb_{2}(X) \geq$ 2, are all knots slice in X?

(b) In particular, are all knots slice in $\mathbb{CP}^{2}\#\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^{2}$? In the K3 surface?

(c) Can the set of slice knots detect exotic smooth structures? That is, do there exist homeomorphic 4-manifolds X and $X^{1}$ and a knot $K \subset S^{3}$ that is slice in X but not in $X^{1}$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.43
records.statement: Let K be a knot on the boundary of $X \setminus B^{\circ 4}$, where X is a negative definite, smooth 4-manifold. Suppose K bounds a smoothly embedded, nullhomotopic surface $\Sigma$ in $X \setminus B^{\circ 4}$. Is the following inequality $2g(\Sigma) \geq$ |s(K)| (8) always satisfied? Here $s(K)$ denotes Rasmussen’s s-invariant [Ras10].

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.44
records.statement:
(a) Let X be a closed, simply connected 4-manifold. Let $g \geq$ 0 and $d \geq$ 0 be integers. Fix $x \in H_{2}(X;\mathbb{Z})$. Does there exist a (smooth, locally flat) generic immersion $f: \Sigma_{g} \to X$ such that $f_{*}[\Sigma_{g}] = x$, with d transverse double points?

(b) An important special case is $d =$ 0. Let $g: H_{2}(X;\mathbb{Z}) \to \mathbb{N}_{0}$ be the genus function assigning to $x \in H_{2}(X;\mathbb{Z})$ the minimal genus of any (smooth, locally flat) embedded surface in X whose fundamental class represents x. The problem is to compute the locally flat genus function for some 4-manifold $X \ne S^{4}$, and to compute the smooth genus function for new 4-manifolds.

(c) For a specific example, is the class (3,2) $\in H_{2}(\mathbb{CP}^{2}\#\mathbb{CP}^{2};\mathbb{Z})$ represented by a sphere?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.45
records.statement:
Let X be a closed simply connected smooth 4-manifold and let $\Sigma$ be a closed, orientable surface. Fix a smooth embedding of $f: \Sigma \hookrightarrow X$ to serve as a basepoint. For which $k\geq 0$ does the equality
$$
\ker i_{*}=\ker s_{*}
$$
 hold, where
$$
\begin{aligned} i_{*}&:\pi_{k}(\operatorname{Emb}^{DIFF}(\Sigma,X^{\circ});f)\to \pi_{k}(\operatorname{Emb}^{TOP}(\Sigma,X^{\circ});f),\\ s_{*}&:\pi_{k}(\operatorname{Emb}^{DIFF}(\Sigma,X^{\circ});f)\to \operatorname*{colim}_{N\to\infty}\pi_{k}(\operatorname{Emb}^{DIFF}(\Sigma,X^{\circ}\#_{N}S^{2}\times S^{2});f). \end{aligned}
$$
 Here $i_*$ is induced by inclusion and $s_*$ by stabilization. To make sense of this for k=0, define $keri_{*}$ and $kers_{*}$ to be the preimages under $i_{*}$ and $s_{*}$ respectively of [f].

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.46
records.statement: Are all groups good?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.47
records.statement: (Round handle problem). Is there a link $L \subset S^{3}$ with vanishing pairwise linking numbers that is not round handle slice?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.48
records.statement: Let $\Delta$ be a contractible, compact 4-manifold. Is the space of homeomorphisms of $\Delta$ that fix the boundary pointwise, with the compact-open topology, a contractible space?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.49
records.statement: Give an effective necessary and sufficient condition for an open 4-manifold to be homeomorphic to the interior of a compact 4-manifold.

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.50
records.statement:
Classify closed topological 4-manifolds (orientable and not) with finite fundamental group, up to homeomorphism. The following infinite families of fundamental groups are of particular interest.

(a) Dihedral groups.

(b) Quaternionic groups.

(c) Abelian groups with two or three generators. A significant starting point would be to complete the classification for 4-manifolds with fundamental group of order at most eight.

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.51
records.statement: Let X be a closed, smooth 4-manifold with fundamental group isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}$. Is the $\mathbb{Z}[\mathbb{Z}]-valued$ intersection form on $\pi_{2}(X)$ extended from $\mathbb{Z}$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.52
records.statement: Let M and N be closed, orientable topological 4-manifolds with $\pi_{1}(M) \cong \pi_{1}(N)a$ good group. Suppose that M and N are simple homotopy equivalent and stably homeomorphic. Is there a simple homotopy equivalence $N \to M$ that lies in the orbit of Id $:M \to M$ under the Wall realization action of $L^{s}_{5}(\mathbb{Z}[\pi_{1}(M)])$ on the simple structure set of M?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.53
records.statement: Does there exist an algorithm that takes as input a closed, triangulated 4-manifold, and outputs in finite time whether or not that 4-manifold is homeomorphic to $S^{4}$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.54
records.statement: The quadratic 2 type of a 4-manifold M is the data $(\pi_{1}(M), \pi_{2}(M), \lambda_{M}, k_{M})$ of the fundamental group $\pi_{1}(M)$, the second homotopy group $\pi_{2}(M)$ considered as $a \mathbb{Z}[\pi_{1}(M)]-module$, the equivariant intersection for $m \lambda_{M}$, and the k-invariant in $k_{M} \in H^{3}(B\pi_{1}(M);\pi_{2}(M))$. Which quadratic 2-types are realized by closed, oriented topological 4-manifolds? Which are realized by closed, oriented, smooth 4-manifolds? Can this problem be solved for specific fundamental groups, for example for certain families of non-cyclic finite groups?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.55
records.statement: Let M and N be closed, orientable, connected 4-manifolds with isomorphic quadratic 2-types. If $\pi_{1}(M) \cong \pi_{1}(N)are$ finite, are M and N homotopy equivalent?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.56
records.statement: (4D s-cobordism conjecture). Let $(W^{4};M_{0}^{3}, M_{1}^{3})$ be a smooth 4-dimensionals-cobordism between closed 3-manifolds. Is W diffeomorphic to $M_{0} \times$ [0,1]?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.57
records.statement: Let X and Y be closed, oriented, smooth 4-manifolds with the same Euler characteristic and signature. Is there a torus link L in X with trivial normal bundle such that some choice of torus surgery along L transforms X into a manifold diffeomorphic to Y? What if we only require that the result be homeomorphic to Y?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.58
records.statement:
(a) Which Seifert fibered homology spheres $\Sigma(a_{1}$, . . . , $a_{n})bound$ acyclic manifolds? Are there any examples with four or more singular fibers that bound acyclic manifolds?

(b) Which Seifert fibered homology spheres bound contractible manifolds? Is there an example that bounds an acyclic manifold but not a contractible manifold?

(c) Are there any Seifert fibered homology spheres that arise as cork boundaries?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.59
records.statement: Are lens spaces topologically homology cobordant if and only if they are homeomorphic?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.60
records.statement:
(a) Let X be an open, spin, smooth4-manifold. Does X have a proper smooth embedding in $\mathbb{R}^{6}$?

(b) By choosing a proper exhaustion function on W,(a) would follow from an affirmative answer to the following. Let (W;M, N) be a compact, smooth spin cobordism with a smooth embedding f of M in $S^{5}$. Is there a smooth embedding F: (W;M, N) $\to (S^{5} \times I;S^{5} \times$ \{0\}, $S^{5} \times$ \{1\}) whose restriction to M coincides with f?

(c) Let (W;M, N) be a compact, smooth spin cobordism with smooth embeddings f of M in $S^{5}$ and g of N in $S^{5}$ such that $\sigma(N, S^{5}) -\sigma(M, S^{5}) = \sigma(W)$. Is there a smooth embedding F: (W;M, N) $\to (S^{5} \times I;S^{5} \times$ \{0\}, $S^{5} \times$ \{1\}) whose restriction to M coincides with f and whose restriction to N coincides with g?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.61
records.statement: What do different 4-manifold gauge theories see?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.62
records.statement:
Let X be a smooth, closed, connected, oriented 4-manifold with $b^{+}_{2}(X)$ >1.

(a) Does X have Donaldson simple type?

(b) Does X have Seiberg–Witten simple type?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.63
records.statement:
How many independent basic classes can a simply connected smooth 4-manifold X have, as measured $bybr(X)$, the rank of the span of the basic classes?

(a) Is there an upper bound $forbr(X)$ in terms of topological invariants of X?

(b) In particular, is $br(X) \leq b^{+}_{2}(X)$ for all simply connected X with $b^{+}_{2}(X)$ odd?

(c) Is there a smooth indefinite, simply connected 4-manifold X with $b_{2}(X) \geq$ 3 for which the image of $ev_{*}: \operatorname{Diff}(X) \to \operatorname{Aut}(Q_{X})$ is finite, or even trivial?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.64
records.statement: Find an irreducible, closed, smooth 4-manifold with nontrivial Bauer–Furuta invariant but with trivial Seiberg–Witten invariant.

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.65
records.statement:
Suppose X is a smooth4-manifold with the homology of $S^{1} \times S^{3}$ whose infinite cyclic cover $\widetilde{X}$ has $H^{1}(\widetilde{X})=0$. Furuta and Ohta [FO93] define an invariant $\lambda_{FO}(X)$ as 1/4 of the signed count of irreducible flat $SU(2)$ connections on X; this requires an orientation of X and a specified generator of $H^{1}(X)$.

(a) Does the following hold? The invariant $\lambda_{FO}(X)$ is an integer, and $\lambda_{FO}(X)\equiv \rho(Y,\mathfrak{s})$, where $\rho(Y,\mathfrak{s})$ is the Rokhlin invariant of an oriented spin 3 manifold Y that is Poincaré dual to the generator of $H^{1}(X)$.

(b) Mrowka–Ruberman–Saveliev [MRS11] give an approach, defining an invariant $\lambda_{SW}(X)$ by counting solutions to the Seiberg-Witten equations and adding an index-theoretic correction term. Is $\lambda_{FO}(X)=-\lambda_{SW}(X)$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.66
records.statement: Can the skein lasagna module detect exotic smooth structures on closed 4-manifolds?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.67
records.statement:
(a) Compute $\pi_{0}(\operatorname{Diff}^{+}(S^{4}))$. Do we have $\pi_{0}(\operatorname{Diff}^{+}(S^{4})) =$ \{1\}?

(b) In particular, does some implantation of the barbell map provide a nontrivial element in $\pi_{0}(\operatorname{Diff}^{+}(S^{4}))$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.68
records.statement:
Does every closed smooth 4-manifold admit an exotic diffeomorphism? How about the following special cases?

(a) Is there a definite smooth closed 4-manifold that admits an exotic diffeomorphism?

(b) Does $S^{2} \times S^{2}$ or K3 admit an exotic diffeomorphism?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.69
records.statement: Does there exist a diffeomorphism of a closed3-manifoldf: $M \to M$ such that f is topologically but not smoothly pseudo-isotopic to the identity?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.70
records.statement: Do there exist $k \geq$ 0 and a smooth closed 4-manifold X such that the map $\pi_{k}(\operatorname{Diff}(X)) \to \pi_{k}(\operatorname{Homeo}(X))$ induced by the inclusion $\operatorname{Diff}(X) \hookrightarrow \operatorname{Homeo}(X)$ is an isomorphism?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.71
records.statement:
(a) Do there exist $k \geq$ 0 and a smooth closed orientable 4-manifold X such that $\pi_{k}(\operatorname{Diff}(X))$ is finitely generated?

(b) Do there exist $k >$ 0 and a smooth closed orientable 4-manifold X such that $H_{k}(BDiff(X);\mathbb{Z})$ is finitely generated?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.72
records.statement:
Let X be a closed orientable topological 4-manifold with finite $\pi_{1}(X)$.

(a) Is $\pi_{k}(\operatorname{Homeo}(X))$ finitely generated for every $k \geq$ 0?

(b) Is $H_{k}(BHomeo(X);\mathbb{Z})$ finitely generated for every $k \geq$ 0?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.73
records.statement: Does the Morlet correspondence $BDiff_{\partial}(D^{n}) \cong \Omega^{n}_{0}(Top(n)/O(n))$ (10) hold for n=4?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.74
records.statement: Does there exist a closed, smooth 4-manifold X and a diffeomorphism f: $X \to X$ such that f is smoothly pseudo-isotopic to the identity, but f is not stably smoothly isotopic to the identity?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.75
records.statement: Let X be a connected smooth 4-manifold with nonempty boundary, with finite $\pi_{1}(X)$, and let $k \geq$ 0. Let $Diff_{\partial}(X)$ denote the group of diffeomorphisms of X that are the identity near $\partial X$. Is the image of the natural map $s_{*}: \pi_{k}(Diff_{\partial}(X)) \to$ colim $\pi_{k}(Diff_{\partial}(X\#_{N}S^{2} \times S^{2}))$ (11) $N \to \infty$ finitely generated? What about the analogous problem in the topological category?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.76
records.statement: Let X be a closed, oriented, simply connected, smooth 4manifold and fix $k >$ 0. Is there $N \geq$ 0 such that, for every $n \geq N$, the natural map $\pi_{k}(\operatorname{Diff}^{+}(X\#_{n}S^{2} \times S^{2})) \to \pi_{k}(\operatorname{Homeo}^{+}(X\#_{n}S^{2} \times S^{2}))$ is surjective?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.77
records.statement: For which $k \geq$ 0 and closed smooth 4-manifold X does the equality $\ker(i_{*}: \pi_{k}(Diff_{\partial}(X^{\circ})) \to \pi_{k}(Homeo_{\partial}(X^{\circ}))) =\ker(s_{*}: \pi_{k}(Diff_{\partial}(X^{\circ})) \to$ colim $\pi_{k}(Diff_{\partial}(X^{\circ}\#_{n}S^{2} \times S^{2})))$ (13) $n \to \infty$ hold?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.78
records.statement: Let X be a simply connected closed smooth 4-manifold. Does $BDiff(X)$ satisfy homological stability over $\mathbb{Q}$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.79
records.statement: Given $k >$ 0, is there a closed, simply connected, smooth 4manifold X and a nonzero homotopy class $\alpha \in \pi_{k}(Diff_{\partial}(X^{\circ}))$ such that $\alpha \in \ker(i_{*}: \pi_{k}(Diff_{\partial}(X^{\circ})) \to \pi_{k}(Homeo_{\partial}(X^{\circ})))$ (14) and $\alpha \notin \ker(s_{*}: \pi_{k}(Diff_{\partial}(X^{\circ})) \to \pi_{k}(Diff_{\partial}(X^{\circ}\#S^{2} \times S^{2})))$? (15)

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.80
records.statement: Is there $n >$ 2 and a smooth closed simply connected 4manifold X for which there is an element of ordernin the $subgroupker(\pi_{0}\operatorname{Diff}(X) \to \pi_{0}\operatorname{Homeo}(X))$? More generally, is there a subgroup of order nin $\ker(\pi_{0}\operatorname{Diff}(X) \to \pi_{0}\operatorname{Homeo}(X))$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.81
records.statement: Is there a smooth, closed, simply connected 4-manifold X for which the group $\ker(\pi_{0}(\operatorname{Diff}(X)) \to \pi_{0}(\operatorname{Homeo}(X)))$ is finitely generated?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.82
records.statement:
Let $\phi$ be a self-diffeomorphism of a closed, simply-connected, smooth 4-manifold X. Suppose that for every smooth surface $\Sigma$ in X, the surfaces $\Sigma$ and $\phi(\Sigma)$ are smoothly isotopic.

(a) Is $\phi$ necessarily smoothly isotopic to the identity map?

(b) Is $\phi smoothly$ isotopic to a diffeomorphism that is supported on $a B^{4} \subset X$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.83
records.statement: For which 4-manifolds does there exist a smooth structure such that there exists a non-smoothable homeomorphism with respect to that smooth structure?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.84
records.statement: Is there a closed oriented smooth 4-manifold X for which every finite subgroup Gof the mapping class group $\pi_{0}(\operatorname{Diff}^{+}(X))can$ be realized by a finite group action on X?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.85
records.statement: Is there a closed orientable smooth 4-manifold X for which the identity component $Diff_{0}(X)$ of the diffeomorphism group is not uniformly perfect?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.86
records.statement: Is it the case that for every closed, smoothable topological 4manifold X, there exists a locally linear finite group action on X, such that for every smooth structure on X, the action is non-smoothable?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.87
records.statement: Is there an exotic action of $\mathbb{Z}/n$ on $S^{4}$ with 0-dimensional fixed point set? 1-dimensional? 2-dimensional?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.88
records.statement: Let $\tau: S^{4} \to S^{4}$ be a free (hence orientation-reversing) involution. Is there an embedded $S^{2} \subset S^{4}$ that is invariant under $\tau$? This is equivalent to the existence of an embedded $\mathbb{RP}^{2}$ in $S^{4}/\tau \cong \mathbb{RP}^{4}$, carrying the nontrivial class in $H_{2}(\mathbb{RP}^{4};\mathbb{Z}/2)$. This condition on the homology class will be assumed for the rest of the problem.

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.89
records.statement:
Classify smooth, effective circle actions on simply connected 4-manifolds with boundary.

(a) Classify simply connected4-manifolds with boundary that admit circle actions.

(b) For each such 4-manifold, classify the circle actions up to conjugation by diffeomorphisms.

(c) Given a 4-manifold X with a circle action on its boundary, when does the action extend over X? When does it extend uniquely?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.90
records.statement:
Do the Chern numbers $c^{2}_{1}$ and $c_{2}$ of every closed, symplectic 4–manifold X that is not a ruled surface satisfy the following?

(a) $c^{2}_{1} \leq 3c_{2}$.

(b) $c^{2}_{1} =3c_{2}$ >0 if and only if $X =\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ or X is a complex ball quotient.

(c) $c_{2} \geq$ 0.

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.91
records.statement: Present a topological construction of symplectic fake projective planes. Does there exist a symplectic fake projective plane that is not a complex ball quotient?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.92
records.statement: Is every symplectic Calabi-Yau surface diffeomorphic to either the K3 surface, the Enriques surface or $a T^{2}-bundle$ over $T^{2}$?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.93
records.statement: Is every symplectic form on the standard K3 surface symplectomorphic to a Kähler form?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.94
records.statement: Are homotopy equivalent Horikawa surfaces in different deformation classes diffeomorphic as 4–manifolds? Are they symplectomorphic?

records.name: Kirby Problem 4.95
records.statement:
