records.statement: Do CAT(0) (or (bi)automatic) groups satisfy the Tits alternative?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 2.9
records.statement: Does every Artin group have a finite $K(G,1)$?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 2.11
records.statement: (Eric Swenson) Let $X$ be a proper CAT(0) metric space and $G$ a finitely generated group acting properly discontinuously by isometries on $X$. (1) Can $G$ be an infinite torsion group? (2) If the action is cocompact, can $G$ contain an infinite torsion subgroup?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 2.12
records.statement: (Kim Ruane) Let $G$ be a Coxeter group, for example a right-angled Coxeter group, acting properly discontinuously by isometries on a CAT(0) space $X$. How is $X$ different from the Coxeter complex? Specifically, if $H$ is a special subgroup of $G$, is there a closed convex subset of $X$ on which $H$ acts cocompactly?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 2.13
records.statement: (Ruth Charney) Classify Coxeter groups up to isomorphism.

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 2.14
records.statement: (Ruth Charney) Classify Artin groups up to isomorphism.

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 2.16
records.statement: (Ruth Charney) Are all [finite type] Artin groups CAT(0)?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 2.17
records.statement: (Ruth Charney) Are all Artin groups automatic?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 2.18
records.statement: (Ross Geoghegan) A proper CAT(0) space $M$ is almost geodesically complete if there is $R\geq0$ such that for all $a,b\in M$ there is an infinite geodesic ray starting at $a$ and passing within $R$ of $b$. If $\operatorname{Isom}(M)$ acts cocompactly on $M$, is $M$ almost geodesically complete?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 2.19
records.statement: (Dani Wise) A triplane is a CAT(0) space obtained by gluing three Euclidean half-planes along their boundaries, and a CAT(0) space $X$ has isolated flats if it contains no isometrically embedded triplane. A subgroup $H$ is quasiconvex relative to an action on $X$ if, for some $x\in X$ and $K$, every geodesic joining two points of $Hx$ lies in the $K$-neighborhood of $Hx$. Conjecture: if $G$ acts properly discontinuously and cocompactly on a CAT(0) space $X$ with isolated flats and $H\leq G$ is finitely generated, then $H\hookrightarrow G$ is a quasi-isometric embedding if and only if $H$ is quasiconvex relative to the action of $G$ on $X$.

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 3.1
records.statement: (Hanna Neumann Conjecture) If A and B are nontrivial subgroups of a free group, then rk(A ∩B) −1 ≤(rk(A) −1)(rk(B) −1).

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 3.2
records.statement: (Swarup) If G is a Fuchsian group, define area(G) to be the area of the convex core of H2/A. Since area(A) = 2π(rk(A)−1) for Fuchsian groups which are free, the Hanna Neumann Conjecture can be phrased in terms of free Fuchsian groups: 2πarea(A∩B) ≤area(A)area(B) whenever A and B are nontrivial free subgroups of a Fuchsian group. Prove such inequalities (possibly with a worse constant) for (not necessarily free) torsion-free quasiconvex subgroups of a quasi-convex Kleinian group in Hn, where area is replaced by the n-dimensional volume of the convex core.

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 3.3
records.statement: (J. Cornick) If G is f.g. and the homological dimension hd G = 1, is G free?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 3.5
records.statement: Conjecture. Limit groups are CAT(0).

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 3.6
records.statement: Characterize groups of the form Fm ∗Z Fn which are limit groups.

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 3.7
records.statement: Characterize 1-relator groups which are limit groups.

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 3.9
records.statement: Conjecture: for $n>1$, the set $$\{(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in F_n^n:x_1,\ldots,x_n\text{ is a basis of }F_n\}$$ is not definable.

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 3.10
records.statement: Conjecture. The only definable subgroups of Fn are cyclic and the entire group.

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 3.11
records.statement: For $x\in[F_n,F_n]$, define its genus as the least $g$ such that $x$ is a product of $g$ commutators. Let $f(g)$ be a uniform bound, independent of $x$, on the number of Nielsen-equivalence classes of expressions of a genus-$g$ element as a product of $g$ commutators. Give an explicit upper bound for $f(g)$.

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 4.1
records.statement: (de la Harpe) Is PSL2(R) a maximal closed subgroup of Homeo+(S1)?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 4.2
records.statement: Is there a proper closed subgroup of Homeo+(S1) that acts transitively on (unordered) 4-tuples? Or k-tuples (k ≠ 3)? Relation to earthquakes?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 4.4
records.statement: (Swarup) Suppose G is a 1-ended finitely presented group that acts on a compact connected metric space X as a convergence group. What can be said about G if X has cut points? Does X have to be locally connected? The model theorem of Bowditch [Bow99] and Swarup [Swa96] says that if G is word hyperbolic, then X is locally connected and doesn’t have cut points. In another interesting case, when G is a geometrically finite Kleinian group and X its limit set, cut points can arise, for example if G splits over a parabolic subgroup.

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 5.1
records.statement: (Jim Anderson) If G is a group of isometries of Hn, denote by Ax(G) the set of axes of the elements of G. If G1 and G2 are finitely generated and discrete, does Ax(G1) = Ax(G2) imply that G1 and G2 are commensurable?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 5.3
records.statement: (Ed Taylor) Does there exist a constant c > 0 such that the limit set of every non-classical Schottky group has Hausdorff dimension ≥c.

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 5.5
records.statement: (Misha Kapovich) Suppose $G$ is a finitely generated Kleinian group in $\operatorname{Isom}(\mathbb{H}^n)$. Is $$\delta(G)\leq\operatorname{vcd}(G),$$ with equality if and only if $G$ preserves a totally geodesic subspace $\mathbb{H}^k\subset\mathbb{H}^n$ such that $\mathbb{H}^k/G$ is compact?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 5.6
records.statement: (Misha Kapovich) Is there ϵ > 0 so that δ(G) < ϵ implies that G is virtually free?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 5.7
records.statement: (Misha Kapovich) Is there a finitely-generated discrete subgroup of SO(n, 1) whose action on the limit set is not ergodic? Is not recurrent?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 6.1
records.statement: (Ian Leary) Suppose G is virtually of type FP over the field Fp of p elements, and let g be an element of order p. Is the centralizer of g in G also virtually of type FP over Fp?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 6.2
records.statement: (Ian Leary) Is there a group of finite vcd that does not act with finite stabilizers on an acyclic complex of dimension equal to its vcd?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 6.3
records.statement: (Peter Kropholler) If G is FP over the rationals, is there a bound on the orders of finite subgroups of G?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 7.2
records.statement: (Swarup) Starting with a finitely presented group $G$, take maximal graph-of-groups decompositions alternately over finite and over two-ended edge groups, each time continuing with the resulting vertex groups. Conjecture 1: there is a finitely presented group for which this process never terminates. Conjecture 2 (Strong Accessibility): for hyperbolic groups, and for CAT(0) groups, this process always terminates.

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 7.3
records.statement: (Sageev) Is there a f.p. 1-ended group G with G ∼= G∗Z?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 7.5
records.statement: (Papasoglou) Is there a f.p. torsion-free group G that does not split over a virtually abelian subgroup, but has infinitely many splittings over F2?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 8.2
records.statement: (Shalen) If a finitely presented group G acts nontrivially (i.e. without global fixed points) on an R-tree, does it act nontrivially on a simplicial tree?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 8.3
records.statement: (Mohan Ramachandran) For a finitely presented group $G$, consider: (A) some finite-index subgroup of $G$ admits a nontrivial action on a simplicial tree; (B) if $X$ is a finite complex with fundamental group $G$, then some covering space of $X$ has at least two ends. To what extent are (A) and (B) equivalent?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 8.5
records.statement: (Noel Brady) Are there groups of type Fn but not Fn+1 (n ≥3) which do not contain Z × Z? All known examples contain Zn−1.

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 8.6
records.statement: (Olympia Talelli) Is there a torsion-free group G of infinite cohomological dimension such that there is n0 with the property that if H is a subgroup of G with finite cohomological dimension cdH, then cdH ≤n0.

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 8.7
records.statement: Can Zp∞be embedded in an FP∞-group? Or in an FP3-group? Can an Fn-group be embedded in an Fn+1-group (n ≥2)?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 8.8
records.statement: Compute the asymptotic dimension of CAT(0) groups, Out(Fn), mapping class groups, nonuniform lattices, Thompson’s group. Is there a group of finite type whose asymptotic dimension is infinite?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 8.9
records.statement: Is there a finitely presented group $G=F/N$, with $F$ a finite-rank free group, such that $$d_G\!\left(N/[N,N]\right)<d_F(N)<\infty?$$ Here $d_F(N)$ is the least number of $G$-orbits of $2$-cells needed to make the associated cover simply connected, while $d_G(N/[N,N])$ is the least number needed to kill its first homology.

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 8.10
records.statement: Suppose $H=F/N$ is finitely presented and contains $C^n$ for every $n$. Write $G_n=H*_{C^n}H=F*F/N_n$. If $C$ is nontrivial and finite, is $$\lim_{n\to\infty}d_{F*F}(N_n)=\infty?$$

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 9.2
records.statement: (Andrews-Curtis) If K and L are simple homotopy equivalent finite 2-complexes, can one transform K to L by a sequence of elementary collapses and expansions of 1- and 2-cells, and by sliding 2-cells (i.e. reattaching them by maps homotopic to the old attaching maps)?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 9.3
records.statement: (Wise) Is there a finite aspherical 2-complex X with π1(X) coherent and with χ(X) ≥2?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 10.1
records.statement: (Igor Belegredek) Let X be a non-positively curved symmetric space. Find conditions on a group Γ so that the space of conjugacy classes of faithful discrete representations of Γ into the isometry group of X is compact (noncompact).

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 10.2
records.statement: (Belegredek) Is there a 3-complex X (not necessarily aspherical) which is not homotopy equivalent to a 2-complex but H³(X; {G}) = 0 for all local coefficients?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 11.1
records.statement: Study the quasi-isometry group QI(Rn). How big is it?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 11.2
records.statement: (Kleiner) What are the quasi-isometries of the 3-dimensional group Sol?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 11.3
records.statement: (Kleiner) What are the q.i’s of the Gromov-Thurston examples of negatively pinched manifolds?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 11.4
records.statement: (Feighn) Let $\phi:F_n\to F_n$ be an automorphism and let $M_\phi$ be its mapping torus. Classify these groups up to quasi-isometry.

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 11.5
records.statement: (Bridson) Classify the mapping tori of automorphisms $\mathbb{Z}^n\to\mathbb{Z}^n$ up to quasi-isometry.

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 11.6
records.statement: (Bridson) Is G×Z quasi-isometric to G for G =Thompson’s group? Any f.g. group?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 12.1
records.statement: (Levitt) Can every measured geodesic lamination with 2-sided leaves on a non-orientable compact hyperbolic surface be approximated by a simplicial measured geodesic lamination with 2-sided leaves?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 12.2
records.statement: (Lubotzky) Does Out(Fn) have the congruence subgroup property?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 12.3
records.statement: (Kapovich) (a) For closed orientable surfaces $\Sigma_g$ and $\Sigma_h$, is there a faithful representation $\pi_1(\Sigma_g)\to\operatorname{MCG}(\Sigma_h)$ whose image consists of the identity and pseudo-Anosov classes, for some $g,h>1$? (b) Is there a four-manifold $M$ which is a surface bundle over a surface such that $\pi_1(M)$ is word-hyperbolic, or such that $M$ is hyperbolic?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 12.4
records.statement: (Bowditch) Is the Weil-Petersson metric on Teichmüller space hyperbolic? Is it quasi-isometric to the curve complex?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 12.5
records.statement: (Brock) What is the rank of the Weil-Petersson metric? What is the rank of the mapping class group?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 12.6
records.statement: Assuming that the fixed subgroup Fix(α) is cyclic, find a bound on the length of a generator of Fix(α) in terms of the complexity of α.

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 12.7
records.statement: Which α preserve an order (invariant under right translations) on Fn? If α has periodic elements it cannot preserve an order. Are there other obstructions?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 12.8
records.statement: Does Out(Fn) (n > 2) have a right orderable subgroup of finite index?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 12.9
records.statement: Can the mapping class group (or a finite index subgroup of it) of a closed surface be embedded into Out(Fn)? Into the mapping class group of a punctured surface?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 12.11
records.statement: (Grigorchuk) Aut(Fn) acts on the space ∂3Fn of triples of distinct ends of Fn. Denote by Yn the compact space (Cantor set) the quotient space of ∂3Fn by the group of inner automorphisms. Thus Out(Fn) acts on Yn. Describe the dynamics of this action; in particular the dynamics of any individual outer automorphism.

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 12.12
records.statement: Do there exist f.g. free subgroups of MCG(S) consisting of identity and pseudo-Anosov mapping classes which are not Schottky?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 12.13
records.statement: Do there exist non-free pseudo-Anosov subgroups?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 12.14
records.statement: For $\operatorname{Out}(F_n)$, do there exist finitely generated free subgroups consisting of the identity and irreducible automorphisms which are not Schottky? Do there exist nonfree subgroups all of whose nonidentity elements are irreducible?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 12.16
records.statement: Does every automorphism h : Fn →Fn leave invariant a finite index subgroup K such that hab : K/K′ →K/K′ has an eigenvalue which is a root of unity?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 12.17
records.statement: Does every closed 3-manifold M which fibers over S1 with fiber of genus ≥2 have a finite cover ˜ M with b1( ˜ M) > 1?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 12.18
records.statement: Is MCG(Sg) →QI(MCG(Sg)) an isomorphism for g ≥3?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 12.19
records.statement: Suppose that φ : MCG(Sg) →MCG(Sg) is a quasi-isometry. Does φ map maximal flats to maximal flats (“maximal flats” come from maximal rank abelian subgroups)?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 12.20
records.statement: For $\operatorname{Out}(F_n)$, is the natural map $\operatorname{Out}(F_n)\to QI(\operatorname{Out}(F_n))$ an isomorphism? Does every quasi-isometry of $\operatorname{Out}(F_n)$ map maximal flats to maximal flats?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 12.21
records.statement: If Γ is an irreducible uniform lattice in a higher rank connected semisimple Lie group, does every homomorphism Γ →Out(Fn) necessarily have finite image?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 12.22
records.statement: Is MCG(Sg,b,n) linear?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 12.23
records.statement: Let $SB_n$ be the singular braid monoid generated by $\sigma_i^{\pm1}$ and singular generators $\tau_i$. Define $\Phi:SB_n\to\mathbb{Z}B_n$ by $\Phi(\sigma_i)=\sigma_i$ and $\Phi(\tau_i)=\sigma_i-\sigma_i^{-1}$. Conjecture: $\Phi$ is injective.

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 12.80
records.statement: (Yves de Cornulier) Let G be residually torsion-free nilpotent. Is G Haagerup (= a-(T)-menable)?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 13.1
records.statement: (Kevin Whyte) Let K be a finite complex with π = π(K) amenable. Is there a uniform bound to the betti numbers of finite covers of K?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 13.2
records.statement: (Kevin Whyte) Is every solvable PD(n) group polycyclic?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 13.3
records.statement: (Henry Glover) Does for every finite graph G the following 1−2−∞- conjecture hold: G is planar, a double cover of G is planar, or no finite cover is planar?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 13.4
records.statement: (S. Ivanov) Is there a f.p. slender group which is not polycyclic-by-finite?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 13.5
records.statement: (Seymour Bachmut) Is SL2(K) finitely generated for K = Z[X, X−1] or K = F[X, X−1, Y, Y −1] for a field F?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 13.6
records.statement: Are 1-relator groups coherent?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 13.7
records.statement: Let $L$ be a flag triangulation of $S^{2k-1}$, let $f_i$ be the number of $i$-simplices of $L$, and define $$\chi=1-\sum_{i=0}^{2k-1}(-1)^i\frac{f_i}{2^{i+1}}.$$ Conjecture: $(-1)^k\chi\geq0$.

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 13.8
records.statement: Do there exist groups G with balanced presentation (same number of generators and relations), with H1(G) = 0 and with unsolvable word problem?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 13.9
records.statement: Is there a sequence of (perfect, of course) groups with balanced presentations among which one cannot recognize trivial groups?

records.name: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 13.10
records.statement: Let $G$ be a one-relator group whose relator $W$ is a cyclically reduced word in the generators, and let $P$ be the submonoid of $G$ generated by all prefixes of $W$. Is the membership problem for $P$ in $G$ decidable?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 1
records.statement: Can the odometer acting on the rooted binary tree be embedded in a nonabelian free pro-$2$ group?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 2
records.statement: Let a finitely presented pro-$p$ group have $r+2$ generators and $r$ relators. Must it have an open subgroup that maps continuously onto a nonabelian free pro-$p$ group?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 3
records.statement: Let $G$ be a closed transitive subgroup of the automorphism group of a rooted tree. Must every level stabilizer of $G$ contain an element acting without fixed points on the boundary?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 4
records.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a countable subgroup of $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$ containing no parabolic elements, and let $\gamma$ be a random element of $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$. Show that $\langle\Gamma,\gamma\rangle$ almost surely contains no parabolic elements.

records.name: Some Questions — Question 5
records.statement: Determine the asymptotic length of a shortest nontrivial group law for the $n$-fold iterated wreath product of $C_2$.

records.name: Some Questions — Question 6
records.statement: Can the sequence of metric balls in an infinite Cayley graph form a family of expanders?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 7
records.statement: Suppose $G$ and $H$ are Cayley, or vertex-transitive, expanders on the same number of vertices and can be matched with asymptotically vanishing edge distance. Must they be isomorphic?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 8
records.statement: If $G$ is a finite vertex-transitive expander, must every almost automorphism of $G$ be close to an automorphism?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 9
records.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be finitely generated and let $\{H_n:n\geq1\}$ be a property-$\tau$ family of finite-index normal subgroups. Does the chain $\Gamma_n=\bigcap_{k=1}^n H_k$ have property $\tau$?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 10
records.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be finitely presented with a chain of finite-index normal subgroups having trivial intersection and property $\tau$. Must $\Gamma$ contain a nonabelian free subgroup?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 11
records.statement: For an infinite $d$-regular Ramanujan graph, does random-walk neighborhood sampling converge to the $d$-regular tree?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 12
records.statement: For a locally convergent sequence $(G_n)$ of bounded-degree integer-labeled graphs, does the normalized rank modulo $p$ of the adjacency matrix converge?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 13
records.statement: For a graph sequence $(G_n)$ define $e((G_n))=\liminf |E(G_n)|/|V(G_n)|$, and define its combinatorial cost as the infimum of $e((H_n))$ over graph sequences $(H_n)$ on the same vertex sets for which the identity maps have uniformly bounded bi-Lipschitz constants. If $(G_n)$ and $(H_n)$ converge locally to the same limit, must they have the same combinatorial cost?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 14
records.statement: Compactness implies that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $K>0$ such that every finite graph can be approximated within error $\varepsilon$ by a finite graph of size $K$. Give an estimate for $K$ in terms of $\varepsilon$.

records.name: Some Questions — Question 15
records.statement: Let $(G_n)$ be a locally convergent graph sequence and let $\mu_n$ be the probability distribution of the roots of the chromatic polynomial of $G_n$. For every $k$, does $\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_{\mathbb{C}}z^k\,d\mu_n$ exist?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 16
records.statement: Which probability measures can occur as eigenvalue distributions of finite $d$-regular graphs? Find natural restrictions.

records.name: Some Questions — Question 17
records.statement: Let $G$ be a $d$-regular Cayley graph with spectral measure $\mu$. Is $\mu$ a weak limit of spectral measures of finite $d$-regular graphs?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 18
records.statement: For each $d\geq3$, does the independence ratio of a uniformly random $d$-regular graph converge in probability as the number of vertices tends to infinity?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 19
records.statement: Do uniformly random $d$-regular graphs converge, in local-global convergence, to the weak closure of independent identically distributed processes?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 20
records.statement: Is the i.i.d. action of the free group $F_2$ a local-global limit of finite actions of $F_2$?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 21
records.statement: Let $\Gamma$ have property (T), and let $(G_n)$ be a sofic approximation of a Cayley graph of $\Gamma$. Can $(G_n)$ be changed by an asymptotically vanishing edit distance to a sequence for which every subsequence of connected components is an expander family?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 22
records.statement: Can every ergodic unimodular random network that is almost surely an infinite tree be obtained as the limit of an expander family?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 23
records.statement: Let $G$ be an infinite vertex-transitive graph, let $A$ be a finite vertex set, let $b$ be a vertex, and let $\partial A$ be the set of vertices at distance one from $A$. Prove that $\sum_{x\in\partial A}d(b,x)\geq |A|$.

records.name: Some Questions — Question 24
records.statement: Define the first $L^2$ Betti number of a vertex-transitive graph $G$ from the expected degree of a free spanning forest. Do $G$ and its square $G^2$ have the same first $L^2$ Betti number?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 25
records.statement: Can free spanning forests be used to prove basic properties of the first $L^2$ Betti number, such as multiplicativity upon passage to a finite-index subgroup?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 26
records.statement: Let $G$ be an infinite Cayley graph of a group that is not virtually cyclic. Prove that there exists $p<1$ for which Bernoulli $p$-edge percolation on $G$ has an infinite cluster.

records.name: Some Questions — Question 27
records.statement: Does every infinite connected Cayley graph admit an invariant random perfect matching?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 28
records.statement: Does every infinite Cayley graph, or every infinite vertex-transitive graph, have a spanning tree without leaves?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 29
records.statement: In every infinite Cayley graph, does the density of dead ends tend to zero?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 30
records.statement: Are factors of i.i.d. on the $3$-regular tree closed in the weak topology? In particular, is the weak limit of majority functions on $n$-balls a factor of i.i.d.?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 31
records.statement: Does every infinite Cayley graph $G$ admit a $G$-invariant proper coloring with $\chi(G)$ colors?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 32
records.statement: Let $X$ be the space of $k$-regular Cayley graphs with the local-convergence topology and let $T\subset X$ be the closed subset of transient graphs. Is the Green function, equivalently the expected number of returns to the identity, continuous on $T$?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 33
records.statement: For every $k>1$, does there exist $C(k)<1$ such that the return probability of every transient $k$-regular Cayley graph is at most $C(k)$?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 34
records.statement: For a nonamenable group $\Gamma$, does the Bernoulli shift $\{0,1\}^{\Gamma}$ factor onto $\{0,1,2\}^{\Gamma}$?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 35
records.statement: Can every $d$-regular graphing without multiple edges be properly edge-colored by $d+1$ colors?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 36
records.statement: Let $(G_n)$ and $(H_n)$ converge to the same graph limit, and let $(T_n)$ be a convergent sequence with each $T_n$ a spanning tree of $G_n$. Do there exist spanning trees $P_n$ of $H_n$ converging to the same limit as $(T_n)$?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 37
records.statement: Let $G$ be a bounded-degree expander, or strongly ergodic, graphing that can be properly colored by $C$ colors with arbitrarily small error. Can it be properly $C$-colored?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 38
records.statement: Let $G$ be a bounded-degree expander, or strongly ergodic, graphing that weakly contains a finite graph $H$. Does $G$ factor onto $H$?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 39
records.statement: Does every higher-rank semisimple real lattice have rank gradient zero?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 40
records.statement: If $A$ and $B$ are countably infinite groups, does $A\times B$ have fixed price $1$?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 41
records.statement: Does every countable group have fixed price; that is, do all its free probability-measure-preserving actions have the same cost?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 42
records.statement: Does every residually finite property-(T) group have rank gradient zero?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 43
records.statement: Let $\Gamma$ act on $X$ by probability-measure-preserving maps and let $H\leq\Gamma$ have finite index. Is $\operatorname{cost}(H,X)-1=(\operatorname{cost}(\Gamma,X)-1)[\Gamma:H]$?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 44
records.statement: For a free action of $\Gamma$ on $X$, is $\operatorname{cost}(\Gamma,X)=\operatorname{cost}(\Gamma,X\times X)$ for the diagonal action on $X\times X$?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 45
records.statement: Let an amenable group $\Gamma$ act ergodically and essentially faithfully on $X$. Is the groupoid cost of the action $1$? If $\Gamma$ is finitely presented, is this true for every infinite ergodic action?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 46
records.statement: Given a graphing of an equivalence relation, is there a subgraphing whose cost is arbitrarily close to the cost of the relation?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 47
records.statement: Can a nonabelian free group $F$ have a nontrivial pseudocharacter invariant under $\operatorname{Aut}(F)$?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 48
records.statement: Are two independent random subsets of $\mathbb{Z}$ almost surely quasi-isometric as metric spaces? What is the answer for other Cayley graphs, such as that of $\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 49
records.statement: Let $P$ be a finite $p$-group of order $n$ and let $w$ be any word. Is the probability that $w$ is satisfied in $P$ at least $1/n$?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 50
records.statement: Let $M$ be the set of measurable real functions, and define $H_f(x,y)=(x,y+f(x))$ and $V_f(x,y)=(x+f(y),y)$. What group is generated by $\{H_f:f\in M\}$ and $\{V_f:f\in M\}$? Is there an $N$ such that every element is a product of at most $N$ such generators?

records.name: Some Questions — Question 51
records.statement: Determine the asymptotic length of the shortest nontrivial word that is a law in every group of order $2^n$.

records.name: Algebraic Stories — Generic $k$-rank
records.statement: Given a triple of positive integers $(k,d,n)$, calculate $\operatorname{rk}_k^\circ(kd,n).$

records.name: Algebraic Stories — Generic $k$-rank
records.statement: The $k$-rank of a general form of degree $kd$ in $n$ variables is given by $$ \operatorname{rk}_k^\circ(kd,n)=\begin{cases} \min \left\{s\ge 1 | s\binom{n+d-1}{n-1}-\binom {s}{2}\ge \binom{n+2d-1}{n-1}\right\}, & \text{ for } k=2; \min \left\{s\ge 1 | s\binom{n+d-1}{n-1}\ge \binom{n+kd-1}{n-1}\right\}, & \text{ for } k\ge 3. \end{cases} $$

records.name: Algebraic Stories — Maximal $k$-rank
records.statement: Given a triple of positive integers $(k,d,n)$, calculate $\operatorname{rk}_k^{\max}(kd,n).$

records.name: Algebraic Stories — Maximal $k$-rank
records.statement: For any positive integers $k,d$, the maximal $k$-rank $\operatorname{rk}^{\max}_k(kd,2)$ of binary forms equals $k$. Additionally, in the above notation, binary forms representable by $\ell_1 \ell_2^{kd-1}$, where $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ are non-proportional linear forms, have the latter maximal $k$-rank.

records.name: Algebraic Stories — The $k$-rank of monomials
records.statement: Given $k \geq 3$ and a monomial $m$ of degree $kd$, determine the monomial $k$-rank $\operatorname{rk}_k(m)$.

records.name: Algebraic Stories — The $k$-rank of monomials
records.statement: Given $k \geq 3$ and a monomial $x^a y^b$ of degree $a+b=kd$, it is known that $\operatorname{rk}_k(x^{a}y^{b}) \leq \max(s,t)+1$, where $s$ and $t$ are the remainders of the division of $a$ and $b$ by $k$, see . Is it true that the latter inequality is, in fact, an equality?

records.name: Algebraic Stories — Degree of the Waring map
records.statement: Calculate the degree of $\widetilde{W}_{k,d}$ for perfect pairs $(k,d)$.

records.name: Algebraic Stories — Ideals of generic forms
records.statement: [Fr\"oberg's Conjecture, 1985] Let $f_1, \dots, f_r$ be generic forms of degrees $d_1, \dots, d_r$, respectively. Then the Hilbert series of the quotient algebra $R = S/(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ is given by $$ \operatorname{Hilb}_R(t)=\left[\frac{\prod_{i=1}^r(1-t^{d_i})}{(1-t)^n}\right]_+. $$ Here $[\sum_{i\ge0}a_iz^i]_+:=\sum_{i\ge0}b_iz^i$, with $b_i=a_i$ if $a_j\ge0$ for all $j\le i$ and $b_i=0$. In other words, $[\sum_{i\ge0}a_iz^i]_+$ is the truncation of a power series at its first non-positive coefficient.

records.name: Algebraic Stories — Hilbert series of generic power ideals.
records.statement: [Fr\"oberg-Iarrobino Conjecture] Given generic linear forms $\ell_1, \ldots, \ell_r$ and a positive integer $d$, let $I$ be the power ideal generated by $\ell_1^d,\ldots,\ell_r^d$. Then the Hilbert function of $R = S/I$ is as in [source label: eq:RALF], except for the cases $(n,r) = (3,7), (3,8), (4,9), (5,14)$ and possibly for $r = n+2$ and $r = n+3$.

records.name: Algebraic Stories — Hilbert series of other classes of ideals
records.statement: For $\mu \neq (d)$, does a generic $\mu$-power ideal have the same Hilbert function as in [source label: eq:RALF]?

records.name: Algebraic Stories — Hilbert series of other classes of ideals
records.statement: [] For generic forms $g_1,\ldots,g_r$ of degree $d>1$, the ideal $(g_1^k,\ldots,g_r^k)$ has the same Hilbert series as the one generated by $r$ generic forms of degree $dk$.

records.name: Algebraic Stories — Lefschetz properties of graded algebras
records.statement: It has been conjectured that each complete intersection $R=S/(f_1,\ldots,f_n)$ satisfies the WLP and also the SLP, see . Does the same hold for $R=S/(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$, with $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ being generic forms, and $r > n$?

records.name: Algebraic Stories — Lefschetz properties of graded algebras
records.statement: When are the WLP and the SLP true for $T_{n,d,k}$?

records.name: Algebraic Stories — Lefschetz properties of graded algebras
records.statement: For $R= S/(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$, where $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ are generic forms, does $R$ satisfy the $\mu$-Lefschetz property for all partitions $\mu$?

records.name: Algebraic Stories — Hilbert functions of fat points.
records.statement: Given a scheme of generic fat points $X \subset \mathbb{P}^{n_1-1}\times\ldots\times \mathbb{P}^{n_t-1}$, what is the multi-graded Hilbert function $\operatorname{Hilb}_{S/I_X}(I)$, for $I \in \mathbb{N}^t$?

records.name: Algebraic Stories — Symbolic powers vs. ordinary powers.
records.statement: For the ideal $I$ of $s$ general points in $\mathbb P^{n-1}$, what is the difference between the Hilbert series of the $m$-th symbolic power and the $m$-th ordinary power?

records.name: Algebraic Stories — Hilbert series of numerical semigroup rings
records.statement: $\mathcal{S}$ is cyclotomic if and only if $k[\mathcal{S}]$ is a complete intersection.

records.name: Algebraic Stories — Non-negative forms
records.statement: Are $B_{n,m}$ and $B'_{n,m}$ finite for any pair $(n,m)$ with even $n$?

records.name: Algebraic Stories — Non-negative forms
records.statement: For any given pair $(n,m)$ with even $n$, $B'_{n,m}=\left(\frac{n}{2}\right)^{m-1}$.

records.name: Algebraic Stories — Non-negative forms
records.statement: Determine $\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{B_{n,3}}{n^2}$.

records.name: Algebraic Stories — Polynomial generation
records.statement: For $n=1$ and given $p$, what are the (lengths of the) possible periods of $\phi$?

records.name: Algebraic Stories — Polynomial generation
records.statement: For $n = 1$ and given $p$, find the minimal positive integer $i$ such that $\psi^i$ is the identity map on the space of polynomials of degree at most $p-1$.

records.name: Algebraic Stories — Exterior algebras
records.statement: Let $f$ be a form of odd degree $d$ in $E$. Is it true that $({\rm Ann}(f))_i = (f)_i$, for $i < (n-d)/2$?

records.name: Algebraic Stories — Exterior algebras
records.statement: Let $f$ and $g$ be generic quadratic forms in $E$ and let $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ be two generic linear forms in $S$. Then the Hilbert series of $E/(f,g)$ is equal to the Hilbert series of $S/(x_1^2,\ldots,x_n^2,\ell_1^2,\ell_2^2)$ and is given by $1 + a(n,1) t + a(n,2) t^2 + \cdots + a(n,s)t^s + \cdots$, where $a(n,s)$ is the number of lattice paths inside the rectangle $(n+2-2s)\times (n+2)$ starting from the bottom-left corner and ending at the top-right corner by using only moves of two types: either $(x,y)\rightarrow (x+1,y+1) \textrm{\ or\ } (x-1,y+1)$.

records.name: Green's conjecture
records.statement: For a non-hyperelliptic algebraic curve, is its Clifford index determined by the extent to which its canonical embedding has linear syzygies?

records.name: Grothendieck–Katz p-curvature conjecture
records.statement: Prove the conjectured local-to-global principle for linear ordinary differential equations known as the Grothendieck–Katz $p$-curvature conjecture.

records.name: Williamson matrix existence problem
records.statement: Determine for which orders Williamson matrices exist; such matrices give a construction of Hadamard matrices.

records.name: Hadamard's maximal determinant problem
records.statement: For each order $n$, determine the largest possible absolute determinant of an $n\times n$ matrix whose entries are all $1$ or $-1$.

records.name: Zariski–Lipman conjecture
records.statement: Let $V$ be a complex algebraic variety with coordinate ring $R$. If the module of derivations of $R$ is free over $R$, must $V$ be smooth?

records.name: Eremenko–Gabrielov secant conjecture
records.statement: Let $m,p\ge 2$, put $d=m+p-1$, and let $F(x)=(1,x,\ldots,x^d)$ be the rational normal curve. For $j=1,\ldots,mp$, let $X_j$ be the $p$-plane spanned by $F(x_{j,1}),\ldots,F(x_{j,p})$, where all $x_{j,k}$ are real and the $mp$ sets of parameters lie in pairwise disjoint intervals. Are all complex $m$-planes meeting every $X_j$ real?

records.name: Geometry of Continued Fractions — Integer trigonometry and IKEA problem
records.statement: Find an integer cosine rule for integer triangles in integer trigonometry.

records.name: Geometry of Continued Fractions — Integer trigonometry and IKEA problem
records.statement: {\bf(IKEA problem.)} Classify all $n$-tuples of LLS-sequences for the angles that form integer $n$-gons.

records.name: Geometry of Continued Fractions — Faces of sails
records.statement: Classify all combinatorial possible types of faces.

records.name: Geometry of Continued Fractions — Faces of sails
records.statement: Classify all empty simplices of dimension $n$ up to lattice congruence.

records.name: Geometry of Continued Fractions — Faces of sails
records.statement: Which $n$-gons are realizable as faces of an $m$-dimensional continued fraction? Here are two essentially geometrically different subcases: ; {\bf Faces at integer distance 1 to the origin:} this is a question of description of integer convex polyhedra that are inscribed to simplices of full dimension in $\r^n$. ; {\bf Faces at integer distance greater than 1 to the origin:} here we have a typical view-obstacle problem, one avoids integer points that are view-obstacles for the corresponding faces.

records.name: Geometry of Continued Fractions — Combinatorial structure of sails
records.statement: Describe all finite two-dimensional sails (and the corresponding continued fractions).

records.name: Geometry of Continued Fractions — Combinatorial structure of sails
records.statement: {\bf (Multidimensional IKEA problem.)} Describe the collections of the sails of the cones for all polytopes of a given combinatorial type.

records.name: Geometry of Continued Fractions — Combinatorial structure of sails
records.statement: {\bf (V. Arnold.)} Does there exist an algorithm to decide whether a given type of fundamental domain is realizable by a periodic continued fraction?

records.name: Geometry of Continued Fractions — Combinatorial structure of sails
records.statement: {\bf (V. Arnold.)} Torus decompositions of integer noncongruent Klein sails are distinct.

records.name: Geometry of Continued Fractions — Combinatorial structure of sails
records.statement: {\bf (V. Arnold.)} Describe all torus decompositions that are realized by periodic two-dimensional continued fractions.

records.name: Geometry of Continued Fractions — Combinatorial structure of sails
records.statement: {\bf (V. Arnold.)} Classify continued fractions that correspond to the same cubic extension of the field of rational numbers.

records.name: Geometry of Continued Fractions — Combinatorial structure of sails
records.statement: Prove the existence of a cone for a single non-periodic combinatorial structure ($n\ge 3$).

records.name: Geometry of Continued Fractions — Sail statistics
records.statement: Find frequencies on $n$-dimensional continued fractions with the highest relative frequencies.

records.name: Geometry of Continued Fractions — Sail statistics
records.statement: For every positive integer constant $C$ there exist only finitely many pairwise integer non-congruent faces with frequencies exceeding $C$.

records.name: Geometry of Continued Fractions — Sail statistics
records.statement: Is that true that sum of all relative frequencies for all possible faces is finite for higher dimensions $(n\ge 3)$?

records.name: Geometry of Continued Fractions — Sail statistics
records.statement: In case of positive answer to the above question find the generalization of the Gauss map and compare the corresponding frequencies of faces with the related frequencies coming from M\"obius geometry.

records.name: Geometry of Continued Fractions — Further open questions
records.statement: Find a natural generalization of the Farey tessellation to higher-dimensional hyperbolic geometry.

records.name: Geometry of Continued Fractions — Further open questions
records.statement: {\bf (Jacobi's last theorem.)} Let $K$ be a totally real cubic number field. Consider arbitrary elements $y$ and $z$ of $K$ such that $0<y,z<1$ (here we assume that $1$, $y$, and $z$ are independent over $\mathbb \q$). Is it true that the Jacobi-Perron algorithm generates an eventually periodic continued fraction with starting data $v=(1,y,z)$.

records.name: Geometry of Continued Fractions — Further open questions
records.statement: Study geometric properties of Markov spectrum.

records.name: Geometry of Continued Fractions — Further open questions
records.statement: Generalize continued fractions to describe 3-bridge knots.

records.name: Some Open Problems in Elasticity — Existence of minimizers
records.statement: Prove the existence of energy minimizers for elastostatics for quasiconvex stored-energy functions $W$ satisfying $W(A)\to\infty$ as $\det A\to0^+$ .

records.name: Some Open Problems in Elasticity — Testing convexity conditions
records.statement: Find useful ways of verifying polyconvexity and quasiconvexity for stored-energy functions arising in anisotropic nonlinear elasticity.

records.name: Some Open Problems in Elasticity — Regularity of minimizers
records.statement: Determine when the minimizer $y^*$ in Theorem 2.1 of the source is smooth.

records.name: Some Open Problems in Elasticity — Lavrentiev phenomena
records.statement: Can the Lavrentiev phenomenon occur for elastostatics under growth conditions ensuring that all finite-energy deformations are continuous?

records.name: Some Open Problems in Elasticity — Weak Euler-Lagrange equations
records.statement: Prove or disprove that, under reasonable growth conditions on $W$, energy minimizers satisfy the weak Euler-Lagrange equations.

records.name: Some Open Problems in Elasticity — A positive Jacobian bound
records.statement: Prove or disprove that, under reasonable growth conditions on $W$, an energy-minimizing deformation satisfies $\det Dy^*(x)\ge\varepsilon>0$.

records.name: Some Open Problems in Elasticity — Smooth self-contact
records.statement: Justify the Ciarlet-Nečas minimization problem, or an appropriate modification, in situations involving smooth self-contact.

records.name: Some Open Problems in Elasticity — Uniqueness of equilibrium
records.statement: Prove or disprove uniqueness of sufficiently smooth equilibrium solutions for pure-displacement problems in homogeneous bodies homeomorphic to a ball when $W$ is strictly polyconvex.

records.name: Some Open Problems in Elasticity — Nonglobal local minimizers
records.statement: Devise general methods for proving the existence of local but nonglobal minimizers and other weak equilibria in nonlinear elastostatics.

records.name: Some Open Problems in Elasticity — Bifurcation theory
records.statement: Develop local and global bifurcation theories for nonlinear elastostatics with mixed displacement-traction boundary conditions.

records.name: Some Open Problems in Elasticity — Variational fracture models
records.statement: Clarify the status of models based on the fracture energy functional (2.31) in the source relative to classical fracture and nonlinear elastostatics.

records.name: Some Open Problems in Elasticity — Global dynamics
records.statement: Prove global existence and uniqueness for suitable initial-boundary-value problems in dynamic nonlinear elasticity.

records.name: Some Open Problems in Elasticity — Qualitative dynamics
records.statement: Develop a qualitative dynamics for dynamic theories of elasticity.

records.name: Some Open Problems in Elasticity — Dynamic stability
records.statement: Develop criteria for dynamic stability and instability of equilibria in nonlinear elasticity.

records.name: Some Open Problems in Elasticity — Atomistic foundations
records.statement: Establish the status of elasticity theory with respect to atomistic models.

records.name: Some Open Problems in Elasticity — Quasiconvexification of energy wells
records.statement: For the set of energy-minimizing gradients $K(\theta)$ defined in the source, determine its quasiconvex hull $K(\theta)^{qc}$ for $\theta\le\theta_c$.

records.name: Some Open Problems in Elasticity — Elastic-crystal free energies
records.statement: For free-energy functions $\psi(A,\theta)$ of elastic crystals, determine boundary conditions under which the minimum is attained and conditions under which it is not.

records.name: Some Open Problems in Elasticity — Dimension reduction
records.statement: Give a rigorous derivation of models of rods, plates, and shells from three-dimensional elasticity as thickness tends to zero.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Topology of integrable systems, Lagrangian fibrations, and their invariants
records.statement: Under which additional assumptions does this principle become a rigorous theorem?

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Topology of integrable systems, Lagrangian fibrations, and their invariants
records.statement: Consider two Lagrangian fibrations $\phi: M^4 \to B$ and $\phi': {M'}^4 \to B'$. Assume that $B$ and $B'$ are affinely equivalent in the sense that there exists an affine diffeomorphism $\psi : B \to B'$. Is it true that under these assumptions the corresponding Lagrangian fibrations are symplectomorphic?

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Topology of integrable systems, Lagrangian fibrations, and their invariants
records.statement: Do local symplectic invariants exist for diffeomorphic degenerate singularities? How many and of what kind are they? This question makes sense even in the simplest case of one-degree-of-freedom systems.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Topology of integrable systems, Lagrangian fibrations, and their invariants
records.statement: Describe the symplectic invariants of stable rank-one singularities described by V. V. Kalashnikov. For such singularities, one of the action variables, say $I_1$, is smooth, and the other $I_2$ is singular. Is it true that $I_1$ and $I_2$ are sufficient for the symplectic classification? Here is an almost equivalent version of this question. Assume that we have two functions $H$ and $F$ that commute with respect to two different symplectic structures $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ and define (in both cases) a stable rank-one singularity described by V. V. Kalashnikov. Assume that the action variables $I_1$ and $I_2$ are the same for $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$. This condition is equivalent to the relation $$ \oint_\gamma \alpha_1 = \oint_\gamma \alpha_2 $$ for any cycle $\gamma$ on any regular fiber $\mathcal L_{f,h}=\{ F=f, H=h\}$ and appropriately chosen $1$-forms $\alpha_i$ such that $d\alpha_i = \omega_i$, $i=1,2$. Is it true that, under these conditions, there exists a smooth map $\psi$ that preserves the functions $F$ and $H$ and such that $\psi^*(\omega_2)=\omega_1$? The source notes that the simplest case is known.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Topology of integrable systems, Lagrangian fibrations, and their invariants
records.statement: Assume that we know explicit formulas for the action variables $I_1,\dots, I_n$ so that we are able to analyse their asymptotic behaviour in a neighbourhood of a singular fiber. Can we recover the topology of this singularity from the asymptotic behaviour (or at least to distinguish between different types of singularities)? For example, we know that, in the case of non-degenerate hyperbolic singularities, the singular part $I_{sing}$ is of the form $h\ln h + \dots$ . Is this property characteristic for non-degenerate hyperbolic singularities? The case of one degree of freedom is understood in .

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Topology of integrable systems, Lagrangian fibrations, and their invariants
records.statement: Describe all topological types of singularities that may appear in algebraically integrable systems with a small ($\leq 3$) number of degrees of freedom, and describe the symplectic invariants of such singularities.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Topology of integrable systems, Lagrangian fibrations, and their invariants
records.statement: [\'{A}. Pelayo] Extend the classification of semitoric systems $F=(J,H)$ in to allow for $F$ having non-degenerate singularities with hyperbolic blocks (a version of this problem was mentioned in various forms in ).

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Topology of integrable systems, Lagrangian fibrations, and their invariants
records.statement: [\'{A}. Pelayo] Consider a compact connected $2n$-dimensional symplectic manifold $M$, endowed with a Hamiltonian $(S^1)^{n-1}$-action; these are called complexity one spaces. Consider an integrable system $f_1,\ldots, f_{n}$ on $M$ where $(f_1,\ldots, f_{n-1}) \colon M \to \mathbb{R}^{n-1}$ is the momentum map of the Hamiltonian $(S^1)^{n-1}$-action. Suppose that the singularities of the integrable system are non-degenerate and also they do not contain hyperbolic blocks. Study how the invariants of the complexity one space are related to the invariants of the semitoric system.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Topology of integrable systems, Lagrangian fibrations, and their invariants
records.statement: [N. T. Zung] Study the topology and geometry of these singular fibers and their small neighbourhoods.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Topology of integrable systems, Lagrangian fibrations, and their invariants
records.statement: [N. T. Zung] Give a clear description of these special singular fibers.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Two-dimensional case.
records.statement: Complete the above table: {\rm (1)} construct new examples of natural Hamiltonian systems on closed two-dimensional surfaces admitting polynomial integrals, describe and, if possible, classify them; {\rm (2)} prove, if possible, nonexistence of such integrals (perhaps under some additional assumptions).

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Two-dimensional case.
records.statement: Construct a natural Hamiltonian system with a nonconstant potential on $S^2$ that admits a nontrivial polynomial integral of degree $5$ and does not admit any nontrivial integrals of smaller degrees.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Polynomial in momenta integrals in higher dimensions.
records.statement: Construct new examples of natural Hamiltonian systems on higher dimensional manifolds which are integrable in the class of integrals polynomial in momenta.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Polynomial in momenta integrals in higher dimensions.
records.statement: Construct stationary axially symmetric 4-dimensional Einstein metrics admitting Killing tensors of higher order.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Polynomial in momenta integrals in higher dimensions.
records.statement: [Gilkey ] In the Riemannian case, is every $1$-homogeneous manifold locally homogeneous?

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Polynomial in momenta integrals in higher dimensions.
records.statement: In a symmetric space, is every Killing tensor a sum of symmetric products of Killing vectors? Equivalently, is it true that the algebra of all polynomial integrals of the geodesic flow in a symmetric space is generated by linear integrals?

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Superintegrable systems
records.statement: {\it Construct a natural Hamiltonian system on the 2-sphere with a nonconstant potential which is superintegrable by integrals of degree $\ge 3$ and admits no nontrivial integral of degree one and two. }

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Superintegrable systems
records.statement: Does there exist a non-conformally flat metric on the sphere $S^n$, $n>2$, whose geodesic flow is maximally superintegrable (in the class of integrals which are polynomial in momenta)?

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Around the Birkhoff conjecture
records.statement: Assume that the exterior of an outer billiard table is foliated by invariant curves. Prove that the table is an ellipse.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Around the Birkhoff conjecture
records.statement: Prove the algebraic version of Birkhoff conjecture for outer billiards in a non-Euclidean surface of constant curvature.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Around the Birkhoff conjecture
records.statement: Prove Conjecture [source label: Descon] it the case that the foliation admits (i) a rational, (ii) an algebraic first integral.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Around the Birkhoff conjecture
records.statement: Is it possible to choose the domain so that the dynamics of the corresponding billiard map are locally (near the 2-periodic orbit) conjugated to the dynamics of the rigid rotation through some angle $\alpha$?

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Geometry of caustics, invariant surfaces, and commuting billiard maps
records.statement: Are there plane billiards, other than ellipses, that possess rational caustics with two different values of the rotation numbers? Same question for outer billiards.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Geometry of caustics, invariant surfaces, and commuting billiard maps
records.statement: Suppose that a billiard table has a sequence of convex caustics with rotation numbers converging to some number $\omega \in (0,1/2)$. Does it imply that the table is an ellipse?

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Geometry of caustics, invariant surfaces, and commuting billiard maps
records.statement: {\rm (M. Bialy)} Are there multi-dimensional convex billiards, other than ellipsoids, having invariant hypersurfaces in the phase space? Same question for multi-dimensional outer billiards.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Geometry of caustics, invariant surfaces, and commuting billiard maps
records.statement: {\rm (A. Glutsyuk, S. Tabachnikov )} Given two nested closed convex hypersurfaces, assume that the billiard transformations on the set of oriented lines that intersect both hypersurfaces commute. Prove that the hypersurfaces are confocal ellipsoids.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Noncommutative integrable maps
records.statement: {\rm (V. Retakh) Establish complete integrability of the noncommutative version of the leapfrog map. Define noncommutative versions of the pentagram map and its higher-dimensional analogs and establish their complete integrability. }

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Bi-Poisson vector spaces
records.statement: Consider the action of $ Aut (V,J)$ on $V$. Describe the partition of $V$ into $ Aut (V,J)$-orbits. More generally, describe the action of $ Aut (V,J)$ on the set of all $k$-dimensional subspaces $U\subset V$ (orbits, invariants, fixed points). Notice that fixed points of this action (i.e., $ Aut (V,J)$-invariant subspaces) are important, as they correspond to well-defined (co)distributions in the context of Poisson pencils.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Bi-Poisson vector spaces
records.statement: Find necessary and sufficient conditions for the bi-Lagrangian Grassmannian $LG(V,J)$ to be a smooth algebraic variety. Describe the partition of $LG(V,J)$ into $Aut (V,J)$-orbits.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Bi-Poisson vector spaces
records.statement: Do bi-integrable systems exist for each algebraic type?

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Argument shift method and Jordan-Kronecker invariants of Lie algebras
records.statement: Compute the Jordan--Kronecker invariants for the most interesting classes of Lie algebras, and particularly for the following {\/\rm(}a{\/\rm)} semidirect sums $\mathfrak{g}+_{\rho}V$, where $\rho: \mathfrak{g} \rightarrow End(V)$ is a representation of a semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ and $V$ is assumed to be commutative; {\/\rm(}b{\/\rm)} Borel subalgebras of simple Lie algebras; {\/\rm(}c{\/\rm)} parabolic subalgebras of simple Lie algebras; {\/\rm(}d{\/\rm)} the centralisers of singular elements $a\in\mathfrak{g}$, where $\mathfrak{g}$ is simple; {\/\rm(}e{\/\rm)} Lie algebras of small dimensions.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Argument shift method and Jordan-Kronecker invariants of Lie algebras
records.statement: Are there any restrictions on the algebraic type of the pencils $\mathcal{A}_{x+\lambda a}$? Which algebraic types can be realised by means of an appropriately chosen Lie algebra{\/\rm?}

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Argument shift method and Jordan-Kronecker invariants of Lie algebras
records.statement: Study examples of ``quadratic $+$ linear'' Poisson pencils. Compute their algebraic types and construct complete families of polynomials in bi-involution for such pencils.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Argument shift method and Jordan-Kronecker invariants of Lie algebras
records.statement: Is it true that for any quadratic Poisson bracket (defined on a vector space), there exists a polynomial integrable system?

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Nijenhuis operators: singular points and global properties
records.statement: Describe closed manifolds $M$ which admit Nijenhuis operators $L(x)$ that are algebraically regular at each point $x\in M$.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Nijenhuis operators: singular points and global properties
records.statement: Let us fix a certain algebraic type of a linear operator, i.e., its Segre characteristic (see above). Does there exist a Nijenhuis operator $L$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with the following two properties: ; $L$ has compact support; ; in a certain domain $U\subset \mathbb{R}^n$, the algebraic type of $L$ does not change and coincides with the given one? More generally, find necessary and sufficient conditions, in terms of the Segre characteristic, for the existence of a Nijenhuis operator in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with the above properties.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Nijenhuis operators: singular points and global properties
records.statement: Construct real analytic examples of Nijenhuis operators on closed two-dimensional surfaces whose eigenvalues are real and generically distinct.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Nijenhuis operators: singular points and global properties
records.statement: Describe all the functions $f(x,y)$ of two variables defined in a neighbourhood of $(0,0)\in\mathbb{R}^2$ such that ; $f_y(0,0)\not\equiv 0$; ; $f_y(0,0)=0$; ; $\frac{f_x(x-f_x) - f}{f_y} $ is locally smooth (or, more precisely, extends up to a locally smooth function).

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Nijenhuis operators: singular points and global properties
records.statement: Consider a smooth map $\Phi=(\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_n): U(0) \to \mathbb{R}^n$, where $U(0)$ is a neighbourhood of the origin $0\in \mathbb{R}^n$. We assume that $0$ is a singular point of $\Phi$, that is, $\operatorname{rank} d\Phi(0) < n$, but almost all points $x\in U(0)$ are regular. Describe those maps $\Phi$ for which all the components of the Nijenhuis operator $L(x)$ defined by [source label: eq10.1] are smooth functions (notice that $L$ is well defined and smooth at regular points of $\Phi$, and we are interested in necessary and sufficient conditions for $L$ to be smoothly extendable onto the whole neighbourhood $U(0)$).

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Nijenhuis operators: singular points and global properties
records.statement: Describe/classify the collections of algebraically independent homogeneous polynomials $\sigma_1, \dots, \sigma_n$, $\deg \sigma_k = k$, in $n$ variables $x_1,\dots, x_n$ with the required property.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Nijenhuis operators: singular points and global properties
records.statement: Describe the structure of singularities of $\Phi=(\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_n): M \to \mathbb{R}^n$ in terms of the singular points of the recursion operator $R$, their linearisations, and the corresponding left-symmetric algebras. What are sufficient and/or necessary conditions for such singularities to be non-degenerate (in the sense of Eliasson )? Notice that, in this case, the algebraic type of $R$ is rather special: at a generic point, $R$ is semisimple, but each of its eigenvalues has multiplicity 2.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Poisson geometry and action-angle variables
records.statement: Extend the action-angle theorem in a neighbourhood of a Liouville torus at singular points of the Poisson structure.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Poisson geometry and action-angle variables
records.statement: Extend the action-angle theorem in a neighbourhood of a Liouville torus at singular points of the Poisson structure for splittable integrable systems.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Poisson geometry and action-angle variables
records.statement: Determine obstructions to the global existence of action-angle coordinates on regular Poisson manifolds.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Poisson geometry and action-angle variables
records.statement: Which foliations with affine leaves can be described as the image of the moment map?

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Poisson geometry and action-angle variables
records.statement: Consider a Poisson manifold $M$ of even dimension such that it is symplectic on a dense set $U\subset M$. Assume that $M$ is endowed with a toric action which is Hamiltonian on $U$. Is there an analog of Delzant theorem for the image of the moment map?

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Poisson geometry and action-angle variables
records.statement: [S. V\ u Ng{\d o}c] Find natural examples of integrable systems in classical mechanics with non-trivial Duistermaat--Chern classes.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Integrability and Quantisation
records.statement: Assume that a classical integrable system $(p_1,\dots,p_n)$ is given on $M$. Does there exist a quantum integrable system $(P_1,\dots,P_n)$ such that $p_j=\sigma(P_j)$?

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Integrability and Quantisation
records.statement: [S. V\ u Ng{\d o}c] Given a set of semiclassical operators that verify conditions [source label: item:self-adjoint ] and [source label: item:commute] above, can one detect the independence axiom [source label: item:independent] in a purely spectral way? More precisely, can one tell from asymptotics of joint eigenvalues or eigenfunctions of $(P_1,\dots,P_n)$ that the principal symbols are almost everywhere independent?

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Integrability and Quantisation
records.statement: [S. V\ u Ng{\d o}c] Write Bohr-Sommerfeld rules for focus-focus singularities in Berezin-Toeplitz quantisation.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Integrability and Quantisation
records.statement: [S. V\ u Ng{\d o}c] Define (and detect) the quantum Chern class.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Integrability and Quantisation
records.statement: [S. V\ u Ng{\d o}c] Compute the Taylor series invariant of semitoric systems directly from the spectrum ``at'' the focus-focus critical value.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Integrability and Quantisation
records.statement: [S. V\ u Ng{\d o}c] Is the singular Bohr-Sommerfeld formal power series in $\hbar$ a spectral invariant?

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Integrability and Quantisation
records.statement: [\'{A}. Pelayo] What information about the principal symbols $f_1,\ldots, f_n$ of a quantum integrable system $T_{1,\hbar},\ldots, T_{n,\hbar}$ can be detected from their semiclasical joint spectrum? For instance, suppose that we know that a certain object -- say, an integer $z$, or a matrix $A$ -- is a symplectic invariant of $(M, \omega, f_1,\ldots, f_n)$. Can we compute this object from the semiclassical joint spectrum?

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Integrability and Quantisation
records.statement: [\'{A}. Pelayo] Can one detect from the joint spectrum of a quantum integrable system $T_{1,\hbar},\ldots, T_{n,\hbar}$ that a singularity is degenerate?

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Integrability and Quantisation
records.statement: [\'{A}. Pelayo] Can one make progress in counting the number of fixed points by studying the spectrum of the quantisation of $\mu \colon M \to S^1$?

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Quantum integrability for polynomial in momenta integrals
records.statement: What are necessary and/or sufficient conditions on a metric $g$ such that every polynomial integral of its geodesic flow is quantisable?

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Quantum integrability for polynomial in momenta integrals
records.statement: Quantise the Mischenko-Fomenko algebra $\mathcal F_a \subset \mathcal P(\goth g)$ for an arbitrary finite-dimensional Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ {\/\rm(}or find an obstruction to quantisation{\/\rm)}.

records.name: Open Problems in Integrable Systems — Integrable systems and geometric quantisation
records.statement: [Miranda-Presas-Solha ] Modify this scheme to get finite dimensional representation spaces for focus-focus and hyperbolic singularities that still capture the invariants of the corresponding integrable systems and their singularities.

records.name: Problems Around Polynomials — Conjecture 1
records.statement: [ Maxwell, seems bad, no tools] For any system of $N$ isolated fixed point charges in $\mathbb{R}^3$, the number of points of equilibrium (assumed finite) of the created electrostatic field $$E(\bar x)=\sum_{i=1}^N\frac{\xi_i(\bar x-\bar x_i)}{|\bar x-\bar x_i|^3},$$ is at most $(N-1)^2$. Here $\xi_i$ is a charge placed at $\bar x_i\in \mathbb{R}^3$ and $\bar x\in \mathbb{R}^3$ is a variable vector.

records.name: Problems Around Polynomials — Conjecture 2
records.statement: [folklore, very irritating] For any set of charges of the same sign in $\mathbb{R}^n$, the set of its points of equilibrium is finite.

records.name: Problems Around Polynomials — Conjecture 3
records.statement: [A. Gabrielov, D. Novikov, B. Sh., seems good, but no progress] Let $(x_1,y_1),(x_2,y_2),\dots, (x_N,y_N)$ be a collection of points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, $\xi_1, \xi_2, \dots , \xi_N$ be arbitrary real charges and $\alpha\ge 1/2$. Then the rational univariate function $$\Psi(x)=\sum_{i=1}^N\frac{\xi_i}{((x-x_i)^2+y_i^2)^{\alpha}},\; x\in \mathbb{R},$$ has at most $N$ local maxima on the whole real line.

records.name: Problems Around Polynomials — Problem 1
records.statement: [B. Sh., looks bad, but very important] Does there exist an upper bound for the number of real roots valid for all non-trivial solutions of all equations [source label: eq:triv] in $\Omega_k$?

records.name: Problems Around Polynomials — Problem 2
records.statement: [D. Khavinson, I. Itenberg, B. Sh., apparently bad] Find the maximal possible number $\#(2k, l)$ of isolated zeros for real non-negative polynomials of degree $2k$ in $l$ variables.

records.name: Problems Around Polynomials — Problem 3
records.statement: [G. Ottaviani, B. Sh., seems good] Find the maximal possible number $\widetilde\#(2k, l)$ of isolated zeros for real non-negative polynomials of degree $2k$ in $l$ variables which are representable as the sums of squares of real polynomials of degree at most $k$.

records.name: Problems Around Polynomials — Conjecture 4
records.statement: [G. Ottaviani, B. Sh., seems good] For any number of variables, $\widetilde\#(2k,l)=k^l$.

records.name: Problems Around Polynomials — Problem 4
records.statement: [S. Fisk, seems bad, see , p. 575] Given a pair of real polynomials $(p,q),$ give restrictions on the location of the roots of $p+iq$ in terms of the location of the roots of $p$ and $q$.

records.name: Problems Around Polynomials — Conjecture 5
records.statement: [P. Br\"anden, I. Krasikov, B. Sh., hopefully good, see ] A difference operator $T(p(x))=a_0p(x)+a_1p(x-1)+\cdots+a_kp(x-k)$ with constant coefficients preserves the set of real-rooted polynomials of degree at most $m$ whose mesh is at least $1$ if and only if the polynomial $T((x)_m)$ is real-rooted and has mesh at least one. Here $(x)_m=x(x-1)(x-2)\dots (x-m+1)$ is the $m$-th Pochhammer polynomial.

records.name: Problems Around Polynomials — Conjecture 6
records.statement: If $p$ and $q$ are real-rooted polynomials of degree at most $d$ and of mesh $\geq 1$, then so is $p \bullet q$.

records.name: Problems Around Polynomials — Problem 5
records.statement: [seems bad, but might be ugly] For a given sign pattern $\sigma,$ which admissible pairs $(pos,neg)$ are realizable by polynomials whose signs of coefficients are given by $\sigma$?

records.name: Problems Around Polynomials — Conjecture 7
records.statement: [J. Forsg\aa rd, V. Kostov, B. Sh, hopefully good, see ] For an arbitrary sign pattern $\sigma$, the only type of pairs $(pos,neg)$ which can be non-realizable has either $pos$ or $neg$ vanishing. In other words, for any sign pattern $\sigma$, each pair $(pos,neg)$ satisfying [source label: stand] with positive $pos$ and $neg$ is realizable.

records.name: Problems Around Polynomials — Conjecture 8
records.statement: [J. Forsg\aa rd, B. Sh., seems good, see ] Let $f(z) = \sum_{k=0}^n a_k z^k$ be a polynomial with positive coefficients, and consider the related (weighted) tropical polynomial \[ f_{trop}(x) =\max_{k}\left(\Log(a_k)+k x + \Log{n\choose k}\right). \] Then the number of real zeros of $f(z)$ does not exceed the number of points in the tropical variety defined by $f_{trop}$, i.e. the number of corners of the continuous piecewise-linear function $ f_{trop}(x),\; x\in \mathbb{R}$.

records.name: Problems Around Polynomials — Conjecture 9
records.statement: [J. Forsg\aa rd, B. Sh., seems good, see ] Let $f(z) = \sum_{k=0}^n a_k z^k$ be a polynomial with positive coefficients. Consider the differences \[ \tilde c_k = (k+1)a_k^2 - k a_{k-1}a_{k+1}, \] where $a_{-1} = a_{n+1} = 0$. Let $0=k_1 < k_2 < \dots < k_m = n$ be the sequence of indices such that $\tilde c_{k_i}$ is positive, and let $v(f)$ be the number of changes in the sequence $\{k_i \mod 2\}_{i=0}^m$. Then the number of real zeros of $f(z)$ does not exceed $v(f)$.

records.name: Problems Around Polynomials — Conjecture 10
records.statement: [J. Forsg\aa rd, B. Sh., seems good, see ]] Let $f(z) = \sum_{k=0}^n a_k z^k$ be a polynomial with positive coefficients. Consider the differences \[ c_k = a_k^2 - a_{k-1}a_{k+1}, \] where $a_{-1} = a_{n+1} = 0$. Let $0=k_1 < k_2 < \dots < k_m = n$ be the sequence of indices such that $c_{k_i}$ is non-negative, and let $v(f)$ be the number of changes in the sequence $\{k_i \mod 2\}_{i=0}^m$. Then the number of real zeros of $f(z)$ does not exceed $v(f)$.

records.name: Problems Around Polynomials — Problem 6
records.statement: [V. Kostov, B. Sh., looks ugly, see ] What additional restrictions besides [source label: eq:1] exist on configurations $\mathcal A_{f}=\{x^{(i)}_{l}\}$ coming from real-rooted polynomial-like functions of a given degree $n$? Or, more ambitiously, given a configuration $\mathcal A=\{x^{(i)}_{l}\vert\; i=0,\ldots,n-1;\,l=1,\ldots n-i\}$ of $\binom {n+1} 2$ real numbers satisfying standard Rolle's restrictions, is it possible to determine if there exists a real-rooted polynomial-like $f$ of degree $n$ such that $\mathcal A_{f}=\mathcal A$?

records.name: Problems Around Polynomials — Problem 7
records.statement: [looks ugly] What symbolic sequences can occur for strictly real-rooted polynomials of degree $n$?

records.name: Problems Around Polynomials — Conjecture 11
records.statement: [B. Sh., seems good] For any real polynomial $p(x)$ of degree $k$ with simple real zeros, $$ \#_{r}\left[(k-1)(p'(x))^2-kp(x)p''(x)\right] \le \#_{nr}p(x), $$ i.e. "Hawaiian`` conjecture holds for $G_1(x)$ as well.

records.name: Problems Around Polynomials — Conjecture 12
records.statement: [B. Sh] For any real polynomial $p(x)$ of even degree, $$ \#_{r}\left[(k-1)(p'(x))^2-kp(x)p''(x)\right] + \#_{r}p(x)>0, $$

records.name: Problems Around Polynomials — Conjecture 13
records.statement: [B. Sh] For any degree $k$ polynomial $p(x)$ with real coefficients, $$ \#_{r}P_{i}(x) \le \min\{{\deg{P_i(x)},k}\}. $$

records.name: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 1.2
records.statement: How big can the set of Valiron deficiencies be for functions in the plane? It is known that $$ N(r,a)=T(r,f)+O\big(T(r,f)^{\frac{1}{2}+\varepsilon}\big) $$ as $r\to\infty$, for all $a$ outside a set of capacity zero (see Nevanlinna . In the case $R<+\infty$ this is more or less best-possible, but in the plane we only know from an example of Valiron that the corresponding set of $a$ can be non-countably infinite. It is also not known whether ([source label: 1.3]) can be sharpened.

records.name: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 1.3
records.statement: If $f(z)$ is meromorphic of finite order $\rho$ and $\sum\delta(a,f)=2$, it is conjectured that $\rho=n/2$, where $n$ is an integer and $n\geq 2$, and all the deficiencies are rational. F. Nevanlinna has proved this result on the condition that $f(z)$ has no multiple values, so that $n(r,a)=\overline{n}(r,a)$ for every $a$ (see also R. Nevanlinna ).

records.name: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 1.4
records.statement: Let $f(z)$ be an entire function of finite order $\rho$, and let $n_1(r,a)$ denote the number of simple zeros of the equation $f(z)=a$. If \[n_1(r,a)=O(r^c),\hspace{1cm} n_1(r,b)=O(r^c),\hspace{1cm} \text{ as } r\to\infty,\] where $a\neq b, c<\rho$, is it true that $\rho$ is an integral multiple of $\frac{1}{2}$? More strongly, is this result true if $\Theta(a)=\frac{1}{2}=\Theta(b)$? (For a somewhat weaker result in this direction, see Gol'dberg and Tairova .)

records.name: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 1.5
records.statement: Under what conditions can $\sum\delta(a,f)$ be nearly $2$ for an entire function of finite order $\rho$? Pfluger proved that if $\sum\delta(a,f)=2$, then (see Hayman ) $\rho$ is a positive integer $q$, the lower order $\lambda$ is such that $\lambda=\rho$ and all the deficiencies are integral multiplicities of $1/q$. If further \[\sum\delta(a,f)>2-\varepsilon(\lambda),\] where $\varepsilon(\lambda)$ is a positive quantity depending on $\lambda$, then Edrei and Fuchs (, ) proved that these results remain true `nearly', in the sense that there exist `large' deficiencies which are nearly positive integral multiplicities of $1/q$, and whose sum of deficiencies is `nearly' $2$. Can there be a finite or infinite number of small deficiences as well in this case?

records.name: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 1.6
records.statement: Arakelyan has proved that, given $\rho>\frac{1}{2}$ and a countable set $E$, there exists an entire function $f(z)$ of order $\rho$, for which all the points of $E$ are deficient. Can $E$ be the precise set of deficiencies of $f$ in the sense that $f$ has no other deficient values? It is also conjectured that if the $a_n$ are deficient values for an entire function of finite order, then \[\sum\big(\log[1/\delta(a_n,f)]\big)^{-1}<+\infty.\] (N. U. Arakelyan)

records.name: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 1.7
records.statement: If $f(z)$ is an entire function of finite order $\rho$ which is not an integer, it is known that (see Pfluger and Hayman ), \[\sum \delta(a,f)\leq 2-K(\rho)\] where $K(\rho)$ is a positive quantity depending on $\rho$. What is the best possible value for $K(\rho)$? Edrei and Fuchs conjectured (see also Hayman ) that if $q$ is the integral part of $\rho$, and if $q\geq1$, then \[K(\rho)=\frac{|\sin(\pi\rho)|}{q+|\sin(\pi\rho)|},\hspace{1cm}q\leq\rho<q+\frac{1}{2},\] \[K(\rho)=\frac{|\sin(\pi\rho)|}{q+1}, \hspace{1cm}q+\frac{1}{2}\leq\rho<q+1.\] This result would be sharp. If $\rho\leq\frac{1}{2}$, there are no deficient values, so that $K(\rho)=1$. If $\frac{1}{2}<\rho<1$, Pfluger proved that $K(\rho)=\sin(\pi\rho)$. See also Hayman .

records.name: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 1.8
records.statement: Following the notation in Problem 1.7, if $f(z)$ is meromorphic in the plane of order $\rho$, it is conjectured by Pfluger , that for $a\neq b$ \[\limsup_{r\to \infty}\frac{N(r,a)+N(r,b)}{T(r,f)}\geq K(\rho).\] This is known to be true for $0<\rho\leq1$. If equality holds in the above inequality, it is conjectured that $f(z)$ has regular growth, i.e. $\rho=\lambda$.

records.name: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 1.10
