Prove that, up to the natural equivalences, the possibilities are exhausted by: $g$ periodic; $g(z+T)=g(z)+K$ with $f$ $K$-periodic; $g$ quadratic; or $g=P\circ h$ with $P$ quadratic, $h(z+T)=h(z)+K$, and $f\circ P$ $K$-periodic.

records.name: Zeros and one-points on three rays
records.statement: Does there exist an entire function whose zeros lie on the positive ray and whose $1$-points lie on two rays making angles $\pm\alpha$ with it, for some $\alpha\in(\pi/3,\pi/2)\setminus\{2\pi/5\}$?

records.name: A fifth-root functional equation
records.statement: For $\omega=e^{2\pi i/5}$, is an entire solution of $$f(\omega z)f(\omega^{-1}z)=f(z)-1$$ unique up to rotation of the variable $z$?

records.name: Levin's derivative-zero problem
records.statement: Let $f$ be entire and suppose every zero of every derivative $f^{(n)}$, $n\ge0$, lies in the closed lower half-plane. Must $f$ lie in the compact-open closure of polynomials whose zeros lie in that half-plane, or have one of the forms $ce^{az}$ and $c(e^{ibz}-e^{id})$, where $c,a\in\mathbb C$ and $b,d\in\mathbb R$?

records.name: Exceptional directions in Gross's theorem
records.statement: For a local inverse germ $\phi_z$ of a meromorphic function $f$ at a noncritical value $w=f(z)$, Gross's theorem gives analytic continuation along almost every ray from $w$. Sharpen 'almost every': what is the smallest possible exceptional set theorem, in capacity, dimension, or another natural sense?

records.name: Gross property of implicit functions
records.statement: Let $F$ be entire in two variables and let a holomorphic germ $\phi$ satisfy $F(z,\phi(z))=0$ near a nonsingular point. Must $\phi$ admit analytic continuation along almost every ray from its base point, as inverse germs of entire functions do?

records.name: Locally constant logarithmic potentials
records.statement: Let $\mu$ be a positive plane measure with $\mu(\{|z|\le r\})\le cr^\alpha$ for some $0<\alpha<1/2$. Can its logarithmic potential $$u(z)=\int\log\left|1-\frac z\zeta\right|\,d\mu(\zeta)$$ be locally constant on an open set meeting every circle centered at the origin?

records.name: Small components of subharmonic level sets
records.statement: Let subharmonic functions $u_k$ on the unit square converge uniformly to $u(x,y)=x$. If $D_k=\{u_k<0\}$ and $D_k^*$ is the component containing $-1/2$, can $D_k\setminus D_k^*$ meet every horizontal segment $[-1+it,1+it]$, $-1<t<1$?

records.name: Decay of separated subharmonic level components
records.statement: Let $u$ be subharmonic on $1<|z|<2$, and let pairwise disjoint open sets $D_k$ be unions of components of $\{u<0\}$. Suppose that for every $r\in(1,2)$, $$\int_{\{\theta:re^{i\theta}\in D_k\}}u(re^{i\theta})\,d\theta\le-\delta_k.$$ Determine the possible decay rate of $\delta_k$, closing the gap between known exponentially decaying examples and the universal bound $\sum_k\delta_k^\alpha<\infty$ for some $\alpha<1/3$.

records.name: Equilibrium for infinitely many positive masses
records.statement: Let positive masses $a_k$ be placed at a discrete set $x_k\in\mathbb R^n$ and suppose $\sum_k a_k/|x_k|^{n-1}<\infty$, so that $$F(x)=\sum_k\frac{a_k(x_k-x)}{|x-x_k|^n}$$ converges. Must $F$ vanish somewhere?

records.name: Goldberg's constant
records.statement: Let $f$ be holomorphic in the unit disk with exactly one simple zero $z_0$ and two $1$-points $z_1,z_2$, counted with multiplicity. Determine the largest universal lower bound $A_2$ for the radius of the smallest hyperbolic disk containing $z_0,z_1,z_2$, and determine whether an extremal function must have a double $1$-point.

records.name: Two one-points in the unit disk
records.statement: Let $f$ be holomorphic in the unit disk, with $f(0)=0$, $f'(0)\ne0$, no other zeros, and exactly two solutions $z_1,z_2$ of $f(z)=1$, counted with multiplicity. Determine the minimum of $\max(|z_1|,|z_2|)$ and the maximum of $|f'(0)|$.

records.name: Real two-one-point extremals
records.statement: Solve the two-one-point extremal problem for real holomorphic $f$: determine the minimum of $\max(|z_1|,|z_2|)$ and maximum of $|f'(0)|$ when $f(0)=0$, $0$ is its only zero, and $z_1,z_2$ are its two $1$-points.

records.name: Belgian Chocolate constant
records.statement: Let $f$ be real and holomorphic in the unit disk, with one simple zero at $0$ and two simple $1$-points at $\pm ia$. Determine the minimum possible value of $a$.

records.name: Rational Goldberg extremals
records.statement: For rational functions of each fixed degree, determine the analogues of Goldberg's constant and the unit-disk zero/one-point extremal quantities, and characterize their extremal functions.

records.name: Littlewood constants $ lpha$ and $ eta$
records.statement: For $\phi(n)=\sup_{\deg p=n}\int_{|z|<1}|p'|/(1+|p|^2)\,dm$, let $\alpha=\limsup\log\phi(n)/\log n$. For a regular compact set $E$, define $\beta_E$ from the growth of lengths of Green-function level curves, and let $\beta=\sup_E\beta_E$ over connected $E$. Is there a connection between $\alpha$ and $\beta$, and in particular is $\alpha=\beta$?

records.name: Better estimates for Littlewood constants
records.statement: Obtain better rigorous estimates for the Littlewood exponents $\alpha$, $\beta$, and for $\sup_c P_c$, where $P_c$ is the pressure for the hyperbolic quadratic polynomial $p_c(z)=z^2+c$ corresponding to the potential $|(p_c^n)'|^{-1}$.

records.name: Extremality of iterated quadratic polynomials
records.statement: Are the iterates $p_c^n$ of hyperbolic quadratic polynomials extremal, or nearly extremal, for the Littlewood exponent $\alpha$ governing mean spherical derivatives of polynomials?

records.name: Maximizing quadratic pressure
records.statement: For which parameters $c$ is the pressure $P_c$ of the hyperbolic quadratic polynomial $p_c(z)=z^2+c$, for the potential $|(p_c^n)'|^{-1}$, close to or equal to its supremum?

records.name: Carleson–Jones quarter conjecture
records.statement: For a regular connected compact plane set $E$, let $\beta_E=\limsup_{\varepsilon\to0}\log l(\varepsilon)/(-\log\varepsilon)$, where $l(\varepsilon)$ is the length of the Green-function level curve $G=\varepsilon$, and let $\beta=\sup_E\beta_E$. Is $\beta=1/4$?

records.name: Connectedness of extremal Green level sets
records.statement: If the definition of $\sup_E\beta_E$ is extended from connected regular compact plane sets to all regular compact sets, is the supremum attained on connected sets?

records.name: Finiteness of Newtonian equilibrium points
records.statement: For finitely many positive charges $a_k$ at points $x_k\in\mathbb R^3$, is the critical set of $u(x)=\sum_{k=1}^n a_k/|x-x_k|$ always finite?

records.name: Number of Newtonian equilibrium points
records.statement: If the critical set of $u(x)=\sum_{k=1}^n a_k/|x-x_k|$ for positive point charges in $\mathbb R^3$ is finite, how many points can it contain? In particular, is Maxwell's bound $(n-1)^2$ valid?

records.name: Maximum length of a polynomial lemniscate
records.statement: For a monic polynomial $p$ of degree $d$, determine the maximum length of the lemniscate $E(p)=\{z:|p(z)|=1\}$. Is the extremal asymptotically $p(z)=z^d+1$, giving maximum length $2d+o(1)$ as $d\to\infty$?

records.name: Rectangular-lattice Landau extremal
records.statement: For the rectangular lattice $\Lambda=\{an+ibm:n,m\in\mathbb Z\}$ with $a^2+b^2=1$ and $a\in(0,1)$, let $f_a:\mathbb D\to\mathbb C\setminus\Lambda$ be the universal cover normalized by $f_a(0)=(a+ib)/2$ and $f_a'(0)>0$. Maximize $f_a'(0)$ over $a\in(0,1)$.

records.name: Median inequality for three subharmonic functions
records.statement: Let $u_1,u_2,u_3$ be subharmonic in the plane with $u_j(0)=0$, and let $v_1\le v_2\le v_3$ be their pointwise increasing rearrangement. Put $I(r,v)=\int_0^{2\pi}v(re^{i\theta})\,d\theta$ and $B(r)=\max_{|z|=r}v_3(z)$. Prove $$\sup_{r>0}\frac{I(r,v_2)}{B(r)}\ge0,$$ or the stronger assertion with $\limsup_{r\to0}$.

records.name: Defect relation for points in $\mathbb P^2$
records.statement: Let $f:\mathbb C\to\mathbb P^2$ be linearly nondegenerate and let $\delta(a,f)$ be the Nevanlinna deficiency of a point $a\in\mathbb P^2$. Prove that for every system of points in general position, $$\sum_a\delta(a,f)\le1.$$

records.name: Holomorphic curves with bounded spherical derivative
records.statement: Let $f:\mathbb C\to\mathbb P^n$ be holomorphic with spherical derivative $\|f'\|(z)=O(|z|^\sigma)$ for some $\sigma>-1$, and let $a_1,\ldots,a_q$ be hyperplanes in general position not covering $f(\mathbb C)$. Prove $$\sum_{j=1}^qN(r,a_j,f)\ge(q+1-n)T(r,f)+O(r^{\sigma+1}).$$

records.name: Modified Cartan conjecture
records.statement: For $p\ge3$, let $V(D)$ consist of zero-free holomorphic vectors $(f_1,\ldots,f_p)$ on $D$ with $\sum f_j=0$, and use the source's definition of a $C$-class for an infinite sequence. Prove that every infinite sequence in $V(D(1))$ has a subsequence for which $\{1,\ldots,p\}$ is a union of disjoint $C$-classes on $D(R_p)$ for some $R_p>0$ depending only on $p$. Can $R_p$ be chosen independently of $p$, and what is the geometric interpretation?

records.name: Few inflection points of holomorphic curves
records.statement: Let $f=(f_0,\ldots,f_n)$ be a linearly nondegenerate holomorphic curve, let $T(r,f)$ have finite lower order $\lambda$, and let $N_1(r)$ be the averaged counting function of zeros of its Wronskian. If $N_1(r)=o(T(r,f))$, prove that $\lambda$ is rational and that $\lim_{r\to\infty}\log T(r,f)/\log r$ exists.

records.name: Generic static-output stabilizability
records.statement: For real matrices $A\in\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times n}$, $B\in\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times p}$, and $C\in\operatorname{Mat}_{m\times n}$ with $n=mp$, determine for which pairs $(m,p)$ a generic system $\dot x=Ax+Bu$, $y=Cx$ admits a real static output feedback $u=Ky$ such that every eigenvalue of $A+BKC$ lies in the open left half-plane.

records.name: Conjugate one-points in the unit disk
records.statement: Let $f$ be holomorphic in the unit disk with a simple zero at $0$, exactly two simple $1$-points at $a$ and $\overline a$, and no other zeros or $1$-points. Determine the minimum possible $|a|$ and the extremal function; in particular, is the minimum the conjectured covering constant $c\approx0.0505468$?

records.name: Symmetric one-points in the unit disk
records.statement: Let $f$ be holomorphic in the unit disk with a simple zero at $0$, exactly two simple $1$-points at $b$ and $-b$, and no other zeros or $1$-points. Determine the minimum $b_0$ of $|b|$ and the extremal function. Is $b_0>c$, where $c\approx0.0505468$ is the conjectured constant in the conjugate-one-point problem?

records.name: Unfolding convex polytopes
records.statement: Does every three-dimensional convex polytope have a non-self-intersecting edge unfolding? Does a minimum spanning tree of the dual edge graph, with a natural dihedral-angle weighting, always specify such an unfolding? Does every convex polytope have a creased unfolding that cannot be refolded into a different convex polytope?

records.name: Acute triangulation of the cube
records.statement: Does the three-dimensional cube admit a triangulation into tetrahedra all of whose dihedral angles are acute?

records.name: Degenerate facets of polytopes
records.statement: A facet of a $d$-polytope is degenerate if it has more than $d$ vertices. Determine the maximum number of degenerate facets of an $n$-vertex $d$-polytope; in particular, can a four-polytope have at least $2n$ degenerate facets?

records.name: Faces of intricate polytopes
records.statement: Determine the maximum total number of faces of a $d$-dimensional convex polytope with $n$ vertices and $n$ facets. In dimension four, do such fat-lattice polytopes have superlinear complexity? Are joins of polygons asymptotically optimal in dimensions at least six?

records.name: Point-hyperplane incidences
records.statement: Given $n$ points and $m$ hyperplanes in $\mathbb R^d$ whose incidence graph contains no $K_{s,t}$, determine the maximum number of incidences. Of special interest is the case $n=m$ and $s=t=d$, where the known bounds are far apart.

records.name: Halving lines and k-sets
records.statement: For an $n$-point planar set, determine the maximum number of halving lines. More generally, determine the maximum number of $k$-sets, subsets obtained by intersecting the point set with a half-plane, and extend the sharp bounds to higher-dimensional halving hyperplanes.

records.name: Tangent pairs of pseudocircles
records.statement: For $n$ pseudocircles in general position, determine the maximum number of tangent pairs and the maximum number of digon cells. Determine whether the worst-case bounds for tangencies and digons are equal for genuine circles.

records.name: Medial surfaces and Voronoi diagrams of lines
records.statement: Determine the worst-case complexity of the medial surface and of an offset surface of an $n$-feature polyhedron, and of the Voronoi diagram of $n$ lines in three-space. The known upper bounds are superquadratic while quadratic lower-bound constructions are known.

records.name: Forced convex subsets
records.statement: Determine the exact Erdős–Szekeres number $f(n)$, the least number of planar points in general position forcing a convex $n$-gon. Also determine sharp bounds for empty convex polygons; the source's former empty-hexagon subproblem has since been resolved.

records.name: Visibility complex of disjoint unit spheres
records.statement: Determine the combinatorial complexity of the visibility complex of $n$ pairwise disjoint unit spheres in three-dimensional space.

records.name: Minimum-area triangles
records.statement: Given $n$ planar points, find a subquadratic algorithm for the minimum-area triangle or prove a quadratic lower bound in a suitable computation model. More generally, close the gap for minimum-volume simplices in fixed dimension.

records.name: Complex collinearities
records.statement: Given $n$ points in $\mathbb C^2$, determine in quadratic time whether three lie on a complex line, or prove a quadratic lower bound; the known algorithm takes $O(n^2\log n)$ time.

records.name: Extreme points
records.statement: For fixed $d>3$, determine whether every point of an $n$-point set in $\mathbb R^d$ is a convex-hull vertex faster than the best known near-$n^{2\lfloor d/2\rfloor/(\lfloor d/2\rfloor+1)}$ algorithm, or prove a matching lower bound.

records.name: A dynamic-programming interval problem
records.statement: Given a sorted list of $n$ real numbers, find for every $1\le k\le n$ the shortest interval containing exactly $k$ entries. Find a subquadratic algorithm or prove a superlinear lower bound.

records.name: Shortest paths in line arrangements
records.statement: Given lines in the plane and two vertices $s,t$ of their arrangement, find a subquadratic algorithm for the shortest $s$-$t$ path along arrangement edges, or prove a quadratic lower bound.

records.name: Straight skeleton of a simple polygon
records.statement: Is there a near-linear-time algorithm to construct the straight skeleton of a simple polygon? Determine the optimal complexity, including for polygons with reflex angles bounded away from zero.

records.name: Crashing motorcycles efficiently
records.statement: Given motorcycles moving simultaneously along fixed rays and crashing upon reaching another track, determine the motorcycle graph in near-linear time. Can one decide which motorcycles survive, or the fate of a single motorcycle, faster? Prove sharper lower bounds.

records.name: Klee's measure problem
records.statement: Determine the optimal complexity of computing the volume of the union of axis-aligned boxes in fixed dimension at least three. In particular, is there a near-linear three-dimensional algorithm or an $\Omega(n^{3/2})$ lower bound, and can fat or equal-sized boxes be handled faster?

records.name: Generating random simple polygons
records.statement: Given a planar point set $P$, sample uniformly from the simple polygons with vertex set $P$ in polynomial time, or determine the complexity of counting them. Determine the maximum possible number of such polygons and analogous bounds for triangulations, paths, and simple spanning trees.

records.name: Building convex polytopes
records.statement: Develop exact polynomial-time algorithms for the constructive forms of Aleksandrov's, Cauchy's, Minkowski's, Steinitz's, and Koebe's polytope-realization theorems: reconstruct a convex polytope from a net, facets with adjacency, area-weighted normals, or a 3-connected planar edge graph.

records.name: Antipodes of symmetric convex bodies
records.statement: On a centrally symmetric convex body, must every pair of points at maximum intrinsic surface distance be antipodal? Resolve this even for rectangular boxes.

records.name: Bounded-degree triangulations
records.statement: Can every convex polytope be triangulated so that every vertex degree, or every edge degree, is bounded by a constant or by a polylogarithmic function of the input size?

records.name: Chromatic number of the plane
records.statement: Determine the least number of colors needed to color the Euclidean plane so that points at unit distance receive different colors.

records.name: Covering points by congruent rectangles
records.statement: Given a finite planar point set and a prescribed rectangle, approximate efficiently the minimum number of congruent copies of the rectangle needed to cover the points; determine the best achievable approximation ratio.

records.name: Triangulating a hypercube
records.statement: Determine the minimum number of $d$-simplices needed to triangulate the $d$-dimensional cube, and its asymptotic growth with $d$.

records.name: Embedding the hyperbolic plane
records.statement: Does the hyperbolic plane admit a smooth isometric immersion into $\mathbb R^4$? More generally, determine the least Euclidean dimension for such an immersion under natural regularity assumptions.

records.name: Rationality of Hermite constants
records.statement: Are the Hermite constants associated with densest lattice sphere packings always rational? Determine their arithmetic nature in dimensions where the exact value is unknown.

records.name: Integer-distance point sets
records.statement: Do there exist seven planar points in general position—no three collinear and no four concyclic—such that every pairwise distance is an integer?

records.name: Mirrored-room illumination
records.statement: Given a polygonal room with perfectly reflecting sides and a point light source, characterize when every point of the room is illuminated. In particular, can a polygonal mirrored room contain a dark region?

records.name: Odd rep-tiling by a 14-omino
records.statement: Can the $3\times6$ rectangle with a $2\times2$ corner removed tile a rectangle using an odd number of congruent copies?

records.name: Prince Rupert ratio for tetrahedra
records.statement: What is the largest possible ratio between the sum of edge lengths of a tetrahedron that can pass through or fit inside another tetrahedron and the sum of edge lengths of the containing tetrahedron?

records.name: Perfect rational triangles
records.statement: Does there exist a nondegenerate triangle whose side lengths, three medians, three altitudes, and area are all rational?

records.name: Comparing sums of square roots
records.statement: Can sums of square roots of integers be compared in polynomial time on a Turing machine? Equivalently, obtain effective polynomial bit bounds for a nonzero difference of two such sums, with consequences for placing Euclidean optimization problems in NP.

records.name: Packing reciprocal rectangles in a square
records.statement: For every positive integer $k$, let $R_k$ be a $1/k$ by $1/(k+1)$ rectangle. Can the entire collection $(R_k)_{k\ge1}$ be packed without overlap into the unit square?

records.name: Triangulations with many distinct areas
records.statement: Find the largest function $t(n)$ such that every convex $n$-gon has a triangulation containing at least $t(n)$ distinct triangle areas; also determine the lattice-vertex special case.

records.name: Log-concave measures
records.statement: For Ollivier's coarse Ricci curvature, smooth uniformly strictly log-concave measures on $\mathbb{R}^N$ have positive curvature. What can be said for a general log-concave measure? In particular, analyze a convex body equipped with Brownian motion conditioned not to leave it.

records.name: Finsler manifolds
records.statement: The space $\mathbb{R}^N$ equipped with an $L^p$ norm has zero coarse Ricci curvature. Does this observation yield useful results for Finsler manifolds?

records.name: Nilpotent groups
records.statement: What is the coarse Ricci curvature of discrete or continuous nilpotent groups? In particular, for the natural random walk generated by $a,b$ on the discrete Heisenberg group $\langle a,b,c\mid ac=ca,bc=cb,[a,b]=c\rangle$, does the negative small-scale curvature tend to zero at larger scales?

records.name: Continuous-time
records.statement: For a continuous-time Markov semigroup $(m_x^t)$ define $$\kappa(x,y)=\liminf_{t\to0^+}\frac1t\frac{d(x,y)-T_1(m_x^t,m_y^t)}{d(x,y)}.$$ Under a natural assumption such as non-explosion, does this definition give the standard elementary consequences of positive coarse Ricci curvature for both diffusions and jump processes, even with an unbounded generator? Is positivity of $\kappa$ enough to imply non-explosion?

records.name: Non-reversible spectral gap
records.statement: Positive coarse Ricci curvature gives a spectral-gap bound for reversible random walks and on finite spaces. What spectral-radius, operator-norm, or Poincaré-inequality bounds hold in the non-reversible case? Can finite-space approximation be used?

records.name: Sharp Lichnerowicz theorem
records.statement: For the $\varepsilon$-step random walk on an $N$-dimensional Riemannian manifold, the coarse-curvature argument gives the lower spectral-gap estimate $\inf\operatorname{Ric}$, whereas the sharp Lichnerowicz estimate is $\frac{N}{N-1}\inf\operatorname{Ric}$. Can the missing directional information be incorporated, for example through reflection couplings, to recover the sharp theorem?

records.name: Non-constant curvature
records.statement: Can estimates based on a uniform lower bound for coarse Ricci curvature be extended to spaces where curvature has only a controlled number of negative or zero values? Can curvature of iterated kernels be related to an average curvature along random-walk trajectories, perhaps by large deviations?

records.name: Isoperimetric profile and curvature at infinity
records.statement: Suppose the global infimum of coarse Ricci curvature is zero, while its infimum on every finite-radius ball about an origin is positive. Is there a systematic relation between the rate at which curvature tends to zero at infinity and the isoperimetric profile? Analyze, for example, the $M/M/k$ queue.

records.name: Local assumptions for concentration
records.statement: Can the bounded-local-variance hypothesis used for concentration under positive coarse Ricci curvature be relaxed while retaining estimates governed by the actual local variance, including estimates that remain bounded in a continuous-time limit when transition probabilities become small?

records.name: Functional inequalities
records.statement: Can concentration consequences of positive coarse Ricci curvature be formulated as transportation or other functional inequalities? In a coarse setting, determine a suitable version that permits non-Gaussian tails at small measures or scales, perhaps using a quadratic-then-linear transport cost.

records.name: Sturm–Lott–Villani definition
records.statement: What is the relationship, if any, between Ollivier coarse Ricci curvature and the Sturm–Lott–Villani displacement-convexity notion, including its $CD(K,N)$ form, especially for discrete spaces?

records.name: Bishop–Gromov theorem
records.statement: Is there an analogue, for positive coarse Ricci curvature, of the Bishop–Gromov theorem or the isoperimetric form of the Gromov–Lévy theorem? Identify suitable comparison spaces or formulate a version that also captures discrete examples such as the cube.

records.name: Entropy decay
records.statement: Does positive coarse Ricci curvature imply a useful exponential entropy-decay statement analogous to that obtained from logarithmic Sobolev inequalities, while correctly treating examples such as binomial distributions on the cube?

records.name: Discrete Ricci flow
records.statement: Let the metric of a Markov space evolve by $$\frac{d}{dt}d(x,y)=-\kappa(x,y)d(x,y),$$ where $\kappa$ is computed from the current metric, with either a fixed or suitably evolving transition kernel. What can be said about the existence, behavior, and limiting geometry of this discrete Ricci flow?

records.name: Positive curvature up to delta
records.statement: Define curvature up to $\delta$ by $$T_1(m_x,m_y)\leq(1-\kappa(x,y))d(x,y)+\delta.$$ Which theorems for positive coarse Ricci curvature extend to this setting? Can one choose a discrete subset and redefine its random walk naturally so that it has genuinely positive Ricci curvature?

records.name: Discrete sectional curvature
records.statement: Replace the $T_1$ distance in the coarse-Ricci definition by $L^\infty$ transport, requiring a coupling that moves every point by at most $d(x,y)$. Does this define a useful discrete sectional curvature, can it be assigned a numerical value, and is it related to Alexandrov sectional curvature?

records.name: Discrete scalar curvature
records.statement: Define a scalar-curvature candidate by $S(x)=\int\kappa(x,y)\,dm_x(y)$, possibly with a distance-dependent weight. Does this quantity have useful geometric or probabilistic properties, such as controlling volume growth?

records.name: L2 Bonnet–Myers and dimension
records.statement: Under the strengthened transport estimate $$T_1(m_x^{*t},m_{x'}^{*t'})\leq e^{-\kappa\min(t,t')}d(x,x')+C\frac{(\sqrt t-\sqrt{t'})^2}{2d(x,x')},$$ the diameter is at most $\pi\sqrt{C/(2\kappa)}$. Is $C$ intrinsically related to a dimension, in particular to the parameter $n$ in the Bakry–Émery condition $CD(K,n)$?

records.name: Alexandrov spaces
records.statement: Do spaces with positive sectional curvature in the sense of Alexandrov have positive coarse Ricci curvature for a natural choice of Markov kernels? Can this be proved by manifold approximation or parallel transport in Alexandrov spaces?

records.name: Expanders
records.statement: Does there exist a family of bounded-degree expander graphs, with spectral gap bounded away from zero and diameter tending to infinity, whose coarse Ricci curvature is non-negative?

records.name: Permutation groups
records.statement: For permutation groups with the transposition random walk, coarse Ricci curvature is positive but gives concentration of the wrong order. Can this discrepancy be explained by hyperbolic-like properties of permutation groups or by a mixture of positive and negative curvature behavior?

records.name: Classification of Finite Metric Spaces and Combinatorics of Convex Polytopes
records.statement: Let $(X,\rho)$ be a finite metric space. Its fundamental polytope $R_{X,\rho}$ is the convex hull of the vectors $e_{x,y}=(\delta_x-\delta_y)/\rho(x,y)$ for distinct $x,y\in X$; its combinatorial structure is the isomorphism class of the face poset of $R_{X,\rho}$. (1) Express this combinatorial structure, including the $f$-vector, directly in terms of linear inequalities in the metric $\rho$. (2) For $|X|=n$, estimate the number of combinatorial structures and its asymptotic growth, especially the number of open (generic) types. (3) Give sufficient conditions for two finite metric spaces to have the same combinatorial structure. (4) Describe the combinatorial types of finite metric spaces that embed isometrically into a Euclidean or Hilbert space; do all combinatorial types occur? (5) Is the stratification of the cone of distance matrices into combinatorial types universal, or are there restrictions on the topological types of its open components?

records.name: N-body problem
records.statement: What is the measure of the set of initial conditions of the Newtonian $N$-body problem that lead to global solutions? The complementary set of singularities splits into collision and non-collision singularities.

records.name: Fractal caustics
records.statement: Are there geodesic flows or Birkhoff billiards with fractal caustics? More specifically, for every $1\leq s<2$, is there a caustic of a convex billiard with Hausdorff dimension $s$; and for every $s\geq1$, is there a Riemannian manifold $M$ and a point whose caustic has Hausdorff dimension $s$?

records.name: Conjugacy
records.statement: If two Birkhoff billiard maps $T_1$ and $T_2$ satisfy $T_1=ST_2S^{-1}$ for a homeomorphism $S$, must their tables be similar? Relatedly, can one hear the shape of a real-analytic convex drum?

records.name: Periodic orbits
records.statement: (a) Is the set of $n$-periodic orbits of a smooth strictly convex Birkhoff billiard nowhere dense for every $n$? (b) Does every polygonal Birkhoff billiard have a periodic orbit?

records.name: Free gas in a moving container
records.statement: Does a free gas coupled to a convex rigid container by conservation of momentum converge weakly to equilibrium, with the container—which moves only by translation—coming to rest?

records.name: Kolmogorov mixing-torus problem
records.statement: Does there exist a Hamiltonian system with a smooth invariant torus on which the induced dynamics is mixing? No such mixing can occur on a two-dimensional torus; the question asks especially for examples in higher dimensions.

records.name: The good, the bad, and the ugly
records.statement: For a Hamiltonian system, call the good set the maximal invariant subset on which the invariant Liouville measure is almost periodic; call the bad set the Pesin set on which the invariant measure has a positive Lyapunov exponent; and call the ugly set the complement of their union. Is there an example in which the ugly set has positive measure?

records.name: Mañé's last theorem
records.statement: In the space of area-preserving $C^1$ diffeomorphisms of a compact manifold, is it generic that the dynamics is either hyperbolic or has zero Lyapunov exponents?

records.name: Calogero–Moser–Vlasov
records.statement: For the infinite-dimensional Calogero–Moser system, in which particles on the real line interact through the inverse-square potential, does the dynamics exist? Is it integrable in the sense that every invariant measure gives rise to almost-periodic dynamics?

records.name: Mather theory near integrable systems
records.statement: Are there quasiperiodic global minimals for metrics on the torus that are close to a flat three-dimensional torus? Here a geodesic is a global minimal if the segment between any two of its points is a minimizing geodesic.

records.name: Order of mixing
records.statement: Let $p$ be a prime for which $$f(u_1,u_2)=1+u_1u_2+u_1^2u_2+u_1^3u_2+u_1^4+u_2^2+u_1^4u_2^2$$ is irreducible, and consider the algebraic $\mathbb{Z}^2$-action associated to $\mathbb{Z}[u_1^{\pm1},u_2^{\pm1}]/\langle p,f\rangle$. Its exact order $M$ of mixing satisfies $3\leq M<7$. What is $M$?

records.name: Mixing of all orders
records.statement: For $\mathbb{Z}^d$-actions by automorphisms of a connected group, mixing actions are mixing of all orders. Can this result be proved using simpler ideas from dynamics, without the known Diophantine estimates?

records.name: Analogues of Pesin theory
records.statement: Is there an analogue of Pesin theory for suitably defined smooth maps of the objects that arise naturally in algebraic dynamical systems—compact sets locally resembling a manifold times a Cantor set, or totally disconnected compact sets? Can any algebraic $\mathbb{Z}^d$-systems with $d>1$ be perturbed in a meaningful way?

records.name: Typical group automorphisms
records.statement: Choose a random subset $Q$ of the primes by independently retaining each prime with probability $1/2$. Is it almost surely true that $$\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\log(2^n-1)\prod_{p\in Q}|2^n-1|_p=\log 2?$$

records.name: Entropy values and Lehmer's problem
records.statement: Given $\varepsilon>0$, does there exist a polynomial $f(x)=\prod_{i=1}^d(x-\alpha_i)\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ whose logarithmic Mahler measure $$m(f)=\sum_{i:\,|\alpha_i|>1}\log|\alpha_i|$$ satisfies $0<m(f)<\varepsilon$?

records.name: Entropy and Deligne periods
records.statement: Let $\log_p:\mathbb{C}_p^*\to\mathbb{C}_p$ be the branch of the $p$-adic logarithm with $\log_p(p)=0$, and let $T_\lambda:x\mapsto\lambda x$ on $\mathbb{Q}_p$. Is there a meaningful entropy-like invariant $h_p$, for example invariant under topological conjugacy, such that $h_p(T_\lambda)=\log_p\lambda$?

records.name: Pingree open problems — Hochman problem 1
records.statement: Let $X=\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ and $Y=\{y\in\{0,1,2\}^{\mathbb{Z}}:y_i\neq y_{i+1}\}$. Both are mixing shifts of finite type with entropy $\log2$, but they are not isomorphic. If $\operatorname{Per}(X)$ and $\operatorname{Per}(Y)$ denote their periodic points, are $X\setminus\operatorname{Per}(X)$ and $Y\setminus\operatorname{Per}(Y)$ topologically conjugate?

records.name: Pingree open problems — Hochman problem 2
records.statement: Let $T:[0,1)\to[0,1)$ be the doubling map $x\mapsto2x\pmod1$, and let $\mu$ be an ergodic measure for $T$ with $0<h(\mu)<1$. Call $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ non-singular for $\mu$ if there is a Borel set $A$ such that $\mu|_A$ and $(f\mu)|_A$ are not mutually singular. Which affine maps $f(x)=ax+b$ are non-singular for $\mu$?

records.name: Pingree open problems — Petersen tail-field problem 1
records.statement: Let $A=\{0,1,\ldots,d-1\}$ and let $\sigma$ be the shift on $A^{\mathbb{Z}}$. Define $(v_n(x))_i=\#\{0\leq j\leq n:x_j=i\}$ and $(w_n(x))_i=\#\{0\leq j\leq n:x_{-j}=i\}$. Put $\mathcal{F}_n^+=\bigcap_{k\geq n}\mathcal{B}(v_n,v_{n+1},\ldots)$, $\mathcal{F}^+=\bigcap_{n\geq0}\mathcal{F}_n^+$, and define $\mathcal{F}^-$ analogously using the $w_n$. Is $\mathcal{F}^+=\mathcal{F}^-$?

records.name: Pingree open problems — Petersen tail-field problem 2
records.statement: With $\mathcal{F}^+$ and $\mathcal{F}^-$ defined from the forward and backward symbol-count tail fields on the full shift $A^{\mathbb{Z}}$, if $\mathcal{F}^+\neq\mathcal{F}^-$, is it nevertheless true that $\mathcal{F}^+$ is trivial if and only if $\mathcal{F}^-$ is trivial?

records.name: Pingree open problems — Ledrappier problem 1
records.statement: Let $M$ be a compact Riemannian manifold of constant negative curvature and $(g_t)_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$ its geodesic flow. Does there exist a probability measure $\mu$ invariant under the time-one map $g_1$ but not under the full flow $(g_t)_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$?

records.name: Pingree open problems — Thouvenot problem
records.statement: Let $(M,T)$ be a smooth map on a manifold with a good symbolic cover: a mixing shift of finite type factors onto $(M,T)$ and is injective on a set of full measure for every invariant probability measure. Let $f\in C^1(M)$ (or smoother), and let $(X,(T_t)_{t\in\mathbb{R}})$ be the flow under $f$. Can every ergodic measure-preserving system with entropy less than $h(X,T_1)$ be realized as an invariant measure for $(X,T_1)$?

records.name: Pingree open problems — Boyle problem 1
records.statement: Characterize mixing shifts of finite type up to topological orbit equivalence.

records.name: Pingree open problems — Boyle problem 2
records.statement: Let $S$ and $T$ be subshifts. If $S$ is a mixing shift of finite type and $T$ is topologically orbit equivalent to $S$, must $T$ also be a mixing shift of finite type?

records.name: Periods of Pseudo-Integrable Billiards
records.statement: Consider billiard tables formed by two concentric semicircles joined by two line segments. Consider trajectories with a fixed circle, concentric with the boundary semicircles, as caustic, and with rotation numbers $\rho_1$ and $\rho_2$ relative to the two semicircles. Are these trajectories periodic, and what periods are possible for given $\rho_1$ and $\rho_2$?

records.name: Little shift equivalence conjecture
records.statement: If a nonnegative integer matrix $A$ has a unique, simple, nonzero eigenvalue $n$, prove that $A$ is strong shift equivalent over $\mathbb Z_+$ to the $1\times1$ matrix $[n]$.

records.name: Classify shifts of finite type
records.statement: Classify shifts of finite type up to topological conjugacy; in particular, give a decision procedure determining whether two nonnegative integer matrices define conjugate shifts.

records.name: Range of the dimension representation
records.statement: Given a mixing shift of finite type $S_A$, determine the range of the dimension representation $\operatorname{Aut}(S_A)\to\operatorname{Aut}(G_A)$.

records.name: Positive rational shift equivalence
records.statement: If positive square matrices $A,B$ are shift equivalent over $\mathbb Q_+$, prove that they are strong shift equivalent over $\mathbb Q_+$.

records.name: Spectral conjecture
records.statement: Let $S\subset\mathbb R$ be a unital subring. Prove that a tuple $\Lambda=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_k)$ is the nonzero spectrum of a primitive matrix over $S$ exactly when it satisfies the Perron, Galois, and nonnegative net-trace conditions stated in the source.

records.name: Generalized spectral conjecture
records.statement: Let $S\subset\mathbb R$ be a unital subring and let $A$ be a square matrix over $S$ whose nonzero spectrum satisfies the spectral-conjecture conditions. Prove that $A$ is strong shift equivalent over $S$ to a primitive matrix.

records.name: Equal-entropy factors conjecture
records.statement: Let $A,B$ be irreducible integer matrices of the same spectral radius. Suppose $\operatorname{tr}(A^n)>0$ implies $\operatorname{tr}(B^n)>0$ for every $n$, and the dimension module of $B$ is a quotient of a closed submodule of that of $A$. Prove that the shift $S_B$ is a factor of $S_A$.

records.name: Factor maps between sofic shifts
records.statement: For sofic shifts $S,T$ with $h(S)\ge h(T)$, give necessary and sufficient conditions for a factor map from $S$ onto $T$. The most fundamental unequal-entropy transitive case has been solved, but the general problem remains.

records.name: Good finitary conjecture
records.statement: Prove that two mixing Markov shifts admit a magic-word isomorphism exactly when they have the same beta function, the same ratio group $\Delta$, and the same canonical generator of the weights quotient group $\Gamma/\Delta$.

records.name: Stochastic zeta functions
records.statement: Characterize the functions that occur as stochastic zeta functions of mixing Markov shifts.

records.name: Beta functions
records.statement: Characterize the functions that occur as beta functions of mixing Markov shifts.

records.name: Expansive directions of two-dimensional SFTs
records.statement: For a $\mathbb Z^2$ shift of finite type $\alpha$, characterize the possible sets $E_1(\alpha)$ of expansive directions, especially under the assumption that $\alpha^{\boldsymbol n}$ is an SFT for some $\boldsymbol n$. The unrestricted first subquestion has since been solved; retain the constrained classification problem.

records.name: Expansive components
records.statement: Suppose a $\mathbb Z^2$ action $\alpha$ has $\alpha^{\boldsymbol n}$ an SFT for some $\boldsymbol n$. Can $\alpha$ have infinitely many expansive components? Can an expansive component have a boundary on a line of irrational slope?

records.name: Commuting expansive automorphisms
records.statement: If $S$ is an expansive automorphism of an irreducible shift of finite type, must $S$ itself be a shift of finite type?

records.name: One-sided full-shift automorphisms
records.statement: Prove that every expansive automorphism of a one-sided full shift is topologically conjugate to a two-sided full shift.

records.name: Commuting powers conjecture
records.statement: If $S$ and $T$ are mixing shifts of finite type, prove that $S^i$ and $T^j$ can commute for all sufficiently large integers $i,j$.

records.name: Furstenberg times-p-times-q problem
records.statement: For multiplicatively independent integers $p,q>1$, can there exist a nonatomic Borel probability measure on the circle, other than Haar measure, that is jointly invariant under $x\mapsto px\pmod1$ and $x\mapsto qx\pmod1$?

records.name: Full-support invariant measures
records.statement: For the symbolic system $X$ constructed in Section 14 of the source from a commuting pair of full-shift endomorphisms, is Haar measure its only invariant ergodic Borel probability measure with full support?

records.name: Invariant measures and subsystems
records.statement: Determine all shift-invariant Borel probability measures and all subsystems of the symbolic system $X$ constructed in Section 14 of the source from the Furstenberg commuting-endomorphism problem.

records.name: Equal-entropy SFT covers
records.statement: For $d>1$, must every $\mathbb Z^d$ sofic shift be a factor of a $\mathbb Z^d$ shift of finite type having the same entropy?

records.name: Equal-entropy subcovers
records.statement: For $d>1$, if a continuous factor map sends a $\mathbb Z^d$ SFT $X$ onto a sofic shift $Y$, must $X$ contain a sofic subshift $W$ with $h(W)=h(Y)$ and image $Y$?

records.name: Stable cellular-automaton limit sets
records.statement: Characterize the stable limit sets of one-dimensional cellular automata.

records.name: Extension of a block code I
records.statement: Let $T$ be a mixing sofic shift with a receptive fixed point. When is there a block code $f:T\to T$ and an SFT $T'\supset T$ such that $f(T')\subset T$?

records.name: Extension of a block code II
records.statement: Let $f$ be a surjective block code from a mixing sofic shift $T$ to itself. When does there exist an SFT $T'\supset T$ such that $f(T')\subset T$?

records.name: Bernoulli factors of group shifts
records.statement: Does every nonabelian $\mathbb Z^d$ group shift factor algebraically onto a Bernoulli group shift?

records.name: Weak algebraic equivalence
records.statement: Is every nonabelian $\mathbb Z^d$ group shift weakly algebraically equivalent to a Bernoulli group shift?

records.name: Classify group shifts
records.statement: Classify group shifts up to topological conjugacy, especially abelian group shifts with completely positive entropy.

records.name: Markov random fields and Bernoulli shifts
records.statement: If a translation-invariant Markov random field $\mu$ on a shift is the unique Markov random field, even without assuming translation invariance, with its conditional probabilities, must the measured shift be isomorphic to a Bernoulli shift?

records.name: Finitary images of IID processes
records.statement: If a $\mathbb Z^d$ SFT has a unique measure of maximal entropy and that measure is Bernoulli, must an i.i.d. process map finitarily onto it?

records.name: Decidability problems in symbolic dynamics
records.statement: Determine whether algorithms exist to: decide conjugacy of two SFTs; decide conjugacy of two two-sided or one-sided sofic shifts; compute the expansive component generated by an expansive SFT automorphism; and decide, for a surjective block code of a full shift, whether it has a continuous right inverse.

records.name: Embedding one-sided subshifts
records.statement: Let $T$ be a mixing one-sided SFT and $S$ a subshift with $h(S)<h(T)$. Give useful necessary and sufficient conditions for $S$ to be isomorphic to a subshift of $T$.

records.name: Embedding under a preimage bound
records.statement: Let $S$ be a one-sided subshift and $T$ the full one-sided shift on $N$ symbols, with $h(S)<\log N$, and suppose no point of $S$ has more than $N$ preimages. Must $S$ be isomorphic to a subshift of $T$?

records.name: Classify one-sided sofic shifts
records.statement: Classify one-sided sofic shifts up to topological conjugacy.

records.name: Equivalence of canonical covers
records.statement: Give a procedure deciding whether two canonical left-resolving irreducible covers of a one-sided irreducible SFT are related by an automorphism carrying one quotient relation to the other.

records.name: Automorphism groups of full shifts
records.statement: Are the groups $\operatorname{Aut}(\sigma_2)$ and $\operatorname{Aut}(\sigma_3)$ isomorphic?

records.name: Virtual FOG conjecture
records.statement: For a mixing SFT $S$, let $\operatorname{Aut}_0(S)$ be the inert automorphisms and $F_0(S)$ its finite-order-generated subgroup. Prove that $\operatorname{Aut}_0(S)/F_0(S)$ is finite.

records.name: Amenable Cantor actions
records.statement: Is every minimal action of a countable amenable group on the Cantor set topologically orbit equivalent to a $\mathbb Z$ action?

records.name: Orbit equivalence and ordered cohomology
records.statement: Classify irreducible SFTs up to topological orbit equivalence; characterize and classify their unital ordered cohomology groups; determine when winding and standard orders agree; and decide whether every subshift orbit-equivalent to an irreducible SFT is itself an SFT.

records.name: Infinite symbolic-extension entropy
records.statement: Can a $C^r$ diffeomorphism of a compact Riemannian manifold have infinite symbolic-extension entropy?

records.name: Entropy structures
records.statement: For each $1\le r\le\infty$, characterize the entropy structures that can occur for $C^r$ diffeomorphisms of compact Riemannian manifolds.

records.name: Periodic points of cellular automata
records.statement: Must every surjective $d$-dimensional cellular automaton have dense periodic points? Must its jointly spatially and temporally periodic points be dense? Are its minimal subsystems dense?

records.name: Jointly periodic points in one dimension
records.statement: Prove that the jointly periodic points of every surjective one-dimensional cellular automaton are dense.

records.name: Growth of jointly periodic points I
records.statement: For a surjective one-dimensional cellular automaton $f$ on the full $N$-shift, let $\nu(f,S_N)$ be the limsup exponential growth rate of points that are spatially fixed by a power of the shift and periodic under $f$. Must $\nu(f,S_N)>1$?

records.name: Growth of jointly periodic points II
records.statement: With $\nu(f,S_N)$ defined as in Question 25.3, must every surjective one-dimensional cellular automaton satisfy $\nu(f,S_N)\ge\sqrt N$?

records.name: Sparse jointly periodic points
records.statement: Prove that for some $N>1$ there is a surjective one-dimensional cellular automaton $f$ with $\nu(f,S_N)<N$.

records.name: Periodic and finite configurations
records.statement: For a $d$-dimensional cellular automaton with $d\ge2$, let $f_P$ and $f_F$ be its restrictions to spatially periodic and finite configurations. Does injectivity of $f_P$ imply surjectivity of $f_F$? Does surjectivity of $f_F$ imply surjectivity of $f_P$? Does surjectivity of $f$ imply surjectivity of $f_P$?

records.name: Surjunctive groups
records.statement: Characterize the countable groups $G$ for which every injective $G$-equivariant cellular automaton on $A^G$, for every finite alphabet $A$, is surjective.

records.name: Salem beta-transformations
records.statement: If $\beta$ is a Salem number, prove that the periodic points of the beta-transformation $x\mapsto\beta x\pmod1$ are exactly $\mathbb Q\cap[0,1)$.

records.name: Adler's renewal question
records.statement: Is every irreducible sofic shift topologically conjugate to a renewal shift?

records.name: Classify sofic shifts
records.statement: Classify two-sided sofic shifts up to topological conjugacy.

records.name: K-groups of canonical matrix systems
records.statement: Which pairs of abelian groups occur as $K_0(M,I)$ and $K_1(M,I)$ for a canonical matrix system of a subshift?

records.name: Flow equivalence of subshifts
records.statement: Classify subshifts up to flow equivalence.

records.name: Pisot substitution conjecture
records.statement: Prove that the substitutive shift of every irreducible Pisot substitution has pure discrete spectrum.

records.name: Nivat's conjecture
records.statement: Let $x\in A^{\mathbb Z^2}$ and let $N_x(n_1,n_2)$ be the number of distinct $n_1\times n_2$ rectangular patterns in $x$. If $N_x(n_1,n_2)\le n_1n_2$ for some positive $n_1,n_2$, prove that $x$ is periodic.

records.name: Low degree rigid systems
records.statement: Consider the planar cubic rigid systems $$\begin{cases}\dot x=-y+x(a+bx+cy+dx^2+exy),\\ \dot y=x+y(a+bx+cy+dx^2+exy).\end{cases}$$ Is $2$ the maximum number of limit cycles?

records.name: Systems with homogeneous components I
records.statement: Is $(n+m)/2$ the maximum number of limit cycles of $$\dot x=P_n(x,y),\qquad \dot y=Q_m(x,y),$$ where $n\neq m$ and $P_n,Q_m$ are homogeneous polynomials of odd degrees $n,m$, respectively?

records.name: Systems with homogeneous components II
records.statement: (i) For the cubic family $$\begin{cases}\dot x=ax+by,\\ \dot y=cx^3+dx^2y+exy^2+fy^3,\end{cases}$$ is $2$ the maximum number of limit cycles? (ii) If it is true, give a simple proof of uniqueness of the limit cycle for $$\begin{cases}\dot x=y,\\ \dot y=-x^3+dx^2y+y^3.\end{cases}$$

records.name: Low-degree classical Liénard systems
records.statement: For the classical polynomial Liénard system $$\dot x=y-F(x),\qquad \dot y=-x,$$ let $\operatorname{Lie}(n)$ be the maximum number of limit cycles when $F$ has degree $n$. Find proofs using Dulac functions that $\operatorname{Lie}(3)=1$ and $\operatorname{Lie}(4)=1$.

records.name: Periodic Riccati differential equations
records.statement: For a general $T$-periodic Riccati equation $$\frac{dx}{dt}=A_2(t)x^2+A_1(t)x+A_0(t),$$ give effective criteria determining whether it has a continuum of periodic solutions or exactly $2$, $1$, or $0$ limit cycles.

records.name: Trigonometric Abel differential equations I
records.statement: For $$\frac{dx}{dt}=(a_0+a_1\sin t+a_2\cos t)x^3+(b_0+b_1\sin t+b_2\cos t)x^2,$$ is $3$ the maximum number of $2\pi$-periodic limit cycles?

records.name: Trigonometric Abel differential equations II
records.statement: Given integers $p>q\geq2$ and $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$, find the maximum number of $2\pi$-periodic limit cycles of $$\frac{dx}{dt}=A_m(t)x^p+B_n(t)x^q,$$ where $A_m$ and $B_n$ are $2\pi$-trigonometric polynomials of degrees $m$ and $n$.

records.name: A new Hilbert sixteenth-type problem
records.statement: Let $\mathcal M_m$ be the family of planar polynomial vector fields that are linear combinations of $m$ distinct monomial vector fields $(x^{n_j}y^{k_j},0)$ or $(0,x^{n_j}y^{k_j})$, and let $\mathcal H^M[m]$ be their maximum possible number of limit cycles. (i) Find upper and lower bounds for $\mathcal H^M[m]$. (ii) Find the least $m$ for which a planar polynomial differential system with $m$ monomials has at least $m+1$ limit cycles.

records.name: A second-order differential equation
records.statement: Let $f$ be a continuous, nonzero, $T$-periodic function and let $p>0$. Find necessary and sufficient conditions on $f$ for the existence of positive $T$-periodic solutions of $x^p(t)x''(t)=f(t)$.

records.name: Number of centers
records.statement: Determine the maximum number $\mathcal{C}_n$ of centers for planar polynomial differential systems of degree $n\geq4$.

records.name: Periodic rational difference equations
records.statement: Consider $$x_{n+k}=\frac{A_0+A_1x_n+\cdots+A_kx_{n+k-1}}{B_0+B_1x_n+\cdots+B_kx_{n+k-1}},$$ where the coefficients are nonnegative, $\sum A_i,\sum B_i>0$, and $A_1^2+B_1^2\ne0$. Call it $p$-periodic if every positive initial condition generates a sequence of least common period $p$. Apart from rescaling and index-dilation equivalents of $$x_{n+1}=x_n,\quad x_{n+1}=1/x_n,\quad x_{n+2}=x_{n+1}/x_n,\quad x_{n+2}=(1+x_{n+1})/x_n,$$ and $$x_{n+3}=(1+x_{n+1}+x_{n+2})/x_n,$$ are there any such periodic equations?

records.name: A class of Hamiltonian systems
records.statement: Consider a Hamiltonian system with a center at the origin and Hamiltonian $$H(x,y)=H_{2n}(x,y)+H_m(x,y),\qquad m>2n,$$ where $H_{2n}$ and $H_m$ are homogeneous polynomials of degrees $2n$ and $m$. Does the period annulus of the origin have at most one critical period?

records.name: Period functions for systems with homogeneous components
records.statement: For $$\dot x=P_{2k+1}(x,y),\qquad \dot y=Q_{2\ell+1}(x,y),$$ where $P_{2k+1}$ and $Q_{2\ell+1}$ are homogeneous polynomials of the indicated odd degrees, (i) characterize all centers and (ii) determine the maximum number of oscillations of the period function among these centers.

records.name: Maximum number of critical periods
records.statement: Let $\mathcal T(n)$ be the maximum number of critical periods that a planar polynomial differential system of degree $n$ can have. Is there a constant $C>0$ such that $\mathcal T(n)\ge Cn^2\log n$?

records.name: Reversible quadratic systems
records.statement: For the family of reversible quadratic centers $$\begin{cases}\dot x=-y+xy,\\ \dot y=x+Dx^2+Fy^2,\end{cases}$$ is $2$ the maximum number of critical periods?

records.name: Reversible equivariant planar differential systems
records.statement: Is the period function associated with the period annulus of the origin for $$\dot z=iz+(z\bar z)^n z^{k+1},$$ where $n$ and $k$ are positive integers, monotonically decreasing?

records.name: Algebraic limit cycles and related questions
records.statement: Determine the entries currently marked unknown in the following comparison between quadratic systems and planar piecewise-linear systems with a straight separation line: maximum limit cycles ($4?$ versus $3?$); algebraic limit cycles ($1?$ versus $2?$); non-hyperbolic algebraic limit cycles ($0?$ versus $1?$); coexistence of algebraic and non-algebraic limit cycles (unknown for quadratic systems and impossible in the piecewise-linear case); and critical periods ($2?$ versus unknown).

records.name: A piecewise-linear Hilbert sixteenth-type problem
records.statement: Let $\mathcal H(n)$ be the maximum number of limit cycles of degree-$n$ planar polynomial systems, and let $\mathcal L(n)$ be the maximum number of crossing limit cycles of planar piecewise-linear systems whose two zones are separated by a branch of a degree-$n$ algebraic curve. Improve, if possible, the known lower bounds $$\mathcal H(2)\ge4,\ \mathcal H(3)\ge13,\ \mathcal H(n)\ge Kn^2\log n$$ and $$\mathcal L(1)\ge3,\ \mathcal L(2)\ge4,\ \mathcal L(n)\ge\lfloor n/2\rfloor.$$

records.name: A Markus–Yamabe problem for differential equations
records.statement: Are there smooth vector fields in $\mathbb{R}^3$ satisfying the hypotheses of the Markus–Yamabe conjecture and having periodic orbits?

records.name: A Markus–Yamabe/La Salle problem for discrete dynamical systems
records.statement: Let $F:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}^2$ be smooth, have a fixed point, and satisfy $$\rho\bigl(|DF(x)|\bigr)<1\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb{R}^2.$$ Is the fixed point globally asymptotically stable?

records.name: Random linear differential equations
records.statement: Let $A_0,\ldots,A_n$ be independent $N(0,1)$ random variables and let $p_n$ be the probability that the zero solution of $$A_nx^{(n)}+A_{n-1}x^{(n-1)}+\cdots+A_1x'+A_0x=0$$ is globally asymptotically stable, equivalently that every root of the characteristic polynomial has negative real part. Find the asymptotic expansion of $p_n$ as $n\to\infty$. Is $(p_n)$ strictly decreasing?

records.name: Triangular billiards
records.statement: Does every triangular billiard have a periodic trajectory?

records.name: An extended Poncelet problem I
records.statement: Do there exist two irreducible algebraic curves of degrees $n$ and $m$, with $n+m>4$, each having an oval, for which the Poncelet map is well defined and conjugate to a rotation of the circle?

records.name: An extended Poncelet problem II
records.statement: Let $\gamma=\{x^2+y^2-1=0\}$ and $\Gamma_\varepsilon=\{p_2(x,y)+\varepsilon p_m(x,y)=0\}$, where $\Gamma_0$ is an ellipse surrounding $\gamma$, the curve $p_2+\varepsilon p_m=0$ is irreducible, $\deg p_m=m\geq3$, and $\varepsilon$ is small. Is the Poncelet map for the two ovals conjugate to a rotation if and only if $\varepsilon=0$?

records.name: Loewner's conjecture
records.statement: Let $f$ be real analytic near the origin, with $f(0,0)=0$, and let $n>1$. Suppose the origin is an isolated equilibrium of $$\dot x=2^n\operatorname{Re}\!\left(\frac{\partial^n f}{\partial\bar z^n}\right),\qquad \dot y=2^n\operatorname{Im}\!\left(\frac{\partial^n f}{\partial\bar z^n}\right).$$ Prove that the index of this vector field at the origin is at most $n$.

records.name: A moments problem I
records.statement: Let $f(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in\mathbb{C}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ satisfy $$M_m:=\int_0^1\cdots\int_0^1 f(x_1,\ldots,x_n)^m\,dx_1\cdots dx_n=0\qquad(m\geq1).$$ Must $f=0$?

records.name: A moments problem II
records.statement: Let $f(x)\in\mathbb{C}[x]$ have $k$ monomials. Does there exist $N(k)$ such that if $$M_n:=\int_0^1f(x)^n\,dx=0\qquad(1\leq n\leq N(k)),$$ then $f=0$? If so, determine $N(k)$ or give a good upper bound.

records.name: Around Kouchnirenko's conjecture I
records.statement: Find a reasonable, or sharp, upper bound in terms of $m_1,m_2$ for the maximum number of simple positive-coordinate solutions of a real polynomial system $f_1(x,y)=f_2(x,y)=0$, where $m_i$ is the number of monomials of $f_i$.

records.name: Around Kouchnirenko's conjecture II
records.statement: Is $(2m_1-1)(2m_2-1)$ the maximum number of simple solutions of a real polynomial system $f_1(x,y)=f_2(x,y)=0$, where $m_i$ is the number of monomials of $f_i$?

records.name: Conjecture of multiplicative persistence
records.statement: For $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\Pi(n)$ be the product of its decimal digits, and let $\operatorname{Pm}(n)$ be the least positive integer such that $\Pi^{\operatorname{Pm}(n)}(n)=\Pi^{\operatorname{Pm}(n)+1}(n)$. Is $\operatorname{Pm}(n)\leq11$ for every $n$?

records.name: The 196 conjecture
records.statement: Define $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ by $f(n)=n+\operatorname{rev}(n)$, where $\operatorname{rev}$ reverses the decimal digits. Are there infinitely many $n$ for which no iterate $f^k(n)$, $k>0$, is a palindrome? Is the least such $n$ equal to $196$?

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 1
records.statement: Determine the structure of the multiple correlation sequences $(\mathcal{C}(n_1,\ldots,n_\ell))$ defined by (source reference E:MultCor). Is it true that any such sequence is an (approximate) integral combination of generalized $\ell$-step nilsequences in $\ell$-variables?

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 2
records.statement: Let $\mathcal C_{T,S}$ be the set of sequences $(\int f\,T^ng\,S^nh\,d\mu)_{n\ge1}$ over probability-preserving systems with commuting $T,S$ and bounded $f,g,h$, and let $\mathcal C_T$ be the subclass in which $T$ and $S$ are powers of one transformation. Show that $\mathcal{C}_{T,S}=\mathcal{C}_{T}$.

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 3
records.statement: If $(a_1(n)),\ldots, (a_\ell(n))$ are sequences of integers, then show that the following %%three statements are equivalent: • The sequences $(a_1(n)),\ldots, (a_\ell(n))$ are good for $\ell$-convergence of commuting transformations. • The sequences $(a_1(n)),\ldots, (a_\ell(n))$ are good for $\ell$-convergence of $\ell$-step nilsystems. • The sequence $\big( \frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N \psi(a_1(n),\ldots,a_\ell(n)) \big)$ converges for every basic generalized $\ell$-step nilsequence $\psi$ in $\ell$-variables.

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 4
records.statement: Let $(a(n))$ be a sequence that satisfies: • for every connected $\ell$-step nilmanifold $X$ and every irrational nilrotation $b$ in $X$ the sequence $(b^{a(n)}\Gamma)_{n \in\mathbb N}$ is equidistributed in $X$, and • the set $\{n\in\mathbb N \colon r| a(n)\}$ has positive upper density for every $r\in \mathbb N$. Show that the sequence $(a(n))$ is good for $\ell$-recurrence of commuting transformations.

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 5
records.statement: If $(a(n))$ is good for $\ell$-recurrence of powers, is then $(a(n)^k)$ good for $1$-recurrence for $k=1,\ldots, \ell$?

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 6
records.statement: If a sequence is good for $2$-convergence of powers, then show that it is good for $2$-convergence of commuting transformations.

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 7
records.statement: Is there a sequence that is good for $2$-recurrence of powers but is not good for $2$-recurrence of commuting transformations?

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 8
records.statement: Give an explicit example of a fast growing sequence that is good for multiple recurrence and convergence of powers and commuting transformations.

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 9
records.statement: Let $\mathcal P$ be an essentially distinct family of integer polynomials, and let $d_{\min}(\mathcal P)$ be the least $d$ for which the Host–Kra factor $\mathcal Z_{d,T}$ is characteristic for the associated polynomial multiple averages in every system. If $|\mathcal P|\geq 2$, show that $ d_{min}(\mathcal P)\leq |\mathcal P|-1. $

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 10
records.statement: Suppose that the sequence of $\ell$-tuples of polynomials $(p_{1,N},\ldots, p_{\ell,N})$ is good. Show that for every ergodic system $(X,\mathcal X,\mu,T)$ and functions $f_1,\ldots,f_\ell\in L^\infty(\mu)$ we have $$ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N\, T^{[p_{1,N}(n)]}f_1\cdots T^{[p_{\ell,N}(n)]}f_\ell=\int f_1\, d\mu\, \cdots \int f_\ell\, d\mu $$ where convergence takes place in $L^2(\mu)$.

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 11
records.statement: Let $(X,\mathcal X,\mu,T)$ be a system and $f, g, h\in L^\infty(\mu)$ be functions. Show that the averages $$ \frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N f(T^nx)\cdot g(T^{2n}x)\cdot h(T^{3n}x) \quad \text{and the averages} \quad \frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N f(T^nx)\cdot g(T^{n^2}x) $$ converge pointwise almost everywhere.

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 12
records.statement: Let $(X,\mathcal X,\mu,T)$ be a system and $f,g\in L^\infty(\mu)$ be functions. If $\Lambda$ is the von Mangoldt function and $\phi$ is a multiplicative function that takes values on the complex unit disc and has convergent means, then show that the averages $$ \frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N \Lambda(n)\, f(T^nx)\cdot g(T^{2n}x) \quad \text{and the averages} \quad \frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N \phi(n)\, f(T^nx)\cdot g(T^{2n}x) $$ converge pointwise almost everywhere.

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 13
records.statement: Let $(a(n))$ be the sequence of integers $(p_n)$, where $p_n$ is the $n$-th prime, or $([n^c])$ where $c>0$, or $(2^n)$. Is it true that for every ergodic system $(X,\mathcal X,\mu,T)$ and all functions $f_0,\ldots, f_\ell\in L^\infty(\mu)$, one has a decomposition $$ \int f_0 \cdot T^{a(n)} f_1 \cdot \ldots \cdot T^{\ell a(n)} f_\ell \ d\mu= \psi(a(n))+e(n), $$ where $(\psi(n))$ is an ($\ell$-step) nilsequence and $\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N|e(n)|=0$?

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 14
records.statement: Let $p_1,\ldots, p_\ell$ be integer valued generalized polynomials. Show that the averages $$ \frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} T_1^{p_1(n)}f_1\cdots T_\ell^{p_\ell(n)}f_\ell $$ converge in the mean as $N\to\infty$.

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 15
records.statement: Suppose that the polynomials $p_1,\ldots, p_\ell\in \mathbb Z[t]$ are pairwise independent. Show that there exists $d\in \mathbb N$ such that the factors $\mathcal Z_{d,T_1}, \ldots, \mathcal Z_{d,T_\ell}$ are characteristic factors for the averages (source reference E:Multies).

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 16
records.statement: Suppose that the polynomials $p_1,\ldots, p_\ell\in \mathbb Z[t]$ are rationally independent. Show that $\mathcal{K}_{rat}(T_1),\ldots, \mathcal{K}_{rat}(T_\ell)$ are characteristic factors for the averages (source reference E:Multies).

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 17
records.statement: Suppose that the polynomials $p_1,\ldots,p_\ell\in \mathbb Z[t]$ are rationally independent and have zero constant term. Show that for every $A\in \mathcal X$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $n\in \mathbb N$ such that $$ \mu(A\cap T_1^{p_1(n)}A\cap \cdots\cap T_\ell^{p_\ell(n)}A)\geq \mu(A)^{\ell+1}-\varepsilon. $$

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 18
records.statement: Let $(X,\mathcal X,\mu,T_1,\ldots, T_\ell)$ be a system and $\{p_1,\ldots, p_\ell\}$ be a family of intersective integer polynomials. Show that for every set $A\in \mathcal X$ with $\mu(A)>0$ one has $$ \mu(A\cap T_1^{p_1(n)}A\cap \cdots\cap T_\ell^{p_\ell(n)}A)>0 $$ for some $n\in\mathbb N$.

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 19
records.statement: Let $(X,\mathcal X,\mu, T,S)$ be a system and $f,g\in L^\infty(\mu)$ be functions. Show that the averages $$ \frac1N \sum_{n=1}^N f(T^nx)\cdot g(S^nx) $$ converge pointwise almost everywhere.

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 20
records.statement: Is it true that one always has a decomposition $$ \int f_0 \cdot T_1^n f_1 \cdot \ldots \cdot T_\ell^n f_\ell \ d\mu= \psi(n)+e(n) $$ where $(\psi(n))$ is an $\ell$-step nilsequence and $\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N|e(n)|=0$?

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 21
records.statement: Let $(X,\mathcal X,\mu)$ be a probability space, $T_1,\ldots, T_\ell \colon X\to X$ be invertible measure preserving transformations, and $p_1,\ldots,p_\ell$ be distinct polynomials with zero constant term. Show that for every $A\in \mathcal X$ with $\mu(A)>0$ we have $$ \mu(A\cap T_1^{m+p_1(n)}A\cap\cdots\cap T_\ell^{m+p_\ell(n)}A)>0 $$ for some $m,n\in \mathbb N$.

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 22
records.statement: Here $\mathcal F=\{a_1,\ldots,a_\ell\}$ is a family of functions of polynomial growth in one Hardy field, and $\operatorname{span}^*(\mathcal F)$ denotes its nonzero linear combinations. . Show that the family of sequences $\{([a_1(n)]),\ldots,$ $([a_\ell(n)])\}$ is good for $\ell$-convergence of a single transformation if and only if every function $a\in\text{span}^*(\mathcal{F})$ satisfies one of the following conditions: • $|a(t)-cp(t)|/ \log t\to \infty$ for every $c\in\mathbb R$ and $p\in \mathbb Z[t]$; \text{ or } • $a(t)-cp(t)\to d$ for some $c,d\in\mathbb R$; \text{ or } • $|a(t)-t/m|\leq C \log{t}$ for some non-zero $m\in\mathbb Z$ and $C>0$.

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 23
records.statement: Here $\mathcal F=\{a_1,\ldots,a_\ell\}$ is a family of functions of polynomial growth in one Hardy field, and $\operatorname{span}^*(\mathcal F)$ denotes its nonzero linear combinations.  and suppose that for every function $a\in \text{span}^*(\mathcal{F})$ we have $|a(t)-cp(t)|/ \log{t}\to\infty$ for every $c\in \mathbb R$ and $p\in \mathbb Z[t]$. Show that for every ergodic system $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$ and functions $f_1,\dots,f_\ell\in L^\infty(\mu)$ we have $$ \lim_{N\to\infty} \frac1N \sum_{n=1}^N T^{[a_1(n)]}f_1\cdots T^{ [a_\ell(n)]}f_\ell=\int f_1\, d\mu\, \cdots \, \int f_\ell\, d\mu $$ where the convergence takes place in $L^2(\mu)$.

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 24
records.statement: Let $a,b$ be distinct positive non-integers. Show that for every ergodic system $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T)$ and functions $f, g \in L^\infty(\mu)$, we have $$ \lim_{N\to\infty} \frac1N \sum_{n=1}^N f(T^{[n^a]}x) \cdot g(T^{[n^b]}x)=\int f \ d\mu \cdot \int g\ d\mu $$ for almost every $x\in X$.

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 25
records.statement: Here $\mathcal F=\{a_1,\ldots,a_\ell\}$ is a family of functions of polynomial growth in one Hardy field, and $\operatorname{span}^*(\mathcal F)$ denotes its nonzero linear combinations.  and suppose that for every function $a\in \text{span}^*(\mathcal{F})$ we have $|a(t)-cp(t)|\to \infty$ for every $c\in \mathbb R$ and $p\in \mathbb Z[t]$. Show that the collection of sequences $\{([a_1(n)]),\ldots,([a_\ell(n)])\}$ is good for $\ell$-recurrence of a single transformation.

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 26
records.statement: Find an example of a function $a\in \mathcal H$ that grows faster than polynomials, meaning, $a(t)/t^k \to\infty$ for every $k\in \mathbb N$, such that the sequence $[a(n)]$ is good for multiple recurrence and convergence of powers.

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 27
records.statement: Let $c$ be a positive non-integer. Show that the sequence $([p_n^c])$ is good for multiple recurrence and convergence of powers.

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 28
records.statement: Show that the sequence $([n \sin n])$ is good for multiple recurrence and convergence of powers.

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 29
records.statement: Show that if $c>1$ is not an integer, then the sequence $([n^c])$ is good for multiple recurrence and convergence of commuting transformations. Moreover, show that if $(X,\mathcal X,\mu, T_1,\ldots,T_\ell)$ is a system and $f_1,\ldots,f_\ell\in L^\infty(\mu)$, then the $L^2(\mu)$-limit $$ \lim_{N\to\infty} \frac1N \sum_{n=1}^N T^{[n^c]}_1f_1 \cdots T^{[n^c]}_\ell f_\ell $$ is equal to the $L^2(\mu)$-limit $\lim_{N\to\infty} \frac1N \sum_{n=1}^N T^{n}_1 f_1\cdots T^{n}_\ell f_\ell $.

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 30
records.statement: Let $\ell \in \mathbb N$ and $c,c_1,\ldots, c_\ell$ be positive real numbers. Show that the prime numbers contain patterns of the form $$ \{m,m+[n^{c}],m+2[n^{c}], \ldots, m+\ell[n^c]\} \quad \text{ and } \quad \{m,m+[n^{c_1}],\ldots,m+[n^{c_\ell}]\} $$ for infinitely many $n\in\mathbb N$.

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 31
records.statement: Suppose that $n\sigma_n\to\infty$. Show that almost surely the sequence $(a_n(\omega))$ is good for multiple recurrence and convergence of commuting transformations. Moreover, show that almost surely the following holds: For every system $(X,\mathcal X,\mu, T_1,\ldots,T_\ell)$ and functions $f_1,\ldots, f_\ell \in L^\infty(\mu)$, the averages %%$$ $$ \frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N T_1^{a_n(\omega)}f_1\cdots T_\ell^{ a_n(\omega)}f_\ell $$ converge in $L^2(\mu)$ and their limit equals the limit of the averages $\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N T_1^{n}f_1\cdots T_\ell^nf_\ell$.

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 32
records.statement: Suppose that $n\sigma_n\to\infty$. Show that almost surely the following holds: For every system $(X,\mathcal X,\mu, T,S)$ and functions $f, g \in L^\infty(\mu)$, we have $$ \lim_{N\to\infty} \frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N T^nf\cdot S^{a_n(\omega)}g= \mathbb E(f|\mathcal{I}_T)\cdot \mathbb E(g|\mathcal{I}_S) $$ where the limit is taken in $L^2(\mu)$. Furthermore, if $\sigma_n=n^{-a}$ for some $a\in (0,1)$, show that the convergence also holds pointwise almost everywhere.

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 33
records.statement: Suppose that $a,b\in(0,1)$ and $a\neq b$. Show that almost surely the following holds: For every system $(X,\mathcal X,\mu,T,S)$ and functions $f, g \in L^\infty(\mu)$ we have $$ \lim_{N\to\infty} \frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N T^{a_n(\omega)}f\cdot S^{b_n(\omega)}g= \mathbb E(f|\mathcal{I}_T)\cdot \mathbb E(g|\mathcal{I}_S) $$ where the limit is taken in $L^2(\mu)$ or pointwise.

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 34
records.statement: Let $(X,\mathcal X,\mu, T_n)$ be a measure preserving system with multiplicative structure and $A\in \mathcal X$ with $\mu(A)>0$. Is it true that there exist $m,n\in \mathbb N$, $m> n$, such that $$ \mu\bigl(T_{2mn} A\cap T_{(m-n)(m+n)} A \bigr)>0\, ? $$

records.name: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 35
records.statement: Let $(X,\mathcal X,\mu, T_n)$ be a measure preserving system with multiplicative structure and $A\in \mathcal X$ with $\mu(A)>0$. Is it true that there exist $m,n\in \mathbb N$ such that $$ \mu\bigl(T_{m(m+n)} A\cap T_{(m+2n)(m+3n)}\cap T_{(m+4n)(m+5n)} A \bigr)>0\, ? $$

records.name: Arnold and Arnold–Givental conjectures
records.statement: For a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of a closed symplectic manifold, prove the Arnold lower bound on its number of fixed points in terms of Morse-theoretic data. In the Lagrangian Arnold–Givental form, prove the corresponding lower bound for intersections of a Lagrangian submanifold with its Hamiltonian image under the standard hypotheses.

records.name: Berry–Tabor conjecture
records.statement: For a generic quantum system whose classical counterpart is integrable, prove that the unfolded high-energy level spacings have Poisson statistics.

records.name: Banach's simple Lebesgue spectrum problem
records.statement: Does there exist an ergodic measure-preserving transformation whose Koopman operator has simple Lebesgue spectrum?

records.name: Eden's conjecture on local Lyapunov dimension
records.statement: For a smooth dissipative dynamical system with a global attractor, is the supremum of the local Lyapunov dimension on the attractor attained at an equilibrium or at an unstable periodic orbit contained in the attractor?

records.name: Kaplan–Yorke dimension conjecture
records.statement: Under the hypotheses in which the Lyapunov (Kaplan–Yorke) dimension is defined from the ordered Lyapunov exponents, prove that it equals the appropriate dimension of the attractor or invariant measure.

records.name: Margulis measure-classification conjecture
records.statement: Classify invariant ergodic probability measures for higher-rank diagonalizable group actions on homogeneous spaces; in particular, prove that the measures satisfying the usual nondegeneracy hypotheses are algebraic (homogeneous).

records.name: Unbounded outer-billiard orbits for almost every polygon
records.statement: Prove that the outer billiard about almost every convex polygon has an unbounded orbit.

records.name: Quantum unique ergodicity
records.statement: Let $M$ be a compact negatively curved Riemannian manifold. Do the probability measures $|\varphi_j|^2\,d\operatorname{vol}$ associated with every orthonormal sequence of Laplace eigenfunctions equidistribute to normalized volume as the eigenvalues tend to infinity?

records.name: Rokhlin multiple-mixing problem
records.statement: Is every strongly mixing measure-preserving transformation strongly mixing of order three?

records.name: Termination of juggler sequences
records.statement: Starting from a positive integer $a_0$, define $a_{n+1}=\lfloor a_n^{1/2}\rfloor$ when $a_n$ is even and $a_{n+1}=\lfloor a_n^{3/2}\rfloor$ when $a_n$ is odd. Does every such juggler sequence eventually reach $1$?

records.name: Completeness of Lyapunov's second method
records.statement: For which classes of ordinary differential equations do the classical and canonically generalized forms of Lyapunov's second method give necessary as well as sufficient conditions for stability or asymptotic stability of motion?

records.name: Local reversibility of reversible cellular automata
records.statement: In every dimension at least three, is each reversible cellular automaton locally reversible?

records.name: Closed-versus-preclosed trajectory lengths
records.statement: In a regular $n$-gon, call a trajectory preclosed when its endpoints divide their boundary edges into equal-length parts and meet those oriented edges at equal angles. Closed and preclosed trajectories are strongly parallel when they have the same sequence of reflection edges. After canceling all common factors from the ratios of lengths of a family of parallel closed trajectories, prove that the remaining integer factors relating closed-trajectory lengths to the corresponding preclosed-trajectory lengths are never equal to $n$.

records.name: Types of vertices of reachable polygons
records.statement: Unfold a billiard trajectory in a regular $n$-gon by reflecting the polygon across each encountered side. A short trajectory joins two vertices and meets no vertex in between; a reachable point is an endpoint vertex occurring in such an unfolding. For an oriented short trajectory, let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be its source and target endpoint angles as in Definition 2.1 of the source, and write $A_k$ for the resulting one of $n-2$ trajectory types (indices modulo $n-2$); in particular $A_0$ is characterized by $\beta-\alpha=2\pi/n$. Call an $n$-gon reachable if it is an $SL(2,\mathbb R)$ image of the original regular $n$-gon and all its vertices except the distinguished vertex $O$ are reachable points. If $n\ge5$ and its clockwise vertices are $v_0=O,v_1,\ldots,v_{n-1}$, prove that $v_1,\ldots,v_{n-1}$ have types $A_0,A_1,\ldots,A_{n-3},A_0$, respectively.

records.name: Reachable points lie on reachable polygons
records.statement: Unfold a billiard trajectory in a regular $n$-gon by reflecting the polygon across each encountered side. A short trajectory joins two vertices and meets no vertex in between; a reachable point is an endpoint vertex occurring in such an unfolding. For an oriented short trajectory, let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be its source and target endpoint angles as in Definition 2.1 of the source, and write $A_k$ for the resulting one of $n-2$ trajectory types (indices modulo $n-2$); in particular $A_0$ is characterized by $\beta-\alpha=2\pi/n$. Prove that every reachable point is a vertex of infinitely many reachable $n$-gons.

records.name: Reachable points on lines through a unitary pair
records.statement: Unfold a billiard trajectory in a regular $n$-gon by reflecting the polygon across each encountered side. A short trajectory joins two vertices and meets no vertex in between; a reachable point is an endpoint vertex occurring in such an unfolding. For an oriented short trajectory, let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be its source and target endpoint angles as in Definition 2.1 of the source, and write $A_k$ for the resulting one of $n-2$ trajectory types (indices modulo $n-2$); in particular $A_0$ is characterized by $\beta-\alpha=2\pi/n$. For $n\ge5$, call reachable points $u,v$ of type $A_0$ a unitary pair if $\det(u,v)=\sin((n-2)\pi/n)$, and put $\lambda=2\cos(\pi/n)$. Prove: (a) $u_m=u+m(\lambda+1)v$ is reachable of type $A_0$ for every integer $m$ for which it lies in the upper half-plane; (b) $w_m=u+(\lambda+m(\lambda+1))v$ is reachable of type $A_1$ whenever it lies there; (c) there are no other reachable points on $u+\mathbb Rv$; and (d) the analogous description on $v+\mathbb Ru$ yields only types $A_0$ and $A_{n-3}$.

records.name: Types of parallel short trajectories
records.statement: Unfold a billiard trajectory in a regular $n$-gon by reflecting the polygon across each encountered side. A short trajectory joins two vertices and meets no vertex in between; a reachable point is an endpoint vertex occurring in such an unfolding. For an oriented short trajectory, let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be its source and target endpoint angles as in Definition 2.1 of the source, and write $A_k$ for the resulting one of $n-2$ trajectory types (indices modulo $n-2$); in particular $A_0$ is characterized by $\beta-\alpha=2\pi/n$. If a short trajectory emanating from $O$ with slope angle $\alpha$ has type $A_k$, prove that the parallel short trajectory from $O$ with slope angle $\ell\pi/n+\varepsilon\alpha$, where $\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}$, has type $A_{\varepsilon k-\ell}$. When $n$ is even, restrict $\ell$ to even integers.

records.name: Length ratios of parallel short trajectories
